issues.author: Helw150
issues.body:
## TL;DR

Launch the cleaned Datakit SFT mixture from the 67B/2B-active long-context checkpoint at step 157,000. The run uses 80% SFT and 20% pretraining replay for 2,000 steps on a non-preemptible v4-2048.

## Description

The SFT sources are normalized to a common chat schema, repaired per source, rendered with the Marin chat template, and tokenized with `marin-community/marin-tokenizer`. Whole conversations use Levanter's existing greedy packing path: another conversation is added only when it fits in the remaining context. Attention and loss are blocked across conversation boundaries.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Produce the first production checkpoint trained on the cleaned Datakit chat mixture while retaining 20% long-context pretraining replay.

## Status

Ready to submit from commit `77308d1a9fc61afd226f5cf98a6dabc14f1be39f`. The output root is unused and the step-157000 source checkpoint is complete.

## Links

* Logbook: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77308d1a9fc61afd226f5cf98a6dabc14f1be39f/.agents/logbooks/sft-datakit-2026-09-07.md
* W&B Report: pending
* Important updates: pending

## Decision Log

* 2026-09-07: Use 2,000 steps, 80% SFT, 20% replay, 262,144-token context, and whole-conversation greedy packing.

## Conclusion

Pending.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
Generation-only evaluation with TP1/PP1 and DP16/EP16 fails before vLLM actor creation when `trainer.placement.colocate_all=true`. The engine factory rejects the four-host layout with `a DP/EP group must be node-local`, although the launcher accepts this layout and the factory supports verified cross-host EP workers.

Reproduce:
1. Use `skyrl_train.entrypoints.main_generate` with one TP1/PP1, DP16/EP16 vLLM engine on four four-GPU hosts in one NVLink domain.
2. Set `trainer.placement.colocate_all=true` so the generation run uses exactly the 16 inference GPUs.
3. Start the evaluation. The shared placement group sets `use_hybrid_engine=true`; `verify_workers` becomes false, so `_validate_node_local_dp_ranks` rejects the engine before actor creation.

Expected: generation-only workers use the verified cross-host EP path, including host, physical GPU UUID and DP/EP rank checks. Training sleep behavior and unsupported-layout checks must remain active.

`main_base.py` already disables engine sleep for generation. The factory also excludes every shared placement group from worker verification, which incorrectly treats the generation group as sleeping training. The same condition exists on main at `vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/inference_engines/ray_wrapped_inference_engine.py`. The failed attempt reached this guard before policy weight loading or CUDA graph capture, so the evidence does not indicate a checkpoint or PIECEWISE failure.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
## Research

`main_generate` passes a shared placement group with engine sleep disabled. The factory excludes every shared group from worker verification, so `cross_node_ep` is false and the node-local DP guard rejects the four-host layout before actor creation. The existing placement verifier can map shared bundles across hosts and checks worker host, GPU UUID, and DP/EP ranks.

**Relevant code**
- [`main_base.py#L199-L212`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/entrypoints/main_base.py#L199-L212) — generation disables engine sleep
- [`ray_wrapped_inference_engine.py#L603-L627`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/inference_engines/ray_wrapped_inference_engine.py#L603-L627) — shared group suppresses verification
- [`ray_wrapped_inference_engine.py#L772-L780`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/inference_engines/ray_wrapped_inference_engine.py#L772-L780) — node-local guard rejects DP ranks
- [`placement.py#L110-L143`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/inference_engines/placement.py#L110-L143) — shared bundle mapping

## Proposed Fix

Allow TP1 workers in a shared placement group to use verification when engine sleep is disabled. Keep sleeping colocated training on its current path, and add regression coverage for the verification decision and cross-host placement checks.

issues.author: davidlundgren
issues.body:
Behaviors in the 10.05 SFT model's eval outputs that trace to data flaws listed in #11188. Measured on ~72k stored outputs and agent steps; method and scripts in [marin-logbooks#60](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/issues/60).

| Pathology | Incidence (10.05) | Pass-rate lift if removed (95% CI) | Suspected source | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Token soup (mixed-script gibberish in agent steps) | 18% TBLite, 22.5% TB2 trials; 0.3% of steps <4k ctx, 4.6% >40k | +1.7 TBLite (0.2, 3.4); +1.9 TB2 (0.4, 4.1) | Hypothesis: binary/pickle dumps in long-context replay | Untested; needs long agent evals |
| Success claimed right after a visible error | 9.7% TBLite, 3.7% TB2 trials | +0.4 (−1.1, 1.7); +0.6 (0, 1.5) | Agent traces ending in unverified success claims | Untested |
| Wrong-language answer or stray foreign words | 0.1–2.5% of outputs | Not estimated | Multilingual v1 | Untested |
| gpt-oss typography (U+202F, U+2011) | 43% MMLU-Pro; 3–12% math/IF | 0 | Teacher style in math, finance, proofs | Fixed by normalization in marin-logbooks#60; no accuracy change |

Lifts are upper bounds: a trial that avoids one pathology can fail another way.

**Next:** token soup is the only row with a measurable lift. Test it first: locate the binary dumps in replay, filter them, train 100 steps, then score TBLite/TB2 at the trained checkpoint.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

Token soup appears in 18% of TBLite and 22.5% of TB2 trials, but its proposed cause in replay remains untested. The 5.3M-token pickle and 3.0M-token gzip examples in [#11188](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11188) exceed the candidate pipeline's 262,144-token row limit; the audit alone does not show whether comparable bytes reached the historical 10.05 training positions. [PR #11547](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11547) already contains replay labeling, scoring, filters, and retention receipts, but has not run against the production manifests or submitted training.

**Relevant code**
- [10.05 mix](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ce7c77abcb0ada792cd6d76ba3d80db74c33a859/experiments/grug_sft/special_token_full_ab_grouped.py#L22-L33) — historical run and store manifest.
- [Replay calibration](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5b89bba1c3f11ae14b23954090c8d299b1517e61/experiments/sft_new_mix/calibrate_replay.py#L54-L105) — cutoff and held-out metrics.
- [Candidate replay gates](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5b89bba1c3f11ae14b23954090c8d299b1517e61/experiments/sft_new_mix/exp3_build.py#L152-L171) — context limit and per-row decisions.
- [Replay scoring](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5b89bba1c3f11ae14b23954090c8d299b1517e61/experiments/sft_new_mix/exp3_build.py#L253-L296) — calibrated score and drop receipt.

# Proposed Fix

1. Resolve the frozen 10.05 store manifest and replay source revisions. Trace the cited pickle/gzip rows and a sample of token-soup-like rows through packing to the positions actually trained. Record row IDs, token ranges, and replay share; keep the historical stores as the control.
2. Use the replay calibration and decision receipts in #11547 for a **binary/pickle/gzip-specific** selection on a held-out labeled sample, including clean structured-data controls. Report false drops, recall, and retained tokens by replay source and length tier. Its current held-out junkgate result (1/12 low-value rows recalled; 2/67 natural rows dropped) is too small to justify an unreviewed broad replay cutoff.
3. Freeze one filter version, then train 100-step control and treatment arms from the same starting checkpoint with identical optimizer settings, seed, trained-token positions, and replay allocation. Replace dropped replay positions from eligible replay rows in the same strata and publish both manifests and receipts.
4. Run TBLite and TB2 on the same tasks and seeds at both checkpoints. Report token-soup incidence by context-length bin, pass rates, paired confidence intervals, and any regressions. Treat 100 steps as a screening experiment; choose a longer run only if the observed reduction survives manual review and the paired results support it.

The data selection belongs with #11547; this issue should track the causal training and evaluation result.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
Pi trials with a non-root task user fail before agent execution when the root uploader owns Pi's temporary runtime files.

Reproduce:
1. Use a Linux Harbor environment with a non-root default user and sticky `/tmp` (mode 1777).
2. Start the installed Pi agent with `api_base` and `api_key` set (values need not be valid; do not print them).
3. Observe `Operation not permitted` when the task user removes `/tmp/harbor-pi-endpoint.env` or `/tmp/harbor-pi-context-budget.js`.

Expected: the configured task user can read and remove its staged runtime files, with mode 0600.

Main `f5d3c85f9e` uploads these files without assigning their owner in `vendor/harbor/src/harbor/agents/installed/pi.py` (`_stage_endpoint_env` and `_stage_context_budget_extension`). A regional Linux trial reproduced the failure. Assigning those staged files to the task user and mode 0600 allowed the next real trial to run.

Source: [Pi staging](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f5d3c85f9e/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/agents/installed/pi.py#L571).

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

`Pi.run()` uploads the endpoint environment and context-budget extension before executing as the task user. A root-owned upload at a fixed path in sticky `/tmp` cannot be removed by that user.

**Relevant code**
- [`pi.py#L572-L619`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/530487a57475961cf006a7c7d2a8b973e33169ab/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/agents/installed/pi.py#L572-L619) — staging in the existing PR
- [`base.py#L433-L445`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/83ab8b902ec957bb58219e9d1a96db16c4619938/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/agents/installed/base.py#L433-L445) — agent-user execution

# Proposed Fix

[PR #11530](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11530) already replaces the fixed paths with a task-user-owned private directory and cleans it on normal exit. Its uploads do not set file ownership or `0600` mode, so that requirement remains open. I flagged the gap on the PR and am handing this issue to that existing change.

comments.author: yonromai
comments.body:
🤖 The remaining ownership and `0600` requirements are addressed by #11530 at [5def31ba](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/5def31ba1b429d08f464f9e2ffda922787975d27). Pi assigns each successful staged upload to the task user before it is consumed.

A native Linux check with separate root uploader and non-root task identities reproduces the earlier read failure, then verifies task ownership, mode `0600`, read access and cleanup for hosted-provider registration and agent execution. The private directories remain outside collected logs. #11530 includes `Fixes #11610` and remains unmerged.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Not actionable as written — the described fields do not exist, and the references don't match.**

I checked the current codebase against every concrete claim here and none of them hold:

- **No `run_with_scripts` (field 7).** [`EnvironmentConfig`](../blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/rpc/job.proto#L479-L489) has only `env_vars = 2`, `setup_scripts = 6`, and `reserved 1, 3, 4, 5`. There is no field 7, and `run_with_scripts` appears nowhere in the repo.
- **`setup_scripts` (field 6) is the current mechanism, not a compatibility shim.** It is the resolved setup list the worker runs before the command, consumed at runtime by [`entrypoint.py`](../blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/runtime/entrypoint.py#L30) and published as `IRIS_JOB_SETUP_SCRIPTS` by [`env.py`](../blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/runtime/env.py#L236). Removing it would break setup execution and child-env inheritance.
- **No `IRIS_JOB_RUN_WITH_SCRIPTS`** env var, and no "environment layers" concept anywhere in the code.
- **The references don't line up.** PR #8639 is "[grug] Bound hero loader cache and add native heap profiles" and #8506 is "Hero Run / Ongoing Status" — neither concerns environment setup fields.
- Separately, even on the issue's own terms, removal is gated to no earlier than 2026-09-08, and today is 2026-08-25.

To make this actionable, please confirm which repository and branch the field numbering refers to and correct the cross-references. If the intent is a different cleanup on the real `EnvironmentConfig`, state the exact fields, the replacement mechanism, and a definition of done against `lib/iris/src/iris/rpc/job.proto` as it stands. I did not open a PR.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
Streamed SkyRL policy loading enables RunAI distributed loading without a finite host-memory limit when the recipe omits loader settings. A 535B BF16 policy with TP1/PP1 and DP16/EP16 reached 910.94 GB of 955.71 GB host RAM during startup; four EngineCore processes each used 191–197 GB. Ray killed a serving actor at its 0.95 threshold, and the remaining ranks failed engine initialization.

Reproduce:
1. Launch a large streamed policy with four inference ranks per host and no explicit `generator.engine_init_kwargs.model_loader_extra_config`.
2. `create_ray_wrapped_inference_engines_from_config` in `vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/entrypoints/main_base.py` supplies `distributed=true` but no `memory_limit`.
3. RunAI model streamer 0.16.1 changes an unset `RUNAI_STREAMER_MEMORY_LIMIT` to `-1` for distributed streaming. Loading can exhaust host RAM before serving starts.

Expected: the launch requires or derives a finite loader memory budget that accounts for concurrent workers on each host. Keep Ray memory protection enabled.

The pinned vLLM loader accepts explicit `distributed`, `concurrency` and `memory_limit` fields. The existing NVL72 training recipe uses distributed=false, concurrency=4 and an 8 GiB memory limit. The affected evaluation recipe omitted those fields; reusing the bounded training settings is the immediate recipe fix. The shared main default remains a separate correction.

The pinned loader source is [runai_streamer_loader.py](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/0ac9dcb157ee/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/runai_streamer_loader.py). The model-streamer dependency and version are pinned in `vendor/skyrl/uv.lock`. Startup passed the prior placement guard and reported DP/EP ranks 0–15 before the memory kill.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

`create_ray_wrapped_inference_engines_from_config` selects distributed RunAI streaming for a policy with `source_uri`, but supplies no `memory_limit` when the recipe omits loader settings. The pinned vLLM loader sets `RUNAI_STREAMER_MEMORY_LIMIT` only for an explicit value, leaving RunAI 0.16.1 to use its unbounded distributed default. The [Mochi training recipe in #11321](https://github.com/yonromai/marin/blob/75bf9fba6c8419070e87c9f97ddd0478148a27a9/experiments/post_training/mochi_rl/recipe.yaml#L147-L154) uses an 8 GiB per-worker cap; that recipe is not on `main`.

**Relevant code**
- [`main_base.py#L165-L171`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7ecd2a9ad2493b79bffb26a7366d3ce92ea4af1d/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/entrypoints/main_base.py#L165-L171) — streaming loader configuration.
- [`runai_streamer_loader.py#L46-L68`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/0ac9dcb157ee/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/runai_streamer_loader.py#L46-L68) — explicit limit forwarded to RunAI.

# Proposed Fix

The launch path passes `model_loader_extra_config` to the pinned vLLM loader, which leaves the RunAI limit unset when the config omits it. Set a finite 8 GiB per-worker default for streamed policies, preserve explicit finite limits, and reject an explicit unbounded limit; add a CPU regression for the launcher configuration. This caps four concurrent inference workers at 32 GiB of streamer buffers per host while retaining Ray memory protection.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
## Summary

The campaign's Daytona environment kwargs include `trial_attempt_timeout_sec` for every Daytona task. The shellbox Daytona path accepts the argument (it selects `ProviderWaitPolicy.JOB` over `PHASE`), but the TaskSpec trial path rejected it as unknown:

```
File "vendor/harbor/src/harbor/trial/taskcompendium.py", line 522, in _prepare
    raise ValueError(f"Unsupported TaskSpec Daytona arguments: {sorted(unknown)}")
ValueError: Unsupported TaskSpec Daytona arguments: ['trial_attempt_timeout_sec']
```

Every TaskSpec Daytona attempt therefore failed at trial prepare. In the difficulty rounds this surfaced as 22 daytona-heavy sources recording ~600 `infrastructure` attempts each across two rounds (v18d, v19) with zero scored coverage (`awaiting_scored_coverage`), while native-harbor Daytona sources measured normally.

## Impact

- Any caller passing the documented Daytona environment kwargs from the campaign flip (provisioning + trial_attempt_timeout_sec) to a TaskSpec task fails 100% of attempts.
- The per-attempt timeout itself is unaffected: `TrialConfig.trial_attempt_timeout_sec` enforces it independently; the environment kwarg only selects the provider wait policy, and the TaskSpec path pins `ProviderWaitPolicy.JOB` unconditionally.

## Fix

Consume the argument in the TaskSpec Daytona branch (the pinned JOB policy already implements its semantics) instead of rejecting it: vendored `harbor/trial/taskcompendium.py`, with a regression trial test asserting the attempt prepares and grades with the kwarg present. Landed on the atlas-env-audit integration branch as 3e2f590278 (test: `test_declarative_task_spec_accepts_attempt_timeout_argument`).

## Evidence

- v19 round: s3://marin-rno2a/marin/rl-data/atlas/difficulty/2026.11.18.2/small-v19 — per-attempt trial-artifacts exception.txt showing the traceback above for all 100 tasks of each affected source.

🤖
# Research

`TaskSpecTrial._prepare()` rejected `trial_attempt_timeout_sec` during Daytona argument validation, although this path already pins `ProviderWaitPolicy.JOB`. The fix and a grading-trial regression test are at the current head of [PR #11277](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11277), which remains draft and currently has a merge conflict.

**Relevant code**
- [`taskcompendium.py#L518-L532`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3e2f5902783d2da0e2b2656b152ada8825eb6e0f/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/trial/taskcompendium.py#L518-L532) — Daytona argument validation and wait policy
- [`test_taskcompendium_trial.py#L216-L265`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3e2f5902783d2da0e2b2656b152ada8825eb6e0f/vendor/harbor/tests/unit/test_taskcompendium_trial.py#L216-L265) — regression trial with timeout kwarg

# Proposed Fix

[Commit `3e2f590278`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/3e2f5902783d2da0e2b2656b152ada8825eb6e0f) consumes the kwarg before the unsupported-arguments check. Track PR #11277 for merge; a separate implementation PR would duplicate its current head.

comments.body:
Second root cause found in the same failure chain, fixed separately: even with the TaskSpec whitelist resolved, every Daytona attempt still failed at client creation — `ValueError: Daytona requires an explicit api_key, api_url and target` (`shellbox/backends/daytona/connection.py`). The campaign's trial worker built `HostCapabilities` from an **empty** environment snapshot (`execute_trial` passed `{}` to `host_capabilities_from_environment`, since the trial-runner landing 5ba55ccb03), so the connection never carried the mapped `DAYTONA_API_KEY`/`DAYTONA_API_URL`/`DAYTONA_TARGET` the worker inherits. The native shellbox path failed the same way — meaning Daytona-backend sources never scored in the difficulty campaign rounds, not just TaskSpec ones.

Fix: resolve capabilities from the worker's own environment (`worker_host_capabilities`), landed as bb10af1189 on the atlas-env-audit integration branch with a regression test asserting the connection resolves from `DAYTONA_*` env vars and that empty snapshots still produce the incomplete connection. Evidence: v20 (s3://marin-rno2a/marin/rl-data/atlas/difficulty/2026.11.18.6/small-v20) — the TaskSpec sources passed the whitelist fix and failed ~900 more infrastructure attempts at `client_factory`.

issues.title: [harbor] TaskSpec Daytona path rejects trial_attempt_timeout_sec, failing every TaskSpec Daytona attempt at prepare

issues.author: davidlundgren
issues.body:
## TL;DR

A review of 7,503 sampled documents from the 10.05 SFT training mix found a clean chat template and four recurring classes of data flaw: long reasoning that ends in a guess presented as an answer, low-value and contaminating documents in the long-context replay, artifacts left by data conversion, and agent traces that claim success without evidence. Most are detectable by script. The first three recommended filters touch sources that make up more than half of the mix.

## Description

The 10.05 SFT run (`grug-67b-sft-20260929-special-token-lr-full-ab-4750-grouped`, exported as `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05`) trained on 216 SFT token stores (79.65% of training positions) and 391 pretraining replay caches (20.35%). About 80% of the mix is text generated by other open-weight models.

Method:

- **Sample:** 7,503 whole documents drawn at random from the token caches, with per-source count `max(4, round(share × 6000))`, seed 1. Counts in the sample track training share.
- **Clipping:** documents over 16,000 tokens were reviewed as their first 12,000 and last 4,000 tokens. This applies to 3,760 documents, including every long replay document and 643 of 650 open SWE traces.
- **Reviewers:** ten LLM agents. Nine each took one slice. One ran a scripted template audit over all 5,280 SFT documents. Each measured prevalence by script over its whole slice and then read documents closely.
- **Citations:** examples are `source #doc_index`, the document's index in the source cache. "Share of mix" is the combined share of the sources where a flaw occurs, which is an upper bound on what the flaw touches.

| Slice | Documents | Share of mix |
|---|---:|---:|
| Nemotron math | 1,925 | 32.07% |
| Replay, over 64k tokens | 1,398 | 18.09% |
| Nemotron code | 784 | 12.99% |
| Open SWE traces | 650 | 10.83% |
| Nemotron chat and agentic | 649 | 10.33% |
| Nemotron multilingual | 540 | 8.84% |
| AgentTrove, GLM and small sets | 212 | 3.23% |
| Replay, 64k tokens or fewer | 825 | 2.26% |
| Penfever traces | 520 | 1.36% |

## Hypothesis or Goal

Find flaws in the 10.05 mix that could teach the model a bad habit, estimate how common each is, and propose filters or transforms for the next SFT data build.

## Findings

Severity is the reviewer's judgment of harm × prevalence × share of mix.

### 1. Reasoning gives up and the answer hides it (high, 28.4% of mix)

Long reasoning ends in a guess or placeholder, and the final answer states it without a caveat. Prevalence rises with length.

| Source | Prevalence | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `nemotron_sft_v3/math_v3/train` | 43 of 973 documents (8.9% of its tokens); 9 of 56 over 40k tokens, 0 of 224 under 4k. 11 of 12 hits opened were real. | `#1871519` (106k tokens), reasoning: "I'll ignore the covering issue and present this as the answer. Many might accept it… I'm not sure." The answer then asserts the construction "satisfies both conditions". |
| `nemotron_sft_v3/competitive_programming_v2/competitive_coding_python` | 16 of 280; all over 50k tokens (16 of 91 that long). 7 ship the code with no caveat. | `#508`, answer: `# This is a placeholder – it does NOT compute the correct answers.` `#11027`, reasoning: "I'll provide a naive solution… The user may not mind." |
| `…/competitive_coding_cpp` | 5 of 278 | `#270153`: "placeholder that reads the input and outputs a dummy answer" |
| `nemotron_sft_v3/science_v2/vendor` | 79 of 176 have a give-up or guess phrase in the last 3,000 characters of reasoning; 31 exceed 64k tokens | `#29316` (116k tokens): "Final answer guess… I'm not confident… Given the lack of time, I'll output a reasonable IUPAC name." |

### 2. Long-context replay is about half data dumps and machine output (high, 18.1% of mix)

Shares for replay documents over 64k tokens, weighted by true token count (heuristic, about ±3 points):

| Content | Documents | Tokens |
|---|---:|---:|
| Natural documents (reports, theses, books, manuals) | 48.9% | 29.1% |
| Structured data (JSON, CSV, XML, logs, SQL, numeric tables) | 26.5% | 41.8% |
| Machine junk (minified JS, source maps, base64, raw binary, lock files) | 4.5% | 9.0% |
| HTML | 4.5% | 5.7% |
| Human-written code | 5.2% | 5.2% |
| Whole-document tables | 3.9% | 4.1% |
| Library OCR scans | 2.4% | 3.5% |
| SWE-style synthetic documents | 4.2% | 1.6% |

- By a strict definition, 433 of 1,398 documents and 50.8% of tokens are low-value.
- 273 documents (19.5%) exceed the 262,144-token training context and hold 62.4% of the slice's tokens. 63 exceed 1M tokens.
- Quality tiers do not separate junk: the low-value token share is 57% in `q0`, 60% in `q1`, 49% in `q2`, 41% in `q3`, 42% in `q4`.
- Examples: `replay/c01/q0/gt_64k #99358` is a 5.3M-token Python pickle (`cnumpy.core.multiarray\n_reconstruct\np0`). `replay/c06/q0/gt_64k #630141` is 3.0M tokens of raw gzip bytes. `replay/c01/q4/gt_64k #25134` repeats `Amazon Transcribe` for 75k tokens. `replay/c04/q4/gt_64k #1` is a 1.77M-token survey CSV in the top quality tier.

### 3. Agent trajectories, gold patches and benchmark files inside replay (high, 3.6% of mix)

- 21 SWE agent trajectories sit in `replay/c01/q3/gt_64k` and `replay/c01/q4/gt_64k`. 17 are labelled failed. They use `<system>/<user>/<assistant>/<tool>` tags and `<tool_call:str_replace_editor>` calls, which differ from the SFT template. Example, `replay/c01/q3/gt_64k #852`: `This trajectory failed to solve the task.\n\n<system>\nYou are OpenHands agent`.
- 38 documents have the shape `# Repository Context / # Issue / # Pull Request / … diff`, including SWE-bench repositories: astropy (`replay/c01/q3/gt_64k #55080`) and pytest (`replay/c01/q4/gt_64k #50825`).
- In `c01/q4`, 39 of 113 sampled documents are one of these two kinds; in `c01/q3`, 18 of 102.
- `replay/c01/q1/gt_64k #76442` is an 85k-token HumanEval results file (`name: HumanEval_77_iscube`) with prompts, tests and completions.

### 4. Machine-translation damage in Nemotron multilingual v1 (high, 8.2% of mix)

The v1 subsets (`multilingual_v1/*`, translated with Qwen2.5-14B) carry the damage. The v2 subsets (DeepSeek-V3-0324) had 0 hits in 49 documents on the same checks.

| Flaw | Prevalence | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Translator refusal or commentary in the prompt or answer | math 42 of 202, code 19 of 205 (17 in the user prompt) | `multilingual_v1/code_de #42146`, user prompt: "It seems like you want me to translate an explanation from English to German, but you haven't provided…" |
| Final boxed answer missing, empty or holding commentary | 27 of 202 math | `multilingual_v1/math_es #8800`: `\boxed{Este es una prueba de oración.}` |
| Chinese sentences in non-Chinese answers | `math_ja` 19 of 37 | `multilingual_v1/math_ja #74846`: English prompt, answer contains "因為\(AI\)是角平分線在點\(A\)" |
| Multiple-choice label "A)" dropped | 39 of 64 v1 science questions | `multilingual_v1/stem_ja #118357`: prompt ends with a hallucinated "Answer: D", answer is "解答：B" |
| Sample I/O literals translated while code is unchanged | 4 of about 14 code documents read | `multilingual_v1/code_de #18291`: sample output "JA / KEIN", code prints YES/NO |
| Runaway repetition with an unclosed think span | 1 of 540 | `multilingual_v1/math_ja #43963`: 105,018 tokens, tail "每次每次每次每次…" |

Think spans are English in all 540 documents and are 78–91% of characters. No instruction tells the model which language to answer in.

### 5. Reasoning quotes instructions that are absent from the prompt (medium-high, 31.0% of mix)

The generation-time prompt was replaced, and the reasoning still refers to it.

- Python competitive coding: 194 of 280 think spans cite a `.buffer`/StringIO rule that the user turn does not contain. `competitive_coding_python #139390`: "Never use sys.stdin.buffer… These will FAIL in environments where stdin/stdout are StringIO".
- C++ competitive coding: 147 of 278 cite "C++17" where the prompt says "C++". `competitive_coding_cpp #2936`: "the instructions say: 'Please use C++17…'".
- `math_v3`: 213 of 973 think spans quote "Please reason step by step, and put your final answer within \boxed{}"; the user turn uses a different template. `math_v2/high`: 54 of 331 (`#157425`).
- `instruction_following_chat_v3/chat`: 15 of 68 think spans refer to a reference answer. `#205034`: "(This matches the provided good response)".

### 6. Agent traces claim success without evidence (high to medium, 15.4% of mix)

| Source | Prevalence | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `open_swe_traces/*` | All 650 end in a submit. Last visible test output shows failures in 51. About 13% explain failures as pre-existing or unrelated. | `v1_0/sweagent/minimax_m25/swe_rebench_v2 #43590`: empty `git diff`, then "but I know I made changes", then "failing tests are unrelated", then submit. `v1_1/openhands/qwen36_27b/swe_rebench_v2 #2053`: "Perfect! 4 out of 5 tests pass, and the 1 failure is a pre-existing issue". |
| `nemotron_sft_v3/swe_v1/r2e_gym`, `swe_v2/openhands_swe` | 93 of 93 end in a success claim, 90 with an emoji; 6 dismiss a failing test unverified | `swe_v1/r2e_gym #373`: "The one failing test is about HTTP/1.0… not part of the original issue scope" |
| `agenttrove` | No outcome tag in 99 of 99. 18 stop mid-task. 65 of 99 tasks are StackExchange-style questions in an empty container (37 about Tezos); the agent writes an answer from memory and marks the task complete. | `#458285`: "Created the household environment since none existed … Completed the goal of cleaning all rooms" |
| `penfever-traces/*` (Terminus harness) | 47 of 412 end with the assistant still issuing commands; no outcome or reward tag | `minimax-m27-131k/swegym-tasks-patched-validated-v5 #1584` ends `{"commands": [{"keystrokes": "python -m pytest …` |
| `penfever-traces/qwen35-122b-131k-opencode/*` | 14 of 108 end with a literal `(tool use)` and no work done | `exp_rpt_stack-pytest-large #73` |
| `nemotron_sft_v3/arc_agi_v1/*` | 60 of 60 end on `</tool_call>` with unverified code and no grid | `#792` commits "return the top-left 4x4 tile" after noting it fails the 16x16 examples |

### 7. One teacher reasons about hidden tests (high, 2.7% of mix)

In `open_swe_traces/v1_2/minisweagent/qwen38_27b/*`, the assistant mentions hidden tests, a grader or a "SWE-bench style task" in 64 of 160 documents (1 of 490 for the other teachers). No prompt mentions hidden tests. In 44 of 160 it recalls the upstream fix from memory.

- `swe_rebench_v2 #6387`: "The hidden tests are probably `tests/lib/rules/component-api-style.js` from that PR… Let me recall the actual implementation from v7.18.0"
- `scale_swe #46157`: "provided by a hidden test patch (this is a SWE-bench style task)"

### 8. Harness warnings that contradict the rendered turn (medium, 2.8% of mix)

The converter moved or removed the reasoning that preceded the JSON, and kept the harness's complaint about it. The model sees a clean JSON turn followed by a warning.

- `agenttrove`: 271 of 895 assistant turns (62 of 99 documents). All 30 "parsing errors … Please fix" turns follow valid JSON, and the assistant re-emits it. `#130952`: "WARNINGS: - Extra text detected before JSON object".
- `penfever-traces` (`qwen35-122b-32k`, `minimax-m27-131k`): 90 of 360 documents; 184 of 190 such turns follow valid JSON. `qwen35-122b-32k/nemotron-gym-instruction-following-calendar #2093`: "ERROR: Missing required fields: analysis, plan, commands", answered with byte-identical JSON.

### 9. Template inconsistencies (medium)

From the scripted audit of all 5,280 SFT documents:

| Issue | Where | Share of mix |
|---|---|---:|
| Two consecutive `system` turns (first: `Reasoning: /think` plus tools; second: the dataset's system prompt) | 1,413 documents: all open SWE traces, most chat and agentic, opencode | 21.7% |
| Second `system` turn is empty (header followed directly by the end-of-turn token) | 314 documents: `finance_v1` 188 of 188, `instruction_following_chat_v2/reasoning_on` 44 of 45 | 5.2% |
| Two tool protocols: `<tool_call>` JSON with `tool` turns (25.3%), and Terminus JSON in plain text with results in `user` turns (2.8%) | `agenttrove #10416` for the second | 28.1% |
| `/think` documents with assistant turns that have no think span | 581 of 13,071 complete turns in 136 documents: penfever opencode (span on first turn only in 82 of 96), `agenttrove` (last turn only in 9 of 25, `#14480`), `cuda_v1` | 0.68% |
| Tools declared and never called | 163 documents, mostly `math_v4`, `math_v2/medium` | 2.5% |
| User message wrapped in literal quotes | 223 opencode documents, e.g. `opencode_v1/agent_skills #4479` | 2.1% |

- Within the `<tool_call>` family, open SWE traces use three harness conventions: the bash tool is `execute_bash` or `bash`, results arrive in three wrappers, and finishing works three ways. Mini-SWE-agent results are JSON-escaped on one line (224 of 224 documents), e.g. `qwen38_27b/swe_rebench_v2 #2444`: `arg) && !arg.is_global_set())\n+ .collect::<Vec<_>>();`.
- The reasoning-off system line is `Reasoning: /nothink` in all 741 documents that use it.
- Reasoning effort has no signal. `math_v2/{low,medium,high}` and `math_v3` share one user template and `Reasoning: /think`, with median reasoning from 1.8k to 17k characters. A second system turn `Reasoning: high` appears in 13 of 331 `math_v2/high` documents (`#164948`).

### 10. Verbosity and teacher habits (medium)

- About 96% of competitive-programming tokens and about 99% of `openthoughts4-code-glm-5.2-n4` tokens sit inside one think span. 64 of 83 OpenThoughts4 documents exceed 32k tokens and 29 exceed 100k. `openthoughts4-code-glm-5.2-n4 #1293` (175k tokens) counts characters by hand: "r(1)a(2)n(3)d(4)o(5)m(6).(7) = 7".
- `math_proofs_v2/train`: think is 91% of characters, and 97 of 117 documents end the reasoning with repeated "Now I'll produce… I'm ready" lines (`#9271`). 86 of 117 are grading tasks, with verdicts skewed to full marks.
- `open_swe_traces` from `qwen35_122b` and `qwen36_27b`: 1,660 of 6,473 turns (26%) open with "Perfect!", "Excellent!", "Great!" or "Good!", against 50 of 3,907 for other teachers. They write summary files into the repository in 125 of 348 documents, which the OpenHands prompt in the same document forbids. `v1_1/sweagent/qwen36_27b/swe_rebench_v2 #3050`: `rm -f CHANGES_SUMMARY.md FINAL_CHECKLIST.md FIX_EXPLANATION.md README_FIX.md SOLUTION_SUMMARY.md VERIFICATION.md`.
- `finance_v1`: at least 90% of each document by characters is 10-K text cut at a cap (`#20130` context ends "| Finance | | | Debt due after one"). Answers were grounded and correct in the 15 checked. gpt-oss typography (U+202F) appears in 173 of 188 answers.
- Customer-service agents fabricate facts in 3 of about 8 read. `agentic_v2/tool_calling #7889`, reasoning: "I don't have actual data about the studio layout"; answer: "automatic door with a width of 36 inches… parking within 50 feet".

### 11. Harness-heavy and contrived agent data (medium)

- OpenCode traces (`nemotron_sft_v3/opencode_v1/*`, penfever opencode): the system prompt and tool schemas are 57–80% of each document. Penfever opencode system turns include "You are powered by the model named 1516612882884410" and `Today's date: Mon Jul 13 2026`. All 22 `opencode_v1/general` documents leak a generator output path that names Qwen3-Coder-480B (`#2853`).
- Penfever `nemotron-gym-*` sets (116 documents) answer a question by writing it to `/app/answer.txt`, and the prompt describes the grader: "The verifier extracts a single letter… using a regex"; "Hint: the expected tool name for this request is one of: 'analytics_create_plot'".
- Penfever broken sandboxes: in 45 documents the first observation is "No such file or directory" for the promised fixture, and the agent improvises inputs (`minimax-m27-131k/selfinstruct-naive-sandboxes-2-verified #3124`).
- Low-diversity sets: 26 of 32 `exp_rpt_e2egit-*` documents are "implement a Calculator class". `llm-verifier-freelancer` is raw scraped job postings.

### 12. Smaller findings

- **Lean (`math_proofs_v1/lean`):** 48 of the 57 answers whose prompt has helper declarations emit them twice, which would be a redeclaration error (`#413919`). 2 of 164 answers contain `sorry` (`#231906` is the six-`sorry` skeleton). No Lean compiler was run.
- **Ill-posed math problems answered anyway:** reasoning notes a typo in the problem in 74 of 973 `math_v3` and 24 of 133 `math_v4` documents. `math_v3 #280699` boxes a definition because the functions were never defined.
- **Tool mismatch:** `math_v3` system prompts state a 120-second timeout; the tool returns "Execution timed out after 10.0 seconds" in 54 turns.
- **Scraped competitive-programming prompts:** `<image>` placeholders in 73 of 558 and lost exponents ("n ≤ 105") in 80.
- **Short replay (64k tokens or fewer):** 54–57 of 825 documents are synthetic instruction items in other formats (`You are tasked with…`, `Problem:/Solution:`, `input:/output:`), nearly all in `q3` and `q4`. Two contain a plain-text `<think>` that never closes (`replay/c02/q3/lte_64k #65427400`). 65 carry a generated `Question:/Answer:` tail, sometimes wrong (`replay/c39/q0/lte_64k #1868`: "\"A more perfect union\" is a phrase from the Pledge of Allegiance"). By reading, 35–40% of this slice is LLM-rewritten web text.
- **Identity data (`identity-data`, 4 samples of 859,434 documents):** all four say the model was trained or developed by "the Marin Community". `#117405` does not deny "trained by OpenAI, right?". `#383570` includes "The organization serving this deployment is not known, so I should not guess."
- **Safety (8 samples):** 5 refuse. Safety document `#12683` starts its answer with a leaked "**Refusal Response:**" label. `#22471` refuses a fictional news story as "misinformation".
- **Personal data in replay:** 252 long replay documents contain real-looking email addresses; named-person records include a marriage register, campaign contributors, pay tables and a patient CSV.

### Checked and found clean

- All 5,280 SFT documents have one `<|begin_of_text|>` at offset 0 and end in `<|eot_id|> <|end_of_text|>`. Roles are `system`, `user`, `assistant`, `tool`. Every document starts with a system turn.
- Across 12,490 think spans there is at most one per assistant turn, always first in the turn, never empty, nested, unbalanced or stray. `/nothink` documents have zero spans in 9,586 turns. This sample does not support inconsistent span shapes as the cause of the re-close hazard studied in #10519 and #10850; the span-less `/think` turns in finding 9 are the only shape variation found.
- No foreign chat-template markers (`<|im_start|>`, `[INST]`, `<|python_tag|>`, `<|eom_id|>`) in SFT or replay, outside the replay trajectories in finding 3.
- No assistant names itself or a teacher's maker. No live-looking API keys or tokens.
- No identical documents. 15 groups (34 documents) share a first user message.
- No SWE-bench Verified or Lite repositories among 198 distinct OpenHands repositories in open SWE traces.
- No SFT document exceeds 262,144 tokens.

## Recommended changes

Ordered by expected benefit against cost. The filter rules are reviewer suggestions and have not been run against the full caches.

1. **Filter the long-context replay.** Drop documents with zlib ratio under about 0.12, a templated-line fraction over 0.6, base64 or binary content, or mean line length over 400. Cap length at 262,144 tokens. Drop documents that start `This trajectory ` or `# Repository Context`.
2. **Remove give-up endings and limit reasoning length.** Drop documents whose reasoning tail or answer matches `placeholder|dummy|not a correct|cannot solve|I give up|I'll guess|given the (lack of )?time`. Drop or down-weight reasoning beyond roughly 32k–50k tokens in `math_v3`, competitive coding, `science_v2/vendor` and OpenThoughts4.
3. **Drop or filter Nemotron multilingual v1.** Keep v2. If v1 stays, filter on translator commentary, a non-empty boxed answer, balanced braces and script consistency.
4. **Fix conversion artifacts.** Merge double system turns and drop empty ones. Strip harness warnings when the preceding rendered turn parses. Relabel `/think` documents with span-less turns as `/nothink` or drop them. Decode mini-SWE-agent tool results to plain text. Unquote opencode user turns and scrub the generator path. Restore the generation-time prompt where reasoning quotes it.
5. **Filter agent traces on outcome.** Join open SWE traces to resolve labels if they exist. Drop rollouts that end mid-task, end in `(tool use)`, or excuse failing tests. Keep AgentTrove tasks that have task files and a recorded pass. Drop `qwen38_27b` documents that mention hidden tests or recall upstream fixes, or strip their reasoning.
6. **Remove question answering from the terminal harness.** Drop or down-weight penfever `nemotron-gym-*` sets.
7. **Run instance-level decontamination** against HumanEval, SWE-bench, R2E-Gym, SWE-Gym, Terminal-Bench, Defects4J and KernelBench.
8. **Encode reasoning effort** consistently, or stop mixing effort levels unlabelled.
9. **Normalise teacher habits:** "Perfect!" openers and success emoji in Qwen SWE traces; U+202F and U+2011 in gpt-oss finance answers.
10. **Review `identity-data` separately** with a larger sample.

## Status

Review complete. No filters have been applied and no retraining has been run.

Limits:

- Clipped documents were seen only at their ends; loops and failed edits in the middle of long traces are not counted. About 6.5% of each long replay document was visible.
- No code was run, no Lean was compiled and no answer key was used. Wrong answers were counted only when the document admitted them.
- Regex counts are lower bounds, each spot-checked on about 10 hits.
- Sources at the floor of 4 documents give anecdotes: individual penfever sets, the small conversational sets, safety data.
- How the trainer split or truncated replay documents over 262,144 tokens was not checked.
- Whether user, system and tool turns carry loss was not checked. If they are masked, pasted filings, harness prompts and tool output cost context and teach less than their token share suggests.
- Benchmark overlap was matched by repository and dataset name. No instance-level join was run.
- Reviewer counts and excerpts were not independently re-derived.

## Links

* Review sample (30-day temporary prefix): `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=30d/sft-mix-viewer/review-2026.11.10-seed1/samples.parquet` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Ftmp%2Fttl%3D30d%2Fsft-mix-viewer%2Freview-2026.11.10-seed1%2Fsamples.parquet))
* SFT Mix Viewer, a separate uniform sample (8 documents per SFT store, 4 per replay cache) with text, token and token-id views: https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/378c3d80-275c-49f2-9913-0bd2c292c354/
* Mix definition and sampler: `infra/marina/apps/sft_mix_viewer/` on branch `dml/sft-mix-viewer` (not yet pushed or merged)
* Model: https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05
* Related: #10400, #10519, #10850, #9212

## Decision Log

* 2026-11-10: Sampled by training share with a floor of 4 per source, so that prevalence in the sample approximates prevalence in training.
* 2026-11-10: Reviewed long documents as head plus tail. Mid-document rates are therefore lower bounds.

## Conclusion

The rendered template is consistent. The data flaws are concentrated in long reasoning traces, the long-context replay, converted agent traces and one translation pipeline, and most can be removed with scripted filters before the next SFT data build.

# Research

The 10.05 audit identifies several distinct data interventions, but its proposed replay and reasoning filters have not been run against the full caches. The review clipped 3,760 long documents, and the repository's replay subset helper preserves whole token rows; dropping or capping rows now would change the mixture without measured false-positive rates, retained-token counts, or a matched control. This is larger than a single code fix.

**Relevant code**
- [Replay selector](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e581f387f0e243b18b6a79e52851f2d17b4c4020/experiments/sft_cold_start/replay_subset.py#L40-L75) — selects whole documents by length.

# Proposed Fix

1. Freeze the 10.05 source/cache revisions, row IDs, tokenizer, and original store manifest as the unchanged control. On a separate labeled sample, measure candidate replay rules by documents and tokens, including clean structured-data controls and each quality tier. Check how the trainer handles rows above 262,144 tokens before choosing a length policy. Publish per-rule precision estimates and full-cache hit counts; the issue's suggested cutoffs are starting hypotheses.
2. Make the first scoped PR a versioned, region-local replay selection step with a per-row keep/drop reason and source-offset hash. Compare it with the frozen control at equal trained-token positions, optimizer steps, and replay share. Report data retention, review error estimates, and paired evaluation results under [policy #10197](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197) before selecting filters for the next SFT build.

**Finding 8 (harness warnings) and finding 6 (success claims without evidence), Terminus-2, runs of 2026-10-24**

| Measure | TBLite (300 trials) | TB2 (267 trials) |
|---|---|---|
| Passed | 85 | 26 |
| Agent steps answered with a harness warning | 9,889 of 13,172 (75.1%) | 10,911 of 16,485 (66.2%) |
| Agent steps answered with a parsing error | 1,330 (10.1%) | 2,293 (13.9%) |
| Next step after a warning or error is flagged again | 94.4% | 94.6% |
| Declared `task_complete` | 214 | 181 |
| Declared complete and failed | 133 (62%) | 155 (86%) |

Nearly every warning is "Extra text detected before JSON object", the string the review found after clean turns in AgentTrove and penfever traces. Steps identical to the previous one are rare (0.7% and 3.5%), so the model ignores the warning but does not re-emit the same JSON. No step has separated reasoning content, so the "extra text" may be the think span arriving inline; I have not checked raw outputs.

**Finding 1 and recommendation 2 (long reasoning, give-up endings), temperature 0.7, 73,664-token cap**

| Benchmark | Model | Accuracy | Outputs ≥100k chars | No boxed answer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AIME24 | 09.21 SFT | 71–73% | 31–34% | 21–24% |
| AIME24 | 10.05 SFT | 78–83% | 27–32% | 12–17% |
| AIME24 | Snowball v0.1 | 73–74% | 5–7% | 3% |
| OlympiadBench | 09.21 SFT | 17–20% | 51–53% | 19–20% |
| OlympiadBench | 10.05 SFT | 18–24% | 45–53% | 18–23% |
| OlympiadBench | Snowball v0.1 | 31–35% | 1% | under 1% |

Ranges are across runs (seven for 10.05, two for 09.21, one or two for v0.1). The long 10.05 outputs wander and stop at the cap; 5–6% are exact loops. On AIME24 the median wrong answer is about 195k characters against about 19k for a right one. MATH-500 is unaffected (95–97%, 3–4% long).

A give-up phrase in the last 3,000 characters followed by a boxed wrong answer appears in 18–27 of 300 OlympiadBench outputs for 10.05. Two of four read were clear guesses, e.g. "Given the time, I'll go with Z=4 and Beryllium", then `\boxed{4}`; treat the rate as an upper bound.

**What this gives the next data build:** baselines and cheap readouts for three patches. The warned-step rate and the declared-complete-but-failed rate on TBLite cover the harness-warning strip and an outcome filter. The share of outputs over 100k characters and the no-answer rate on AIME24 and OlympiadBench cover the reasoning-length cap.

Not covered: the SWE-bench Verified run of the same date failed at the harness (496 of 500 trials exited before the first agent step). "Perfect!" openers and hidden-test mentions were under 1% of Terminus steps.

issues.author: dlwh
issues.body:
## TL;DR

Add a pinned generative OpenAI MRCR task to Marin's served evaluation path and run a bounded smoke against the registered Snowball 67B S3 export. Issue #8701 measured teacher-forced response likelihood; this follow-up requires the model to generate the requested prior response and its nonce.

## Description

Marin's pinned Evalchemy runtime has no working MRCR task. The new task should use OpenAI MRCR revision `f4c69fae7cf81f7ca26b9fee34b392a50f6b8a1d`, preserve the dataset's message order, render explicit `User:` and `Assistant:` roles for the base model, and call the completions endpoint. The scorer must return zero when the response omits the nonce, then remove the nonce from both response and gold before applying `difflib.SequenceMatcher`.

The first run should use the existing `snowball` export at `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/exports/grug/june-67b-a2b/step-42150/hf-bf16-vllm/d819cbc63780bd86/`. It should select one example from each MRCR length-bin and needle-count cell that fits the server's advertised context, use deterministic greedy decoding, and preserve raw prompts, generations, per-sample scores, prefix-hit rate, and cell coverage.

## Hypothesis or Goal

The shared evaluation launcher can serve Snowball on CoreWeave, execute canonical MRCR generation through Evalchemy, and write scored sample artifacts without a new checkpoint export. A successful smoke establishes the evaluator and serving path needed for the step-141000/156000/157000 checkpoints in #8701.

## Status

Implemented in #8706. Smoke run `20260826-180537-snowball-mrcr-smoke-40df` succeeded across all 12 context-fitting cells with zero Iris failures or preemptions.

## Links

* Paired likelihood experiment: #8701
* Implementation: #8706
* Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/openai/mrcr/tree/f4c69fae7cf81f7ca26b9fee34b392a50f6b8a1d
* Run evidence: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8702#issuecomment-5430184744
* Durable results: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/20260826-180537-snowball-mrcr-smoke-40df/results`
* Logbook: none
* W&B Report: none

## Decision Log

* Use the existing Snowball S3 export before exporting the #8701 checkpoints.
* Keep the task definition in Marin and load it through Evalchemy's local task path.
* Use completion-style prompts with explicit role labels because the evaluated checkpoint is a base model.
* Use greedy decoding for reproducible checkpoint comparisons; do not compare the score directly with OpenAI's sampled API results.

## Conclusion

The Snowball export serves real MRCR through the shared CoreWeave path and writes complete scored artifacts, so no additional export work is needed for this checkpoint. Model quality is low: aggregate MRCR accuracy was `0.004714223641098665`, and only 2 of 12 generations passed the exact nonce-prefix gate. The evaluator is ready to use after exporting the step-141000/156000/157000 checkpoints from #8701.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Analysis — not opening a PR (multi-repo experiment + cluster smoke).**

This is an experiment that spans the pinned Evalchemy fork and a live CoreWeave serve→eval run, not a self-contained code fix. The generative MRCR task (dataset load at the pinned revision, `User:`/`Assistant:` rendering, completions endpoint, nonce-gated `SequenceMatcher` scorer) has to land in the fork; Marin only pins its commit and selects the task. The smoke also needs an 8×H100 CoreWeave node to serve Snowball, which I can't run here. Handing back root cause and a proposed approach for review.

**Research**

The MRCR task does not exist in Marin — the task body lives in the external Evalchemy fork, which Marin pins by commit. Marin's served path already builds a per-task run config (`generation`, `completion_only`, `max_length`) and hands the served OpenAI URL to the Evalchemy child; task selection is a small config yaml. Snowball serving is already registered, including the base-model concat chat template and the EP/DP sharding for the 256-expert MoE, so no new export or serve wiring is needed.

- [`external_dependencies.py` L55-62](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8e27d964c1e3852f755036e74314a230a9920381/lib/marin/src/marin/external_dependencies.py#L55-L62) — `EVALCHEMY` fork pin; the MRCR task and scorer land here, then re-pin `commit`.
- [`evalchemy/runner.py` L141-181](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8e27d964c1e3852f755036e74314a230a9920381/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evalchemy/runner.py#L141-L181) — per-task `dir`/`generation`/`completion_only`/`max_length` and `extra_gen_kwargs` passed to the served run.
- [`models.py` L119-123](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8e27d964c1e3852f755036e74314a230a9920381/experiments/evaluation/models.py#L119-L123) — `snowball` export already registered with `CONCAT_CHAT_TEMPLATE` and EP/DP on 8×H100.
- [`configs/evalchemy/gsm8k-smoke.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8e27d964c1e3852f755036e74314a230a9920381/experiments/evaluation/configs/evalchemy/gsm8k-smoke.yaml) — config-yaml pattern (`tasks` + `task_options` + `limit`) a new `mrcr.yaml` mirrors.

**Proposed approach**

1. In the Evalchemy fork, add the generative MRCR task at revision `f4c69fae7cf81f7ca26b9fee34b392a50f6b8a1d`: preserve message order, render explicit `User:`/`Assistant:` roles, call completions, and score with the nonce gate (return 0 when the response omits the nonce, else strip the nonce from response and gold before `difflib.SequenceMatcher`). Re-pin `EVALCHEMY.commit` in `external_dependencies.py`.
2. Add `experiments/evaluation/configs/evalchemy/mrcr.yaml` selecting the task with `generation: true`, `completion_only: true` (base model → completions, not chat), greedy decoding (`temperature=0` via `extra_gen_kwargs`), and `max_length` matching the server's advertised context.
3. Run the bounded smoke against `snowball` through the served-evalchemy launcher, selecting one example per length-bin × needle-count cell that fits context, and persist raw prompts, generations, per-sample scores, prefix-hit rate, and cell coverage.

**Two decisions to settle before implementation**

- Cell-stratified "one example per length-bin × needle-count cell that fits context": implement inside the fork's dataset filter, or as a Marin-side sampler feeding `limit`? Context-fit depends on the served `max_length`, which argues for the task owning it.
- Artifact capture: confirm the fork's MRCR task emits per-sample logs the existing `lm_eval_samples` path can read, so prefix-hit rate and cell coverage roll up without a bespoke writer.

Once the fork task and a preferred split of the two decisions are agreed, the Marin side (dependency re-pin + `mrcr.yaml`) is small; the fork task and the CoreWeave smoke are the substantive work.

issues.body: By default Coreweave treats all pods as critical. We can provide hints for non-critical jobs with a CKS label as noted above. Let's adjust Iris to set these as appropriate. comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read issue + actionability check
- [x] Locate pod-manifest label stamping and priority bands
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (no overlapping PR/issue)
- [ ] Confirm exact CKS label key + values (blocked on screenshot content)
- [ ] Implement band→CKS-hint mapping + test

# Research

Iris task pods carry no CoreWeave workload-criticality hint, so CKS treats every pod as critical and won't drain them for node maintenance/reclamation. Pods are built one-per-attempt in `_build_pod_manifest`; the priority band (`PRODUCTION`/`INTERACTIVE`/`BATCH`) is already resolved there and drives the Kueue priority class and native `priorityClassName`, so it's the natural key for a criticality hint. The `cks.coreweave.cloud/` prefix is already used at the node level (`SYSTEM_CRITICAL_LABEL`).

**Relevant code**
- [`backends/k8s/tasks.py#L888-L917`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py#L888-L917) — pod `labels`; `effective_band` resolved here
- [`backends/k8s/tasks.py#L1019-L1021`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py#L1019-L1021) — band → native `priorityClassName`
- [`job.proto#L614-L617`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/rpc/job.proto#L614-L617) — `PRIORITY_BAND_{PRODUCTION,INTERACTIVE,BATCH}`
- [`platforms/k8s/constants.py#L16-L25`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/k8s/constants.py#L16-L25) — existing CoreWeave `interruptable` toleration
- [`platforms/k8s/nodepool_manifests.py#L15`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/k8s/nodepool_manifests.py#L15) — node-level `cks.coreweave.cloud/system-critical`

# Proposed Fix

Stamp a CKS pod-criticality label in the `_build_pod_manifest` `labels` dict, keyed off `effective_band`:

| Band | Hint |
|------|------|
| `PRODUCTION` | critical (default — omit label) |
| `INTERACTIVE` | graceful-interruptible |
| `BATCH` | interruptible |

Define the label key/values as constants next to `COREWEAVE_INTERRUPTABLE_TOLERATION`. Test: assert the manifest label per band via the existing k8s pod-manifest test.

**Blocking question:** the exact CKS label key and its value strings live only in the screenshot, which I can't fetch (auth-gated attachment) or confirm via web search from here. Please confirm before I implement — specifically the label key (e.g. `cks.coreweave.cloud/<?>`) and whether the values are `critical` / `interruptable` / `graceful-interruptible`. This is a production-scheduling label, so I won't guess it.

This is a new scheduling feature touching live CoreWeave behavior, so per policy I'm posting analysis for review rather than opening a PR up front.

issues.author: muchanem
issues.body:
Sub-issue of #8366 (item 2). `load_parquet_batch` decodes every row group that overlaps its row range, then applies `filter_expr` with `table.filter` (`lib/zephyr/src/zephyr/readers.py:312`). There is no statistics-based row-group pruning, no page-index pruning, and no in-decoder filtering. #4344 chose this deliberately to fix the pyarrow.dataset memory blowup (#4325) and measured the cost: 0.17s vs 0.01s for a selective filter on a small column subset. A DataFusion-backed reader restores pushdown and retires pyarrow reader bugs we have hit (#5334 page headers over 8 MiB, apache/arrow#39808, #4586).

Plan:

- Swap at the `InputFileSpec` -> RecordBatch boundary. `_compute_file_pushdown` (`plan.py:517`) and the pipeline API do not change.
- One datafusion-python `SessionContext` per worker subprocess, configured like finelog's engine (`lib/finelog/rust/src/query/mod.rs:227`): `pushdown_filters` and `reorder_filters` on, a memory pool sized from the Iris task allocation so a bad scan fails with `ResourcesExhausted` instead of OOM-killing the worker, a parquet metadata cache, `repartition_file_min_size` lowered from the 10 MiB default.
- A `to_datafusion_expr` lowering for the `zephyr.expr` AST, beside `evaluate` and `to_pyarrow_expr`.
- One `register_object_store` per bucket using the CoreWeave contract from finelog's deployer (`lib/finelog/src/finelog/deploy/_k8s.py:158`): bucket spliced into the endpoint host, region `auto`, virtual-hosted addressing. Credentials come from the same rigging config the fsspec path reads.
- Intra-file row order is preserved; consumers assert it (sorted merge joins, `verify_fuzzy_dups`). Scan repartitioning is pinned accordingly.
- A backend enum selects pyarrow or datafusion during development and review only. After review the switch is wholesale and the pyarrow path is deleted. Deletion is gated on row-sliced specs (`approx_shard_bytes` spans): datafusion-python cannot select row groups today, so those specs need a PyO3 shim or an upstream change first.

Spikes before the implementation PRs:

1. Scan `s3://marin-us-east-*` through datafusion-python. cwobject.com accepts virtual-hosted addressing only, and finelog never scans S3 through its query context, so this path is unproven here. Fallback is the `object_store` env contract; failure reroutes the project to a PyO3 extension (`lib/dupekit` precedent).
2. Wheel coverage for every machine type we run: x86_64 (cw-rno2a and cw-us-east-02a GPU and CPU pools), aarch64 (cw-us-east-08a Grace), macOS arm64 dev machines. A missing wheel means a Rust toolchain build in every Iris worker venv.
3. A single-file microbenchmark: full scan at parity, a selective predicate winning, and a `pushdown_filters` regression check (5 of 43 ClickBench queries got slower even after the arrow-rs page-cache fix).

Benchmarks: tier 1 extends `lib/zephyr/tests/benchmark_parquet_reader.py` with a synthetic corpus sweeping row-group size, filter-column clustering, selectivity, and projection width. Tier 2 extends `experiments/datakit/zephyr_benchmark.py` over `sample_0.1b_7d7d8fd7` and `sample_100b_8ae7a94f`, one Iris job per workload and config point. Workloads: normalize, the common_corpus language/open-type predicate, the minhash two-column scan, scatter-chunk reads, the consolidate attribute join, and the global exact-dedup id scan. Each run records wall clock, bytes fetched, GET count, peak RSS, and DataFusion's `row_groups_pruned_statistics` counters.

Regression tests: a three-way differential asserting `evaluate`, `to_pyarrow_expr`, and `to_datafusion_expr` select identical rows on generated tables, with null semantics pinned by test; spec parity across backends (filter-column widening, row ranges, `include_file_paths`, row order); a golden-file corpus where the #5334 repro passes; the #4325 RSS bound kept green.

Scope: reader backend only. The SQL surface stays with #7686, distributed DataFusion with #7588, Polars pipeline internals with #8154/#8256. #5861 proposed a SQL loader and was declined; this issue stays below that line. Automatic lambda lowering is tracked in #8416 and projection inference in #8417. Landing is a stacked PR series at the end of the campaign.

Done when:
The DataFusion reader lands, the differential/parity/corpus suites run in unit CI, the benchmark report over the six workloads is posted here, and the pyarrow path is removed.

issues.author: Helw150
issues.body:
## TL;DR

The four-site Pallas SConv variant passed matched Gate 1 at d512 and d768 on v5p-8. It improved Paloma macro loss at both scales while reducing throughput by about 5.7%. The quality gain outweighed the TPU cost: combined effective speedup was 1.242 at d512 and 1.131 at d768.

## Results

| Cell | Control loss | SConv loss | Loss delta | Control throughput | SConv throughput | Throughput ratio | Quality speedup | Combined speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| d512 | 3.67605 | 3.62268 | -0.05337 | 366,600 tokens/s | 345,197 tokens/s | 0.9416 | 1.3189 | 1.2419 |
| d768 | 3.29501 | 3.26632 | -0.02869 | 245,904 tokens/s | 231,991 tokens/s | 0.9434 | 1.1989 | 1.1311 |

Each pair uses the same model scale, optimizer, data mixture, evaluation, seed, sequence length, batch size, token budget, current recipe defaults, and v5p-8 topology. SConv is the model-level difference. Throughput is the mean over the final 100 logged training steps after deduplicating restored global steps by latest timestamp. Final logged token counts match within each pair: 915,931,136 at d512 and 2,996,305,920 at d768.

## Artifacts

- d512 control W&B: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/MOE-PSC-CTRL-101-d512-v5p8
- d512 SConv W&B: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/MOE-PSC-101-d512-v5p8-gate1
- d768 control W&B: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/MOE-PSC-CTRL-102-d768-v5p8
- d768 SConv W&B: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/MOE-PSC-102-d768-v5p8-gate1
- d512 control checkpoint: `gs://marin-us-central1/grug/moe_pallas_sconv_control_d512/2026.08.18/checkpoints/step-3494/metadata.json`
- d768 control checkpoint: `gs://marin-us-central1/grug/moe_pallas_sconv_control_d768/2026.08.18/checkpoints/step-11430/metadata.json`
- Logbook: `.agents/logbooks/moe-pallas-sconv-v5p8.md`
- Implementation PR: #8387
- Kernel dependency: #8331

## Interpretation

The prior 0.517 and 0.612 effective-speedup values used historical May Recipe cells with different sequence length, accelerator, PKO, long-RoPE, and z-loss settings. They are descriptive cross-recipe comparisons and do not isolate SConv.

The matched controls reverse that conclusion. On TPU, SConv has a measured 5.84% throughput cost at d512 and 5.66% at d768, but improves loss enough to produce effective speedup above 1 at both scales.

The numerical Pallas convolution core was not the source of the integration failures. The code defects were at explicit-mesh, mixed-precision cotangent, and empty-mesh integration boundaries. The control runs also confirm that the live interruptions were infrastructure faults: d512 completed without preemption, while d768 completed with three worker-reconciliation preemptions, zero task failures, and successful checkpoint recovery. No Pallas, XLA, OOM, non-finite loss, or accelerator-device error appeared.

## Decision

Matched Gate 1 required combined effective speedup above 1 at both scales. The variant passed. Gate 2 is eligible but has not been launched as part of the matched-control run.

## Prompt (verbatim)

> Cool, can you run a test run on v5p 8 using these layers Mayank added as a experiments/grug/moe/agent.md ablation?

comments.body:

No PR. This is an experiment whose definition of done is a **live v5p-8 run** (verify compile, fwd/bwd, doc-boundary masking, training progress), and it depends on an **unmerged** PR. That is outside the automated issue-fix path — it belongs to the `experiments/grug/moe` experiment workflow once the dependency lands. Analysis below for a human to drive.

# Research

The layer this issue integrates does not exist on `main`. #8331 (`DepthwiseCausalConvolution`, branch `conv`) is **open**, and its Pallas TPU forward/backward only runs in the TPU CI suite — so a v5p-8 smoke is exactly the missing coverage. The target recipe `experiments/grug/moe` currently has **no** conv sites and no `sconv*` config knobs.

A parallel, further-optimized SConv effort is already in flight and should shape this work:
- `experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L410` — existing pad-and-shift `ShortConv`, wired at k/v/attn/mlp via `sconv_sites`/`sconv`/`sconv_kernel` (identity-init, segment-aware).
- #8369 `[levanter] Fused depthwise causal conv for ShortConv` — open; a bandwidth-bound Pallas rewrite of the same op.
- #8359 (merged) `Remove the value-branch SConv from the hero` — the hero deliberately dropped the **V** site for cost. Integrating #8331's four sites verbatim (incl. V) re-adds a site the hero team just removed.

**Relevant code**
- [`experiments/grug/moe/model.py#L270`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe/model.py#L270) — `CausalSelfAttention`; K/V proj + `attn_out` (L367) are two of the four sites.
- [`experiments/grug/moe/model.py#L535`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe/model.py#L535) — `MoEMLP`; branch output is the `mlp_out` site.
- [`experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L452-L465`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L452) — reference wiring pattern to mirror (`sconv_k`, gating on `sconv_sites`).
- [`experiments/grug/moe/agent.md#L161-L186`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe/agent.md#L161) — v5p-8 Iris submission command for the smoke.

# Proposed approach

1. **Land #8331 first.** Nothing here compiles until `levanter.layers.depthwise_causal_convolution` is on `main`.
2. **Config knobs on `GrugModelConfig`** (mirror hero): `sconv: bool = False`, `sconv_sites: tuple[str, ...] = ("k", "v", "attn", "mlp")`, `sconv_kernel: int = 4`. Default off so the baseline stays byte-identical.
3. **Insert four `DepthwiseCausalConvolution` layers**, identity-init, at K/V proj (post-projection, per-head channels), `attn_out` (L367), and `mlp_out` (`MoEMLP.__call__`). Pass `segment_ids` from the `AttentionMask` (`model.py#L316`) into the layer's mask argument so packed-doc boundaries never mix across taps — this is the load-bearing correctness property to check.
4. **Smoke on one v5p-8** at `d512` per `agent.md`, `--version dev`, conv on. Confirm compile, finite loss/grads, and that toggling `sconv` off reproduces the baseline. Not a Gate 1 quality run.
5. **Reconcile with the hero direction** before a full gate: #8359 removed the V site for throughput; decide whether the gate recipe keeps 4 sites or matches the hero's 3, and whether to build on #8369's fused kernel instead of #8331's.

Open question for @Helw150: integrate #8331's layer as written (4 sites incl. V), or align the smoke with the hero's current 3-site (`k`, `attn`, `mlp`) configuration?

<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This issue tracks expert-parallel MoE performance on B200/GB200, starting from #7012's single-rack MFU target and then moving to larger production-like Grug configurations. Early 32-GPU tests showed EP could become net-positive, several higher-EP attempts were blocked or confounded by XLA/JAX CUBIN-load and NCCL restart failures, and later fixed/controlled runs showed ring EP working at multi-rack scale but often near EP1 parity. The latest D6144 measurements use the #7201 architecture in the standalone #7279 harness. Within that harness, `ring_cute` EP4 is the fastest control (+16.7% throughput over EP1), and latent `L3072/I3072/e256` with `ring_cute` EP4 preserves total routed-expert parameter count while halving active routed-expert work and EP payload. It improves throughput by 16.0% and median step time by 13.8% versus the fastest standalone control. These measurements do not reproduce #7201's production-launcher throughput, which is 245.9K tok/s for unchunked `sonic_cute` EP1 and 253.0K tok/s with chunked-expert FSDP. The e128 latent variant is throughput-first if halving routed-expert parameters is acceptable, but EP>1 for that arm is currently blocked by the intermittent JAX 0.10.1 CUBIN loader issue tracked in #7421.

## Description

Spun out of #7012 (single-rack B200 MoE MFU above 20%) -- the EP thread has outgrown a side-note there. Baseline evidence, all in the logbook (B200MFU-017 through -031):

- EP backend ladder at 32 GPUs: ring / ring_cute / ragged_all_to_all (+one-shot-kernel flag) / a2a_cute across EP2-EP32. The a2a default-path pathology was root-caused to XLA's one-shot ragged-all-to-all kernel (~297 ms/call; corroborated by openxla/xla#33386) and collapses 7.7x with one flag (1.88 -> 14.41%).
- 32-GPU regime change: EP goes net-positive because dispatching tokens beats FSDP-all-gathering expert weights every layer; a2a_cute is EP-flat and crosses ring_cute at EP16, making it the cross-NVL-domain candidate.
- Step anatomy: collectives are about 48-50% of device-busy time, dominated by many small per-layer dispatch legs; NVLink counters show 80 GB/s per GPU/direction at EP4 (133-136 at EP1) against 956 GB/s capability -- latency-bound, with large bandwidth headroom at fixed traffic.
- Remat at 32-way: `none` fits and wins d2560 (15.04%); `all_but_moe` ports to the EP backends (d5120 16.90%).

Current 32-GPU bests: d2560 **15.04%** (ring_cute EP4, remat none), d5120 **16.90%** (ring_cute EP8, all_but_moe).

## Hypothesis or Goal

The EP dispatch/combine path can move from many small serialized legs to fewer/larger/overlapped transfers, converting NVLink headroom into MFU. Targets: d2560 >=18% and d5120 >=20% at 32 GPUs; a validated cross-rack (IB) EP recipe past one NVL72 domain.

Hypothesis queue (expected-value order):

1. Chunked-pipeline EP block (TE NCCL_EP-style decomposition: SM-capped persistent comm kernels feeding chunked expert GEMMs) -- the decomposition, not the SM budget, is the valuable half (B200MFU-016/-021).
2. Overlap: manual-FDO PGLE (auto-PGLE crashes multi-host, B200MFU-030) and collective-matmul-style overlap of dispatch with expert GEMMs.
3. Leg reduction: SonicMoE-style gather/combine under ring/a2a (replaces the take/scatter-add legs); capacity-factor and padding tuning.
4. Cross-rack ladder past 72 GPUs: a2a_cute over IB (the regime it is predicted for; transport pre-flight validated in B200MFU-028).
5. MXFP8 expert GEMMs + fp8-wire dispatch (halves dispatch bytes; compute is only about one third of busy time, so GEMM-only gains are capped).
6. Upstream asks: XLA one-shot ragged-all-to-all single-host performance and the NCCL-path per-call host sync (extends openxla/xla#33386).

## Status

2026-07-21: single-rack GB200 D6144 standalone-harness results are complete. For the #7201 architecture in this harness, the fastest control is `ring_cute` EP4 at 220,648 tok/s and 19.686% GB200 MFU. These values are for within-harness comparisons and do not reproduce #7201's production launcher. For latent MoE, `L3072/I3072/e256` with `ring_cute` EP4 preserves total routed-expert parameter count while reducing active routed-expert work: 256,059 tok/s, 16.3862 s median step, and 19.401% architecture-aware MFU. The `L3072/I3072/e128` EP1 result is faster if fewer routed-expert parameters are acceptable, but EP>1 is blocked by the intermittent CUBIN loader issue tracked in #7421.

* 2026-07-21 -- In the standalone matrix using the #7201 D6144 architecture, ring EP4 is the fastest control. Prefer latent `L3072/I3072/e256` with ring EP4 when total routed-expert parameter count should remain fixed and reduced active routed-expert work is acceptable.

🤖 **High-EP ragged-a2a ladder (EP16/32/64 inside one NVL72 rack): total negative — EP8 is the hard ceiling for every backend at b1024, and the EP16 CUBIN bug is upstream XLA, not our adapter** (logbook B200MFU-033)

Follow-up to the reference-config rerun above. Since a2a was the only backend surviving EP≥8 and the rack has NVLink headroom, we ran `{ragged_all_to_all_cute, pure-XLA ragged_all_to_all + NCCL-path flag}` × `{EP16, EP32 (replica-2), EP64 (replica-1 — EP is capped at the copy size, and at 64 by the expert count, so a 72-GPU gang would buy nothing)}` at the reference config. **All six arms fail:**

| arm | layout | failure |
|---|---|---|
| a2a_cute EP16 | rep2 | CUBIN-load `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE` (2nd fresh-cache run — deterministic) |
| **pure-XLA raa EP16** | rep2 | **identical CUBIN failure — no CuTe/QuACK anywhere in this arm** |
| a2a_cute EP32 | rep2 | OOM: single **104.13 GiB** alloc in `jit_train_step` |
| pure-XLA raa EP32 | rep2 | OOM: 104.03 GiB (same intermediate) |
| a2a_cute EP64 | rep1 | CUBIN-load failure |
| pure-XLA raa EP64 | rep1 | NCCL `ncclGroupEnd` → `Cuda failure 2 'out of memory'` |

Findings:

1. **The EP16 CUBIN failure is upstream XLA GPU codegen.** The pure-XLA arm reproduces it with zero custom kernels in the graph, which resolves the "a2a16 trigger unidentified" question from the last update and removes the CuTe adapter as a suspect. Combined with the ring family's 2³¹-element all-gather boundary, the reference config now has **no working backend above EP8**.
2. **EP32's wall is an SPMD partitioner fallback, not the dispatch buffers.** Both EP32 arms OOM on the same ~104 GiB temporary, and their compiles emit `spmd_partitioner.cc` "Involuntary full rematerialization … will replicate the tensor and then partition it" warnings (XLA b/433785288, slated to be fixed by Shardy) for the microbatch input resharding into the copy's `(data, expert)` mesh. The a2a dispatch buffers really are EP-degree-independent — but what SPMD synthesizes around them isn't once the data axis collapses (data=1 at EP32 under replica-2).
3. Incidental: the benchmark's input pipeline carries an `s32[1024,4096]` batch tensor pinned `{maximal device=0}` that SPMD force-replicates on every compile — benign here, but it's the same device-0-pinning pattern as the FA4 `pure_callback` metadata issue that wedges the driver at 8 racks (#7012). That pattern is now two-for-two on this hardware week; worth hunting down generally.
4. Practically: intra-rack EP>8 at production batch is **blocked upstream**, so the `--xla_dump_to` → openxla repro (EP16 pure-XLA raa is the cleanest: stock jaxlib, one flag, deterministic) is now the gating item for rack-scale EP here, not an optional cleanup. Short-term nothing is lost — EP's margin at 16 seq/GPU is only +0.6 pp — but cross-rack EP, where FSDP stops scaling, needs this fixed or designed around (bounding the per-shard token×EP product, or TE NCCL_EP whose chunked staging never materializes group-scale buffers).

Next: file the openxla issue with an HLO dump; optionally a b512@EP16 control to pin the trigger to the token×EP product rather than EP degree per se.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 **The EP≥8 CUBIN-load bug is root-caused and worked around — high-EP at the reference config is unblocked** (logbook B200MFU-034)

Follow-up to the high-EP ladder above. After a ~15-job bisection, the `Failed to load in-memory CUBIN … CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE` failure is **not a kernel or shape bug at all**: it's XLA's per-kernel-module executable layout (LLVM-module-split parallel compilation → ~5.6k separate CUBIN modules loaded per device at first execution) interacting with **CUDA lazy module loading** and the full process state (near-capacity `cuda_async` pool + NCCL communicators + 4 contexts). The driver returns a spurious `INVALID_VALUE` ("compiled for a different GPU?" — it isn't) instead of an honest error.

Key evidence:
- Fails only at L48 × b1024 × EP≥8; **identical per-GPU MoE buffer shapes pass at 4/8/16 GPUs** — the -032 "2³¹-element x_global" attribution was correlation within the 64-GPU grid, not the cause.
- The dumped 34.7 MB train-step PTX compiles and loads fine offline; **all 6,859 per-kernel CUBIN blobs** (captured via `--xla_gpu_kernel_cache_file`) load individually and in kept-loaded/concurrent storms; module-count (100k) and memory-pressure probes error honestly (`CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY`) — the artifact and the driver are each fine in isolation.
- Three independent one-line fixes, each verified green on the exact failing config:
  1. **`CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=EAGER`** ← adopting as the gang default (no compile-time cost)
  2. `--xla_gpu_force_compilation_parallelism=1`
  3. `--xla_gpu_enable_llvm_module_compilation_parallelism=false` (most targeted)

Implications for this issue: the "EP8 ceiling" from the last update was an artifact of this bug — ring/a2a EP≥8 at b1024 should now run under EAGER, so the high-EP intra-rack scaling question is measurable again. (The EP32 replicate-then-repartition OOM, XLA b/433785288, is a separate real limit and stands.) Next: re-run the EP16/EP32 a2a arms under EAGER for actual MFU numbers, and file the upstream report from the evidence dossier.
