What the data say:
- On identical tasks, GLM LOW rows push the student far below the parent, and contributor rows lift it above the parent on SWE-bench. The contributor-side +10 is the first gap against the parent that clears noise.
- Less GLM data does not help. lowshared used 39% of LOW plain's tokens and is not closer to the parent; 85 of its 100 SWE-bench episodes hit the context limit and it submitted 12 times. A lower learning rate (3e-7: SWE −7 [−13, −1] against 1e-6) and an earlier checkpoint (2 of 3 epochs: +5 [−4, +13]) also did not rescue the GLM rows.
- On contributor rows, plain, RS-multi, recovery and plateau dropping are indistinguishable.
- Limits: single runs on 100 tasks; the pair is matched on tasks, not tokens; read the small-budget pair for the gap, not for absolute levels.

Not tested: what remains between the row sets is the teacher (GLM 5.3 against Kimi/Qwen) and the harness format. Our GLM rows use each eval's own action protocol; the contributor rows use the other one.

Trace decontamination: the trained trace text was checked against the 100 SWE-bench gold and test patches and the 100 TBLite tests and solutions. There were 3 flags, all TBLite, all generic code (imports, a file-reading loop). Nothing was excluded.

Cost of these runs: 184.9 H100-h training and 106.4 H100-h screens. Documented total for the experiment: about 6,070 H100-h (a partial subtotal, not an invoice).

comments.author: karansag
comments.body: 🤖 **Summary: no SFT method beat plain SFT by enough to matter; the source of the traces decided the result. The experiment is stopped and written up.** ## Data We took 2,200 TMAX and 2,100 SWE-smith tasks and regenerated traces using GLM 5.3. This way, both would have a consistent teacher. We also ran these traces using the corresponding eval harness under policy. For SWE-smith, this was `mini-swe-agent`, and for TMax, it was `Terminus-2`. Relay pools were also constructed similarly, starting with a base Snowball and handing off to GLM 5.3 Note that GLM 5.3 was tried with different effort levels (as per comments above). We used the contributor rows directly (SWE-smith + TMax under Kimi 2.5 / Qwen3.6-27B) for both pilot sweeps and as a final run to assess the impact of our data after a negative with GLM 5.3 traces. ## What we did We compared plain SFT, rejection-sampled SFT (RS-multi), relay, recovery and plateau dropping for agentic coding on Snowball v0 and v0.1. The task pool was about 2,200 TMax and 2,100 SWE-smith tasks. Traces came from GLM 5.3 at three reasoning efforts, then from the contributor traces (Kimi-2.5 SWE-smith, Qwen3.6-27B TMax). Screens: SWE-bench Verified random-100, TBLite-100, GSM8K and BFCL-Parity. ## What we found 1. **Every arm trained on GLM 5.3 traces scored below its parent** on SWE-bench and TBLite, while gaining on GSM8K and BFCL. The students took about twice the steps of their training traces, ran into the 32k context limit in most SWE-bench episodes and rarely submitted. 2. **Methods mattered little.** Only relay on LOW rows beat plain SFT (SWE-bench +8 [+1, +16]), and it still trailed its parent. On contributor rows, plain, RS-multi, recovery and plateau dropping were indistinguishable. 3. **The rows mattered most.** With the same 1,432 tasks, parent and recipe, contributor rows beat GLM LOW rows by SWE-bench +26 [+17, +36] and TBLite +9 [+1, +17]. The contributor side also beat parent v0.1 on SWE-bench by +10 [+1, +19]. 4. **Less GLM exposure did not help.** A lower learning rate, an earlier checkpoint and a smaller subset all stayed below the parent. ## Hypotheses (untested) Why the GLM arms lost while the contributor rows gained, and why collaborators got large SFT gains from Kimi and Qwen traces on a weaker Snowball parent ([blog post, 2026-10-21](https://lukedhlee.github.io/blog/2026/10/21/turning-snowball-into-a-coding-agent/)). Ordered by how much evidence we have. 1. **Teacher traces.** GLM 5.3 episodes were long, reasoning-heavy and often ended at the context limit; the students copied that. Kimi and Qwen traces did not. The matched pair (+26 SWE-bench on the same tasks) is the strongest evidence we have for anything. A different teacher on the same tasks and format would test it. 2. **SFT alone does not fix action behavior.** The collaborators' best results came from SFT then RL; their trace analysis found RL cut invalid actions from about 80% to 2% and taught the model to submit its best effort instead of running out of context. Those are exactly the failures of our GLM students. RL from a shootout checkpoint would test it. 3. **Training stack.** The collaborators report that an early relay advantage disappeared after correcting training precision and MoE expert capacity. Our arms trained before #10492 made expert capacity configurable; at the default capacity with expert parallelism, overflow tokens are dropped silently (seen later in the identity work). Whether the shootout arms dropped tokens is not known. It can be checked by replaying one saved run with drop counting. 4. **Eval protocol.** Our screens use 32k context, 1,800 s and one trial; the collaborators use 64k, a 3x timeout and three repeats. Our GLM students produce longer episodes, so our limits may punish them more than a longer protocol would. The 65k-context and 5,400 s checks ran on the parent only, not on a student. 5. **Parent headroom.** Their parent was the general-SFT 09-21 checkpoint (12.8% SWE-bench under Terminus-2). Ours were merged and RL-trained parents, and v0 already carries a relay graft trained on 1,012 of the same Kimi trajectories. Demonstrations may have less to add to our parents. 6. **Harness format.** Our GLM traces were recorded in each eval's own harness and hurt that eval; the contributor traces were recorded the other way round and did not. Training in the eval's own format may overwrite the parent's behavior there. But the collaborators' Kimi SWE traces are Terminus-2 format and their SWE eval runs under Terminus-2, and that worked, so this is weaker than it first looked. Format is confounded with the teacher. Re-recording GLM traces in the other format (about 125 H100-h) would separate them. 7. **Training dose.** We trained 3 epochs at 1e-6. The collaborators' RL started from a 7-epoch SFT model, and their RL ablation found more epochs helped until overfitting. This would not rescue the GLM arms, which got worse, but the contributor rows were never trained past 3 epochs. Cost: about 6,070 H100-h documented. ## Records - Paper (15 pages, PDF, with the three experiment diagrams): [agentic-sft-shootout.pdf](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/f0ad30e1ebafa432c3af144aa6faad76119a6c97/logbooks/10213-sft-shootout/agentic-sft-shootout.pdf), with a short [notebook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/f0ad30e1ebafa432c3af144aa6faad76119a6c97/logbooks/10213-sft-shootout/notebook.md) and the diagram sources in marin-logbooks. - Results by round: the comments above, last two dated 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-24. - Code: reusable parts in draft PRs #10255 (plateau dropping in `train_lm`), #10887 (recording relay proxy and trace rebuild) and #10888 (recovery rows). The rest of the experiment code is archived on marin-logbooks branches `codex/10213-sft-shootout-pr`, listed in the notebook. - Models: private `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-SFT-Shootout-*` repos on the Hub.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
When a served model's Iris task is preempted and replaced, the native capability proxy answers requests that arrive during the replacement with HTTP 502 `upstream transport error: client error (Connect)`. Clients see a hard failure for a gap Iris is already recovering from.

Impact: on 2026-10-18 an Evalchemy GSM8K screen on H100 lost 112 of 1,319 rows. Kueue preempted the serve task at 00:14:07 UTC; Iris rescheduled it and the replacement was initializing from 00:14:55. At 00:19 the proxy returned 502 to the queued requests, the client exhausted its retries, and the rows were recorded as `EVALCHEMY_INFRASTRUCTURE_ERROR` (`model_transport`). Recovery needed a manual selective rerun of the 112 doc ids and a cached regrade before the record could be merged (1,215/1,319 after recovery).

A second instance on 2026-10-19 lost 960 of 1,319 GSM8K rows. Kueue preempted the serve task at 03:42:04 UTC. Requests in flight at that moment got 502 `client error (SendRequest)` (15 responses at 03:42). Requests sent afterwards got 502 `client error (Connect)` (985 responses from 03:42 to 03:47) until the client gave up, and the rows were recorded as `EVALCHEMY_INFRASTRUCTURE_ERROR`. The same serve task was preempted six more times over the next 11 hours (attempts 1 to 6) at interactive priority. That record needed a full GSM8K rerun.

The 502 comes from the native proxy's upstream error path ([`lib/iris/rust/src/lib.rs` L1243-L1246](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8e99858a17df0463daac6b104f5eddb0ffa79ffd/lib/iris/rust/src/lib.rs#L1243-L1246)), which maps any connect failure to `BAD_GATEWAY`. [`lib/iris/docs/federation.md`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8e99858a17df0463daac6b104f5eddb0ffa79ffd/lib/iris/docs/federation.md) documents this message as "cannot connect to its upstream".

Reproduce:
1. Serve a model through a capability URL (for example the eval launcher with Harbor or a capability-routed Evalchemy run).
2. Send a steady stream of requests through the capability URL.
3. Preempt or cancel the serving task and let Iris start a replacement under the same endpoint name.
4. Requests sent before the replacement registers return 502 with the message above.

Expected: while the endpoint's job is still live and a replacement task is pending or initializing, the proxy holds the request until the endpoint registers again (bounded by the request timeout), or returns 503 with `Retry-After`. Clients retry connect errors and 503s with backoff for at least the documented serve replacement time. A replacement can take much longer than a request timeout: in the second instance the serve stayed unavailable for the rest of the GSM8K client's retry budget. Holding requests therefore covers short gaps only. Long gaps need the 503 signal so that the client can pause instead of recording failures.

Done when: a serve-replacement test through the capability proxy completes requests sent during the gap, or receives 503 with `Retry-After`, and no 502 is returned while the job is live.

Related: #10237 covers the direct-route client (`remote_inference`) keeping a stale address after rescheduling.

Evidence (Iris task events and the Evalchemy client log, URLs omitted):

```
2026-10-18T00:14:07.473Z attempt 0  k8s/kueue        WorkloadEvictedDueToPreempted  Preempted to accommodate a workload (UID: 3fc9af02-…)
2026-10-18T00:14:50.525Z attempt 0  iris/controller  TaskRetryScheduled             Backend reported PREEMPTED; controller returned the task to PENDING.
2026-10-18T00:14:55.578Z attempt 1  k8s/container    PodInitializing
[00:19:08] eval-gsm8k-0shot-2a8d8acc/0 | API request failed! Status code: 502, Response text: {"error":"upstream transport error: client error (Connect)"}. Retrying...
[00:19:09] eval-gsm8k-0shot-2a8d8acc/0 | API request failed! Status code: 502, Response text: {"error":"upstream transport error: client error (Connect)"}. Retrying...
```

Second instance: serve task `/karan/eval-20261019-025403-task238-arm-recovery-lr1e-06-step791-04d5/inference-177d09d0c73a4f048310e082db087746/0` (Kueue `WorkloadEvictedDueToPreempted` at 03:42:04, 05:19:02, 07:12:39, 10:56:25, 11:04:59, 14:19:01 and 14:24:54 UTC), evaluator task `/karan/eval-20261019-025403-task238-arm-recovery-lr1e-06-step791-04d5/eval-gsm8k-0shot-4ac3cd86/0`, record `20261019-025403-task238-arm-recovery-lr1e-06-step791-gsm8k-0shot-6554` (`infra_failed`, 359/1,319 scored).

First instance: serve task `/karan/eval-20261018-000555-task204-lr1e-06-step1095-1b9b/inference-a54b7942d3b34ffba92e5f0d4192aa69/0`. Evaluator task: `/karan/eval-20261018-000555-task204-lr1e-06-step1095-1b9b/eval-gsm8k-0shot-2a8d8acc/0`. Record: `20261018-000555-task204-lr1e-06-step1095-gsm8k-0shot-77c1`.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

Iris keeps a serving endpoint's last address until its lease expires (at most 10 minutes). The native proxy can therefore route a request to a preempted task; its upstream transport error path returns 502. Once the lease expires, the registry omits the endpoint and the same live job can instead return 404. The registry has no replacement state, so changing 502 to 503 alone would leave that later gap unresolved. [PR #10033](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10033) handles Evalchemy's direct-route relay and does not change this capability path.

**Relevant code**
- [`endpoint_service.py#L40-L49`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/endpoint_service.py#L40-L49) — ten-minute registration lease.
- [`endpoint_service.py#L165-L177`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/endpoint_service.py#L165-L177) — live mappings enter the proxy snapshot.
- [`lib.rs#L230-L264`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/rust/src/lib.rs#L230-L264) — expired mappings are skipped.
- [`lib.rs#L1190-L1240`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/rust/src/lib.rs#L1190-L1240) — transport failures become 502.
- [`client.py#L79-L93`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evalchemy/client.py#L79-L93) — Evalchemy allows eight request retries.

# Proposed Fix

The failure chain is task preemption → old endpoint address remains routable → connect/send fails → proxy returns 502; after lease expiry, lookup returns 404. This needs a controller/proxy availability contract and a capability-client retry budget, so it is larger than a local status-code patch.

1. Preserve an authenticated endpoint name while its owning task is being retried. Publish `ready` versus `replacing` in the controller's proxy snapshot/deltas; preemption and lease expiry make the old address unavailable, replacement registration restores `ready`, and terminal job/task state removes the route. Reconstruct the same state after controller restart.
2. Return 503 with `Retry-After` for `replacing` and for connect/send failures to task-owned endpoints, including a race before the registry update. Keep ordinary 404 for unknown names and 502 for unrelated upstream/protocol failures. Do not replay an in-flight POST inside the proxy.
3. Verify the pinned Evalchemy and Harbor capability clients retry 503 according to `Retry-After` with a time budget tied to the evaluation deadline and stop on terminal serve state. Extend their policy where needed; leave the direct-route relay in #10033 alone.
4. Add a real HTTP capability-proxy test that sends requests before preemption, during replacement, after the old lease expires, and after a new address registers. Assert no 502/404 during the recoverable gap, 503 plus `Retry-After` until recovery, successful forwarding afterwards, and terminal/unknown routes ending promptly. Cover an in-flight send failure and the federated capability relay as separate cases.

Open decision: the repository documents a 10-minute endpoint lease but no upper bound on serve replacement. Use the evaluation's overall deadline as the retry cap unless a shorter serve-replacement contract is established; eight immediate request retries are insufficient for the observed multi-minute gaps.

comments.body:
🤖
## Research

#10169 is merged and covers brokered evaluator recovery, but the native capability proxy still returns 502 on a stale task address. On lease expiry the endpoint projection hides and sweeps that address, so the proxy then returns 404 even while Iris can replace the task. Endpoint close also removes the registration before replacement.

## Proposed Fix

Keep a known task-owned endpoint as an unavailable proxy route while its task remains retryable, without exposing its expired address to endpoint discovery. Return 503 with Retry-After for that route and for a task-owned upstream transport failure; a replacement registration restores normal forwarding. Add HTTP regressions for stale, expired, replacement, and terminal routes. The Evalchemy client on main already retries 503 and respects Retry-After within its transport budget.

Iris keeps a known task-owned endpoint route while its task is nonterminal, returns 503 with `Retry-After: 5` when the old address fails or its registration is unavailable, and forwards through a replacement registration. Federated capability URLs carry the child's 503 to the caller. Request timeouts remain 504, and unknown endpoints remain 404.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
Marina cannot serve a named app publicly. An app with `name` in `applet.toml` (for example EvalDash, served at a host such as `evaldash.oa.dev`) is always behind Marina's authentication. `marina release --mode public` fails with "Named applications are private; public applets use the isolated applet origin" ([`applets.py:562`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/fb9ef1e6e9/infra/marina/src/marina/applets.py#L562-L563)). `marina apps mode UUID public` fails with "Named applications remain private" ([`applets.py:911`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/fb9ef1e6e9/infra/marina/src/marina/applets.py#L909-L915)). A bound named host also stays authenticated (`infra/marina/README.md`, "Named app hosts").

Today a public app must be unnamed. It is then served only at `https://public.applets.marina.oa.dev/a/<uuid>/`, and it loses the features that require a name: data URLs, scheduled jobs and agent panels. For example, the Snowball family tree (#10719) can stay public only as an unnamed app at a UUID URL.

Done when: a checked-in named app, deployed from `main`, can be released in public mode and served read-only without sign-in on its own hostname. Write routes, SQL, publication and MCP must stay private, as they are for public applets today.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
## Research

Named public release and mode changes are rejected in [`applets.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/fb9ef1e6e9c41159f047e69b455389a6739e6280/infra/marina/src/marina/applets.py#L558-L563) and [`set_mode`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/fb9ef1e6e9c41159f047e69b455389a6739e6280/infra/marina/src/marina/applets.py#L904-L920). The [public service](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/fb9ef1e6e9c41159f047e69b455389a6739e6280/infra/marina/src/marina/server.py#L244-L256) admits only `/a/*` GET/HEAD requests; [named routes](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/fb9ef1e6e9c41159f047e69b455389a6739e6280/infra/marina/src/marina/server.py#L1297-L1368) require authentication, and [Pulumi](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/fb9ef1e6e9c41159f047e69b455389a6739e6280/infra/marina/__main__.py#L377-L389) maps every configured named host to the authenticated service. PR #10829 uses an unnamed public applet and does not change these gates.

## Proposed Fix

1. Add an explicit public named-host inventory to Marina configuration and Pulumi. Map those hosts to the existing unauthenticated reader service; keep private named hosts on the IAP service. Resolve each public hostname through `applet_hosts` and return 404 for an unbound, archived, or private app, checking the current mode on every request.
2. Serve only the bound app's root, assets, `data/` files, and GET/HEAD backend routes on its public hostname, with anonymous identity. Preserve revision redirects and cache revalidation after host rebinds. Keep SQL, publication, mode changes, MCP, other Marina control routes, and mutating methods unavailable on the public service.
3. Remove the named/public rejection from release and mode changes once that route gate is in place. Report the bound public hostname in release and mode responses, falling back to the public UUID URL until a host is bound. Update the Marina README with the release, binding, and revocation steps.
4. Add regression tests for public named release and mode changes; anonymous page, asset, data, and API reads; 404s for private, archived, unbound, and cross-app host requests; and rejection of writes and control routes. Check the Pulumi domain mapping in preview before rollout. Review the app's GET handlers before publication because Marina cannot prove they have no side effects.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
TL;DR: With expert parallelism 4 and `capacity_factor` 1.0, the Levanter MoE ring dispatch (`ring_gather_combine`) drops 8-23% of expert assignments per layer on the Snowball model. It drops them silently, because overflow reporting is off. Padding tokens are dispatched with no validity mask, so they take capacity too. On the precision gate, the drops cut top-1 agreement with vLLM to 0.85-0.93 (limit 0.975). With capacity 4.0 the drops go to 0 and top-1 rises to 0.990-0.996. A dropless setting is added in draft PR [#10685](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10685); existing callers keep capacity 1.0.

Part of #10695.

Mechanism, from a [source review](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-r5-config-forward-diff-marten-md) of the run's pinned commit:

- The Snowball config sets capacity factor 1.0 with expert parallelism 4. The GPU default dispatch is `ring_gather_combine`. Overflow reporting is disabled.
- The ring gives each expert shard roughly one quarter of all assignments. It caps assignments per expert shard and drops the overflow (`grug/_moe/ep_ring.py:199-223`, prefix cap and drop at `:49-51`).
- Accepted assignments are sorted by expert id and flat position. So whether a token is dropped depends on the other tokens and rows in the batch.
- Snowball passes no `token_valid` mask to `expert_mlp` (`snowball.py:609-615`). Right-padding tokens are routed and dispatched like real tokens. The attention mask does not remove them from MoE dispatch.
- vLLM has no such capacity limit. It sends every selected assignment through FusedMoE. The Levanter training forward therefore differs from the served forward.

Observed:

- The [precision gate](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-lr0-r5-gate-reading-shoveler-md) compares Levanter log-probabilities with stored vLLM values. It ran on 4 hosts and failed 21 checks. Top-1 agreement was 0.860 (check), 0.851 (contrastive), 0.933 (long) and 0.933 (long past window). The limit is 0.975. p99 |Δ log-prob| was 2.06-3.79 nats (limit 0.70). Route set agreement with the torch reference was 0.415 over 805,974 position-layers.
- A [single-host diagnostic](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-diag-moe-drops-r2-reading-chukar-md) (one H100x8 node, data 2 × expert 4) ran three arms on the same gate inputs:

| arm | capacity factor | drops, all 26 layers | top-1 (check / contrastive / long / past window) | gate failures |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| expert 4 | 1.0 | 899,514 of 6,922,240 | 0.886 / 0.862 / 0.928 / 0.930 | 21 |
| expert 4 | 4.0 | 0 | 0.994 / 0.990 / 0.993 / 0.996 | 5 |
| expert 1 (local path) | 1.0 | 0 | 0.987 / 0.994 / 0.991 / 0.997 | 3 |

- Each layer has 266,240 assignments. Drops at capacity 1.0 range from 21,687 to 62,290 per layer. That is 8-23%.
- Without drops, p99 |Δ log-prob| falls from 2-4 nats to 0.45-0.65. Contrastive won/lost agreement goes from 62/64 to 64/64. Contrastive candidate-score p99 falls from 7.9 to 1.13-1.15.
- Against a torch reference, the first sublayer that departs from BF16 noise is the layer-0 MoE output: 69.1 BF16 steps at capacity 1.0 against 19.1 at capacity 4.0. All earlier ops match the dropless arm bit for bit. The error then grows: the layer-1 MoE output is 252.3 steps at capacity 1.0 and 13.6 at capacity 4.0.
- The drop counts are recomputed on the host from each arm's routes with the ring capacity rule, padding included. The GPU backend gave no count because `report_capacity_overflow=False`. A CPU test checks that the recompute matches the backend count (4 of 4 pass).
- The single-host arm at capacity 1.0 reproduces the 4-host gate numbers closely. The capacity drops are the main cause of the gate failure. The cross-host context axis adds little or nothing visible, but this run did not test that axis directly.

At capacity 4.0 a [second diagnostic job](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-diag-moe-fix-r1-reading-chukar-md) recorded 0 sender and 0 receiver drops on all 26 layers. A 16-update [SFT run](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-sft-m16-r3-reading-chukar-md) at batch 8 × 8192 on 4 slices, with capacity 4.0, recorded 0 drops summed over all updates, counters and layers.

Impact: any Snowball or other Grug MoE run that uses this ring dispatch with an expert axis and capacity factor 1.0 trains on a forward that drops expert assignments. The dropped set depends on batch composition and padding, and nothing is logged. We have measured this only on Snowball at expert parallelism 4. We have not measured how many of the drops come from padding tokens.

Expected: the expert-parallel forward matches the local path and vLLM. Padding takes no expert capacity. Any remaining overflow is counted and reported.

A dropless setting is added in draft PR [#10685](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10685); existing callers keep capacity 1.0.



Related: the identity SFT in #10491 trained V13 (released as v0.1.1) at expert capacity factor 1, and V19 at capacity 4. Draft PR #10492 makes the capacity factor configurable for that work.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

The current Snowball forward fixes expert capacity at 1.0 and passes neither a token-validity mask nor overflow reporting, so padding can consume capacity and valid routes can be dropped silently. Draft [#10685](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10685) adds a capacity setting and a masked, counted forward; [#10690](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10690) requires factor 4 for identity SFT, but the LR0 trainer in [#10693](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10693) still calls `compute_next_token_loss`, so its updates do not enforce the new counts.

**Relevant code**
- [`snowball.py#L534-L563`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4432377550/lib/levanter/src/levanter/models/snowball.py#L534-L563) — fixed capacity and unchecked dispatch.
- [`ep_ring.py#L61-L95`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4432377550/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ring.py#L61-L95) — shard capacity and clipping.
- [#10685](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10685) — masked forward and drop counters.

# Proposed Fix

Complete the existing PR stack, then use the checked Snowball loss in the actual SFT and LR0 trainer steps while preserving their current loss terms. Record sender and receiver drops each update and fail the run on any nonzero count; verify the padded expert-4 case and repeat the precision gate and short SFT check with zero drops. The default unchecked forward in #10685 retains capacity 1.0, so other Snowball and Grug callers need an explicit safety policy before this issue is resolved for all callers.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 Status after PR 10685 (merged 2026-11-10). The drops happen in Levanter's expert-parallel ring dispatch (`levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ring.py`). vLLM never drops.

**Fixed by PR 10685**
- `SnowballConfig.moe_capacity_factor` is a checked setting. It is kept when the HF config is loaded. Setting it to the expert-axis size (4 here) keeps every assignment.
- `activations_with_stats(token_valid=...)` skips padding and returns per-layer drop counts.

**Still open on main**
- The default is still `moe_capacity_factor = 1.0`, the setting that dropped 8–23% of assignments. No recipe on main sets a higher value; only tests do.
- The normal training forward passes no `token_valid` mask. Padding still uses capacity, and drops are still not reported.
- The recipes that would have used the dropless setting and the checked forward were not merged: PR 10690 (identity SFT, capacity 4) and PR 10693 (LR0 trainer) are both closed.

For RL and on-policy distillation, the trainer must match vLLM, so these runs should be dropless. Suggested close condition: Snowball post-training runs are dropless by default (or fail on any drop), and the training forward masks padding and logs drop counts.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
Mini840 and Micro210 (#10804) are 840-task and 210-task stratified random subsets of 21 of the 26 #10197 benchmarks, built so checkpoints can be screened cheaply between full evaluations. The datasets are model agnostic, but the only launcher that runs them is a Qwen-specific harness on an unmerged branch, and its documented path is a 21-task smoke run (one task per benchmark). Running any Marin checkpoint through the compact policy today means writing a new launcher. The full policy takes one YAML per model and one command per suite.

What exists:

- The runtime lives on branch `benfeuer/mini840-e2e-launch` (head `36ce62ec`). Draft #10817 was closed by its author on 2026-11-02 without a merge or a stated reason. `experiments/evaluation/mini_policy_runtime/` does not exist on `main`; the README tells users to clone commit `f1a9e964` to run anything.
- The launcher hard-codes the candidate. `profile.py:19-20` pins `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B` at one revision; `launch.py:57` fixes TP2 on two H100s, `launch.py:103` the `qwen3_coder` tool parser, `launch.py:109` `enable_thinking: True`, `launch.py:110` temperature 0.6 / top-p 0.95, and `launch.py:201` the Qwen tokenizer. `--model-uri` swaps the weight mirror only. The README says other models should "load the same TaskRolloutSpecs ... in a separate MarinSkyRL run", which means a new launcher per model family. None of the 39 model configs under `experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/model-configs/` is read. The committed Snowball configs there (for example `laion-snowball-67b-a2b-relay-sft-acont-step999.yaml`: GrugMoE, `hermes` parser, DP8 with expert parallel, 73,728-token cap, `skip_special_tokens: false`) cannot be expressed through this launcher without editing its source.
- One run is five manual stages: export four secrets from Secret Manager; run a CPU staging job (`stage_inputs`); run a CPU environment-preflight job that may build container images; print a launch plan, then resubmit with `--run`, which also co-hosts an 8×H100 MiniMax judge for OlympiadBench and BixBench unless `--judge-base-url` points at a running one; then run `audit_results`, which only checks that every rollout reached verification. The README then asks the operator to download native traces and inspect every tau3 (customer-service agent benchmark) attempt by hand, because a counterpart transport failure there returns a zero reward with no exception.
- Micro210 has no launch path. `stage_inputs.py:45` stages only the 21-task smoke slice and the full 1,626-rollout Mini cohort. The README says Micro is the first 210 Mini tasks and gives no command for it.
- Cluster and priority are fixed. `launch.py:209-216` targets `cw-rno2a` only; `launch.py:174` accepts `--priority batch|production` and not `interactive`, the priority non-release evals should run at.
- Results do not reach EvalDash. Rewards land as SkyRL eval dumps under `s3://marin-rno2a/marin/checkpoints/mini840-e2e/<version>/exports/dumped_evals/eval_only/`. Nothing in the runtime writes a `record.json` under `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/`, where full-policy records live and EvalDash reads them, so a Mini score cannot be viewed beside the same model's full-policy score.
- Mini scores have no stated relation to full-policy scores. The execution profile differs from #10197: 65,536-token context and 16,384 output tokens for every benchmark instead of per-benchmark settings, thinking always on, the Pi agent harness for all seven agentic benchmarks instead of each benchmark's original harness, and generated-choice TruthfulQA instead of likelihood MC2. #10804 says this profile "has not yet been prospectively compared with the full policy", and the 0.818 rank correlation reported there was measured with a ridge predictor that the datasets do not ship; raw Mini means have not been validated against anything. The only Mini run to date is the 21-rollout Qwen smoke. No model has a complete Mini840 or Micro210 score.

Impact: on 2026-11-04 nine candidate checkpoints (identity SFT for #10695, OPD and SFT arms for #9920 and #9984, SFT-shootout arms for #10213) needed a cheaper screen. The compact policy was not usable for them, so all nine went through the full 26-benchmark suite: 8 H100s per model for about 26 hours each, because the seven agentic benchmarks run serially per serve.

Done when:

- The runtime is on `main` with the pinned-vLLM launch-rejection tests from #10817.
- `launch.py` takes a campaign model-config YAML and derives tokenizer, chat-template thinking controls, tool parser, serving topology and sampling from it. A committed Snowball config runs the smoke slice end to end without code edits.
- One command stages, preflights and launches a named model on Mini840 or Micro210, with cluster and priority (including `interactive`) as flags and an optional existing judge endpoint.
- Each benchmark result is written as a `record.json` under `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/`, with the launcher's `--version` cohort label set to `mini840` or `micro210`, so EvalDash shows it next to the model's full-policy records.
- A prospective comparison on at least two checkpoints outside the #10804 study reports per-benchmark deltas and rank agreement between Mini840, Micro210 and the full policy, judged against the gates #10804 proposed (0.95 rank correlation, 95% decisive agreement), and is posted to #10804 or here.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

The current campaign launcher already accepts a `ModelConfig`, priority, optional hosted judge, and a record destination. The Mini runtime is a separate SkyRL path on unmerged branch `benfeuer/mini840-e2e-launch`; it pins Qwen serving and stages no Micro210 cohort. Open [#10844](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10844) and [#10845](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10845) extract reusable native Harbor/Pi behavior from closed [#10817](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10817), so the remaining work should build on them.

**Relevant code**
- [`cli.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/b3db2227da816626f3d992bb1baae14935340dc5/experiments/evaluation/cli.py#L147) — campaign launch options.
- [`model_config.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/b3db2227da816626f3d992bb1baae14935340dc5/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/model_config.py#L187) — candidate serving and generation schema.
- [`launch.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/36ce62ecb793ef31def1b87ea7847e643e08691e/experiments/evaluation/mini_policy_runtime/launch.py#L49) — fixed SkyRL topology and generator.
- [`stage_inputs.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/36ce62ecb793ef31def1b87ea7847e643e08691e/experiments/evaluation/mini_policy_runtime/stage_inputs.py#L22) — smoke and Mini staging only.
- [`records.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/b3db2227da816626f3d992bb1baae14935340dc5/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/records.py#L508) — EvalDash record contract.

# Design

Add `mini840` and `micro210` as compact suite selections in `experiments.evaluation.cli launch`, backed by an eval-only SkyRL executor. The campaign CLI will resolve the same model YAML used by full-policy runs, then stage the pinned cohort, preflight its native environments, submit the candidate and optional judge, audit rollouts, and publish records. SkyRL currently owns the candidate vLLM engine, so this executor needs a dedicated execution path under the campaign CLI; it cannot be passed an existing campaign `EvalExecutor` endpoint without changing SkyRL. Keep the frozen 65,536/16,384 context/output profile and Pi agent behavior explicit in the compact suite so its scores remain distinguishable from #10197.

Delivery sequence:

1. **Runtime base.** Reconcile #10844/#10845, then port the remaining Mini runtime from #10817 onto current `main`, including the pinned-vLLM launch-rejection regression. Retain the source revisions, repaired grading wheels, native environment policy, and sanitized trace audit. Do not duplicate behavior those PRs already land.
2. **General model and one-command launch.** Replace Qwen constants with a lowering from `ModelConfig`: checkpoint and tokenizer revisions, chat template and thinking arguments, parser, sampling, TP/PP/DP/expert parallelism, context cap, and GPU allocation. Reject unsupported combinations before allocating GPUs. Add a pinned Micro210 staging path (210 tasks, 450 expanded rollouts) alongside Mini840 (840 tasks, 1,626 rollouts); validate cohort identity and the complete environment manifest before submission. Route credentials through the existing Iris secret declarations. Expose cluster, priority (including `interactive`), and `--judge-base-url`; keep the existing hosted-judge option. A target invocation is `... cli launch --model-config <snowball.yaml> --evals mini840 --federated_cluster cw-rno2a --priority interactive --version mini840`, with `micro210` substituted for the smaller cohort.
3. **Records and visibility.** Convert verified SkyRL rollout outputs into one `EvalRunRecord` per benchmark under `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/<run_id>/record.json`. Record the model config/digest, cohort source revision, effective serving settings, judge, task coverage, raw mean reward, artifact path, and failed or partial status. Give compact records cohort-qualified eval names, a shared group ID, and `version=mini840` or `micro210`; confirm EvalDash ingests them next to the model's full-policy runs without treating the cohort label as policy conformance. Never count a Tau3 transport failure as a valid zero reward.
4. **Prospective validation.** Run a 21-task Snowball smoke, then complete both cohorts on at least four new checkpoints with existing full-policy records. Compare the same 21 benchmarks using raw per-benchmark means and equal benchmark weighting, reporting deltas, rank correlation, decisive agreement, and measured GPU-hours. Two checkpoints give a degenerate Spearman result, so use at least four even though the issue's minimum is two. Judge against #10804's 0.95 rank and 95% decisive-agreement gates; publish the run IDs and results here or on #10804. Full-policy release evaluation remains required until the gates pass.

## Testing

Unit tests should cover model-config lowering, frozen cohort selection and counts, manifest rejection before GPU submission, output-to-record conversion, partial/error classification, and record round-trips. Run the repository's default tests and pre-PR checks, then verify the Snowball smoke on Iris with all 21 rollouts and seven native verifier paths. The complete cohort runs are separate, costed validation work.

## Open question

Does eval-only SkyRL support the committed Snowball DP8/expert-parallel configuration without extending its role plan or vLLM argument forwarding? Resolve this with a dry-run topology check and the Snowball smoke before claiming support for arbitrary campaign models.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
One SWE-bench Verified trial in the 2026-11-04 eval campaign (model Contributor-Plain, trial `django__django-10880__Wspb9gU`) finished its agent phase at 22:51Z on Nov 4 and never reached verification. At 09:12Z on Nov 5 the stage still reported 499/500 completed and 1 running, with no terminal record. The campaign runs the seven Harbor benchmarks serially per model inside one group, so the six benchmarks queued behind SWE could not start. The group had to be stopped and the remaining six relaunched; the SWE score was reconstructed from the 499 per-trial `result.json` files.

Why nothing fired:

- Harbor's `Trial._await_phase` bounds `agent.run` only (agent 1800 s, verifier 300 s, agent setup 360 s, environment build 1800 s). The `finally` block that syncs agent output and the artifact work after it are outside every phase bound. The verifier timeout is not armed until verification starts.
- `trial_attempt` timeout resolves to null in the campaign's job and trial config, so there is no whole-trial deadline either.
- Stopping the trial's sandbox from outside (Daytona SDK stop, then 404 on get) did not unblock the driver: the stage still showed 499 at 09:12Z. Trial cancellation is not exposed; the trial is an async task inside the shared driver.

This is a different mechanism from #10608, where leftover Pi processes make the verifier time out. Here the verifier never starts and no timeout is armed.

Reproduce:
1. Launch a campaign Harbor group with the standard config (`experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/`, `launch-campaign.sh --harbor`).
2. Make one trial hang between agent completion and verification (for example, stall the sandbox during output sync).
3. Observe the stage never finalizes and the remaining benchmarks in the group never start.

Expected: every trial has a wall-clock deadline that covers the whole attempt, not only the agent phase. When it fires the trial is recorded as an infrastructure error, the stage finalizes with that trial missing, and the next benchmark in the group starts.

Evidence (sanitized, on the campaign host): `plain-swe-timeout-and-reconstruction-findings-r1.json` (sha256 7cd7c5d2…); native job config sha256 46ca2aaf…, trial config sha256 c09a9ce8….

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

The eight campaign Harbor policies leave `trial_attempt_timeout_sec` unset, so the admitted attempt has no deadline while output sync runs outside the agent phase. The vendored Harbor queue already selects and persists a `TrialTimeoutError` when this deadline expires, but the campaign allows ten retries of that error; adding only a deadline could repeat the stall eleven times.

**Relevant code**
- [`swebench-verified.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1ca7f3f4bdd37a8075aaf16a75908014c9be2798/experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/harbor-configs/swebench-verified.yaml#L1-L21) — missing deadline and retry policy
- [`queue.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1ca7f3f4bdd37a8075aaf16a75908014c9be2798/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/trial/queue.py#L325-L353) — admitted-attempt supervision
- [`common.sh`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1ca7f3f4bdd37a8075aaf16a75908014c9be2798/experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/common.sh#L447-L460) — campaign config checks

# Proposed Fix

Set a 5400-second attempt deadline in all eight campaign policies. The configured build, setup, agent, and verifier caps total 4260 seconds; 1140 seconds remain for output sync and cleanup. Remove `TrialTimeoutError` from the infrastructure retry allowlist so a timed-out attempt is recorded once, and make `validate-campaign.sh` reject policies missing either constraint. Verify that a stalled output sync yields a terminal trial result and lets the next serial benchmark start.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body: 🤖 PR #10963 sets a 5400-second deadline for each campaign Harbor attempt and removes `TrialTimeoutError` from the retry allowlist, so an expired attempt is recorded once. Campaign preflight and the focused Harbor tests pass. The broader local test run stopped because this sandbox's Python lacks `os.pidfd_open`; the original Daytona sync stall was not reproduced locally.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
On cw-rno2a at interactive priority, Kueue preempted the owned 8xH100 serve of a paired-maths screen three times in about an hour (2026-11-10 02:10–03:15 UTC). Each preemption failed the whole screen. Over the same window, a BFCL eval on the shared evaluation runner survived its own preemption. The difference is the harness, not the cluster.

The screen's driver submits its serve and its CPU evaluator jobs with `max_retries_preemption=0` and `max_retries_failure=0`: `experiments/post_training/identity_fullscreen_owner/owner.py` lines 82 (serve) and 225 (evaluators) on the branch `task/366-ws3-paired-math`. That is unpushed experiment code, not part of main. It overrides the `--max-retries-preemption` default of 10 in [`lib/marin/src/marin/inference/iris_cli.py:394`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f6c200af77/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/iris_cli.py#L394). The driver also talks to the serve's capability URL directly, so it does not use the broker recovery from #10169. A preemption before readiness raises `Owned serve terminated before readiness`. A preemption after readiness turns every in-flight trial request into HTTP 502, and the driver does not resume partial trials.

## Which eval paths tolerate preemption

| Path | Preemption behavior | Tracking |
|---|---|---|
| Harbor / Evalchemy on `marin.evaluation.runner`, brokered serving | Pauses, waits for the replacement serve, resumes from saved output. BFCL survived a preemption on 2026-11-10. | #10169 (merged) |
| Direct capability-URL clients | The proxy returns 502 while Iris replaces the serve task. | #10273, fix in #10721 (open) |
| SkyRL eval-only runs | A kill before the last rollout writes no results. | #10837, fix in #10840 (open) |
| Iris retry after a sealed Evalchemy record | The retry can overwrite the sealed record. | #9972 |
| Eval driver pod itself evicted (Harbor groups, 2026-11-06 00:17 UTC, 106.0 H100-h; Echo incident record https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/961, Marina login required) | The group is lost; the serve recovery does not cover the driver. | none |
| Custom drivers that own a serve with preemption retries set to 0 (this report) | The first preemption is fatal. Partial trials are lost. | none |

## Reproduction

1. Run an experiment driver that submits a vLLM serve through `marin.inference.iris_cli` and overrides `max_retries_preemption=0`, then runs CPU evaluator jobs against the serve's capability URL.
2. Run it at interactive priority on cw-rno2a while higher-priority GPU work is queued.
3. Kueue evicts the serve pod (`WorkloadEvictedDueToPreempted`).
4. Before readiness, the driver raises `Owned serve terminated before readiness`. After readiness, the trials see HTTP 502 `upstream endpoint request failed` until their retries run out, and the root job fails with `Full screen has incomplete command coverage; available outputs retained`.

## Expected behavior

A preempted serve is replaced, and the eval resumes or reruns only the unfinished trials, as the brokered runner already does. A driver that needs a fixed serve attempt for provenance should record the attempt id instead of disabling preemption retries.

## Evidence (cw-rno2a, interactive band, 2026-11-10 UTC)

| Root job | Serve preempted | Outcome | H100-h |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/karan/pathb-paired-math-t334-proj-ct-r1-r1` | during vLLM engine init, before readiness | root FAILED 02:12:36 after 1m49s | 0.166 |
| `/karan/pathb-paired-math-t334-proj-ct-r1-r2` | 2m15s on node, before readiness | root failed after 20m06s | 0.301 |
| `/karan/pathb-paired-math-t334-soup3-r1` | 7m10s in, after readiness | all three trials failed on 502 | 0.957 |
| `/karan/eval-t334-proj-ct-r1-bfcl-run-01-8eccd44c` (control, brokered runner) | GPU attempt preempted at 27.8 s | replacement attempt started, run continued | — |

All three serve children report `WorkloadEvictedDueToPreempted: Preempted to accommodate a workload`. Retries were 0/0 on every failed serve.

## Time wasted

These numbers come from our preemption record for this campaign. They count every preempted attempt in our run ledgers, not just the three screens above.

**Allocation exposure, not proven irrecoverable work.** GPU-h lost below is requested GPUs × native physical attempt duration. It is not proof that all work/results were lost; partial outputs/checkpoints may survive. Actual wasted-work total and result-loss flags remain UNKNOWN without application-result evidence.

Known H100 allocation-exposure subtotal: **44464309/75000 = 592.857453333 H100-h**; 6 affected GPU windows have UNKNOWN bounds. Scope coverage is incomplete: 288 roots were absent from the hub; 32 have no recoverable native attempt archive. Never treat these as zero.

Known H100 exposure by original host-root priority band:
- UNKNOWN: 738347/28125 = 26.252337778 H100-h
- PRIORITY_BAND_PRODUCTION: 69253/11250 = 6.155822222 H100-h
- PRIORITY_BAND_INTERACTIVE: 42033697/75000 = 560.449293333 H100-h

Known H100 exposure by harness pattern (training/export kept separate):
- Harbor group: 1441913/2500 = 576.765200000 H100-h
- training/export/other (separate from eval patterns): 757717/450000 = 1.683815556 H100-h
- owned-serve driver: 46157/28125 = 1.641137778 H100-h
- broker+workers: 127673/10000 = 12.767300000 H100-h

2026-11-06 00:17Z five-group Harbor incident: **47718767/450000 = 106.041704444 H100-h**. This is a tagged subset of the overall total, not an additional charge. CPU root preemptions and killed GPU descendants are linked; CPU trigger rows contribute 0 GPU-h.

Ten largest rows by GPU-h:

| Job root | Cluster | Band | Diagnostic | GPU-h (allocation proxy) |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| `/karan/eval-20261105-094057-open-athena-Snowball-67B-A2B-SFT-Shootout-Contributor-Plain-v0.1-2026.10.22-a93c7339c5c24329ad01883ab6470d16-e342989c` | cw-rno2a | PRIORITY_BAND_INTERACTIVE | Parent job terminated; native parent-preemption teardown | 150.930528889 |

| `/karan/eval-20261105-223905-open-athena-Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A3-2026.10.30-10460a5f620146f8a5963b2ca8c62856-ab71bc7d` | cw-rno2a | PRIORITY_BAND_INTERACTIVE | Parent job terminated; native parent-preemption teardown | 13.001195556 |
| `/karan/eval-20261105-230644-open-athena-Snowball-67B-A2B-MixedRS-SFT-Step727-5184af10c09c40028fda5cf72b58c531-aa6a2a41` | cw-rno2a | PRIORITY_BAND_INTERACTIVE | Parent job terminated; native parent-preemption teardown | 9.287055556 |

Full record (93 rows): `/mnt/storage/karan-scratchpad/task-334/preemption-record-r1/preemptions.md`, sha256 `668d8e86de9e…`. Machine-readable copy: `preemptions.json` (sha256 `06ce208a7f91…`); manifest `sha256-manifest.json` (sha256 `88af65dc5033…`). These paths are on a team host, not public.

## Proposed fix

- Move the paired-maths screen onto `marin.evaluation.runner` with brokered serving, or keep Iris's default preemption retries on the owned serve and re-resolve the endpoint after a replacement.
- Make trials resumable: skip trials that already have a sealed result, and rerun only unfinished ones.
- For any driver that keeps preemption retries at 0, request `production` priority per launch with owner sign-off, or document that preemption is fatal.

🤖
# Research

The paired-maths driver sets preemption retries to zero for its serve and CPU evaluators, then sends trials to the serve's capability URL. A serve eviction is therefore terminal for that driver, and unfinished trials have no replay point. The driver is absent from `main`, and `task/366-ws3-paired-math` is not published on GitHub; the shared evaluation runner already has broker and evaluator-attempt recovery from #10169. Open PR #10721 addresses the direct proxy's 502 response during replacement, but does not make this driver's trials resumable.

**Relevant code**
- [`iris_cli.py#L394`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f6c200af77357342016df8f8a559b1503f571ddc/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/iris_cli.py#L394) — default 10 preemption retries.
- [`runner.py#L114-L145`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f6c200af77357342016df8f8a559b1503f571ddc/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/runner.py#L114-L145) — wait and retry evaluator attempts.
- [`runner.py#L399-L434`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f6c200af77357342016df8f8a559b1503f571ddc/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/runner.py#L399-L434) — retry in the same output directory.
- [`serving_config.py#L267-L288`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f6c200af77357342016df8f8a559b1503f571ddc/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/serving_config.py#L267-L288) — broker for single-task eval serving.

# Proposed Fix

1. Publish the paired-maths driver and its trial output contract. Port it to the shared evaluation runner's `EvalExecutor`/broker path, and retain a nonzero serve preemption retry budget. Keep #10721 scoped to proxy responses.
2. Give each trial a stable identity covering the model, command, scoring configuration, and seed. Write a validated result durably before marking the trial complete; on an evaluator or owner restart, load completed trials and run only missing ones. Apply a nonzero preemption retry budget to the CPU jobs after this replay path exists.
3. Exercise serve eviction before readiness, serve eviction with requests in flight, and CPU evaluator eviction. Each case should finish the same trial set without duplicate scoring or lost completed results. Check that a retry cannot replace a sealed successful record, the failure tracked in #9972, before enabling parent-job retries.

This needs the unpublished driver and a replay contract, so it is larger than a safe isolated fix in the current checkout. No PR for the owner driver is open.

comments.body:
🤖 Closing. The cause was in the reporting driver, not in Iris or the shared eval runner. The paired-maths driver on the unpushed branch `task/366-ws3-paired-math` set `max_retries_preemption=0` on its serve and evaluator jobs. That told Iris not to replace the serve, so the first Kueue eviction was fatal. The Iris default is 10.

Guidance for eval drivers that own a serve:
- Use `marin.evaluation.runner` with brokered serving. It waits for the replacement serve and resumes from saved output (PR 10169).
- Otherwise keep the default preemption retries. To pin a serve attempt for provenance, record the attempt id instead of disabling retries.

Related work, tracked elsewhere:
- PR 10721 (open): retryable 503 instead of 502 for direct capability-URL clients while a serve is replaced.
- PR 10840 / issue 10837: partial SkyRL eval results.
- Issue 9972: retries overwriting sealed records.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
The SWE-smith Harbor task packages in `DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s` (and the same layout in `mlfoundations-dev/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests`) leave the repository's full git history in the agent's container. The image built from `environment/Dockerfile` keeps a local `main` branch with the unbroken code and about 944 other branches, so the agent can print the fix with `git diff HEAD main -- <package>` or `git show main:<file>`. `/tests` and `/solution` are correctly absent from the image.

Reproduce: build `swesmith-00003`'s `environment/Dockerfile` from the package, run it with no network, then `git log --oneline` (three commits: Initial commit, Bug Patch, Remove F2P Tests), `git branch -a` (944 branches including `main`), `git diff HEAD main -- oauthlib` (the exact fix).

Impact on existing data: in `open-athena/Kimi-2.5-swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s-maxeps-32k`, 860 of 5,237 passing trials (16.4%) and 433 of 4,119 failing trials run history-reading commands (`git show main:<path>`, diffs against `main` or `HEAD~N`, checkout or restore from history, `git log -p`). Some are benign (a diff against `HEAD~1` shows only the removed tests); many copy the original file. So the reported pass rate on these packages is inflated, and trace sets built on them carry shortcut solutions: the Kimi set above, the `GLM-4.7` and AgentTrove swesmith streams, and the allkimi relay data (`laion/calibforge-relay-traces`, `kimi_swesmith` rows) that was DARE-grafted into Snowball v0 (`open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Merge-Campaign3-DARE-Linear-02-2026.10.12`). SWE-bench Verified is not affected: there the fix is not in the repository's past.

A plain squash is not enough, because `tests/test.sh` itself uses history (`git checkout <task branch>; git checkout HEAD~1`) to restore the removed fail-to-pass tests before running pytest.

Expected: during the agent phase the repository has one commit, no other branches, no remote and no reflog; the verifier restores the fail-to-pass tests from outside the agent's view (for example, ship the test files in `tests/` and copy them in, or keep a git bundle that only the verifier unpacks). For each task, the gold patch still passes, the unpatched repository still fails, and the history-reading commands above return nothing.

Done when: a fixed package build exists with that validation on a sample of tasks, existing SWE-smith pass rates and training sets built on the leaky packages are re-reported with history-reading trials removed or flagged, and the shootout pool in #10213 uses the fixed packages.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

The reported `swesmith-00003` image retains the pre-bug `main` branch and earlier commits, so an agent can recover the fix from Git history. Removing old refs alone is insufficient if the object database still contains the clean tree; the current verifier also uses `HEAD~1` to recover fail-to-pass tests. The reported 860/5,237 passing and 433/4,119 failing history-reading trials are contamination candidates, not yet an audited count of trials that copied the fix. Marin consumes these external packages and traces, while the package builder is outside this checkout.

**Relevant code and artifacts**
- [DCAgent package release](https://huggingface.co/datasets/DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s) — affected task source.
- [Shootout #10213](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10213) — waits for stripped packages.
- [AgentTrove ingestion](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/agenttrove.py#L17) — SWE-smith trace consumer.
- [Relay source PR #10027](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10027) — registers Kimi SWE-smith rows.

# Proposal

## Outcome

Publish an immutable, revision-pinned Harbor package release whose agent image contains the bugged working tree in one new Git repository with one commit, one task branch, no `main`/remote/tags/reflog, and no recoverable old objects. Keep the fail-to-pass test payload in Harbor's verifier-only `tests/` area and copy it into the repository when scoring. Record the old and new package revisions and per-task content digests; do not overwrite the release used by existing trials.

## Plan

1. Change the package producer to create a fresh `.git` after applying each bug patch, rather than squashing the existing repository in place. Export required test files from the source package into verifier-only storage before discarding history. Make `tests/test.sh` restore those files without `git checkout` or `HEAD~1`; keep `solution/` and `tests/` out of the agent container.
2. Validate a stratified sample across repositories and test layouts in offline Harbor runs. In each agent image, require one reachable commit and no old refs, remotes, reflogs, or dangling objects containing the clean fix. Exercise `git show main:<file>`, `git diff HEAD main -- <package>`, `git show HEAD~1`, `git log -p`, and `git fsck --unreachable`; none may reveal the clean file. For each sampled task, the untouched bugged tree must score 0 and the gold patch must score 1 under the revised verifier. Publish task IDs, package digests, commands, and results with the new release.
3. Audit the Kimi, GLM-4.7, AgentTrove, and allkimi relay/Snowball v0 provenance at trial or row level. Classify history commands as benign inspection, fix recovery, or unresolved; report raw and unflagged success rates with denominators, plus counts by outcome and category. Publish flagged row IDs or a reproducible manifest and clean-filtered trace revisions where the source can be republished. Annotate existing model and dataset results; filtering rows cannot undo training already performed on Snowball v0.
4. Pin the fixed package revision in the #10213 SWE-smith pool and block the eight-attempt generation until the package validation passes. Keep the already stated pilot-trace history filter separate from the new pool validation. Coordinate Harbor release acquisition with [#10198](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10198); its cache work does not repair the package contents.

## Risks and open questions

The package producer and release permissions are external to this repository, so the new dataset revision needs an owner with access to that build pipeline. The verifier payload must be checked against every sampled task's required test files; a one-commit image can still give false rewards if a file is omitted. Excluding all history-reading trials gives a conservative subset, not an unbiased replacement for a fresh evaluation on fixed packages.

comments.body:
🤖 Fixed SWE-smith packages for the #10213 pool, with validation on 20 tasks. The same class of leak is also present in TMax.

**Fixed packages.** `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/sft-shootout/pool/swesmith-packages.parquet` (sha256 `f004b109edf8aa9274693c07e01266d14469ec8c61fe695cc516aa1175117407`), 2,100 tasks. The schema is the same as the DCAgent parquet (`path`, `task_binary`), and the folder names are unchanged. The source is `DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s@78b0d879`. The upstream dataset is not modified. Code: [`experiments/post_training/sft_shootout_pool/`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/3bc613878c/experiments/post_training/sft_shootout_pool) on branch `task/206`.

- `environment/Dockerfile`: after the upstream `git fetch && git checkout <instance>`, the same `RUN` replaces the repository: `rm -rf .git && git init && git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main && git add -A && git commit -m "Initial commit" && git reflog expire --expire=now --all && git gc --prune=now`. This is a new `.git`, not a squash, so no old objects remain in the container's filesystem. The base image's lower layers still hold the old `.git`, but the container cannot read them.
- `tests/f2p_restore/`: the files that the upstream `git checkout HEAD~1` would change, at their parent contents, plus `deleted.txt`. They are computed from a bare clone of `github.com/swesmith/<repo>`. On `swesmith-00003` they match the image's own `git show HEAD~1:<path>` byte for byte.
- `tests/test.sh`: `git checkout <instance>; git checkout HEAD~1;` is replaced by `cp -a /tests/f2p_restore/files/. /testbed/` plus the deletions. The rest is unchanged. Harbor uploads `tests/` only to the verifier (checked in harbor 0.24.0 `verifier/verifier.py`; only `agents/oracle.py` uploads `solution/`).

**Validation** on 20 pool tasks, one from each of 20 repos, in local Docker following Harbor's phase order:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Agent-phase repository: 1 commit, 1 branch, 0 remotes, empty reflog, no `HEAD~1`/`main~1`/`origin/main`/`master` | 20/20 |
| Gold patch (`solution/solve.sh`) then `tests/test.sh`: reward 1 | 20/20 |
| Unpatched tree: reward 0 | 19/20 |
| Leak commands (`git log --all -p`, `git show HEAD~1`, `git diff HEAD main`, `git diff HEAD~1`, `git fsck --unreachable --lost-found`, `git stash list -p`, `git show main:<every file>`) print a clean-only line | 0/20 (upstream `swesmith-00003` control: 2/2) |

- `swesmith-01094` (`ariga/atlas`) also scores 1 unpatched with the unmodified upstream package, so its verifier does not detect the bug. This is an upstream defect, and it means DCAgent's "oracle verified" does not imply that an unpatched run fails.
- "Clean-only line": a source line the Bug Patch removed that occurs nowhere in the bugged tree. 7 of the 20 tasks have none, so only the ref checks apply to them.
- The filesystem search found no git leak. It did find copies of clean lines in installed packages: `setuptools/_vendor/typeguard` is an older vendored typeguard, which is relevant for `agronholm/typeguard` tasks (57 in the pool). The `_pytest` (iniconfig) and `rapidfuzz` (thefuzz) hits are probably coincidental.
- Residual: `github.com/swesmith/<repo>` is public and keeps every instance branch, so an agent with internet access can still fetch the fix. In the Kimi traces this happened once (`git fetch origin; git show origin/main:<file>`).

Per-task results: `pool/swesmith-validation-20.jsonl` and `pool/swesmith-leak-probe-20.jsonl`.

**TMax: same class of leak, different mechanism.** In `allenai/TMax-SFT-16.5K@848e2182` `tasks.zip`, 221 of 2,200 environments build verifier assets into the agent's image (for example `/opt/oracle/<reference program>`, `/app/verifier/ground_truth_valid_events.txt`, `/home/user/oracle.py`), and `test_final_state.py` reads them. In 181 of the 221, the instruction never names the path. In the #202 Qwen3.6-27B success traces (`allenai/tmax-sft`), 63 trajectories across 18 tasks name one of these hidden paths in a bash command. That is a heuristic: naming a path doesn't prove the answer was copied. The pool excludes the 181 (`excluded.jsonl`, `leak_risk=hidden_verifier_assets`) and keeps the 40 visible ones. TMax's Harbor converter (`hamishivi/tmax@6d3d606c`) does not copy `task.json` (including its `truth` field), `solutions/`, `setup.sh` or `test_initial_state.py`; `test_final_state.py` goes only to `tests/`.

**Effect on #202's pilot training set:** 860 Kimi history-reading passes and those 63 TMax trajectories were removed before training (manifest `selection.swesmith_git_history_rule` and `selection.tmax_hidden_asset_rule`).

🤖 The public `github.com/swesmith` mirrors are now unreachable while the agent runs, and a second leak was found in mini-swe-agent's own install.

**TL;DR**
- During the agent phase, the sandbox can reach only the model proxy. github.com, PyPI, apt and every other host fail DNS, and direct-IP HTTPS (GitHub 140.82.112.3, 140.82.114.4; 1.1.1.1) has its TLS handshake cut. Setup and the verifier keep full network.
- mini-swe-agent 2.1.0 installs a tool env that the agent can read. It holds clean copies of three pool repos: pygments, pandas, tenacity. GLM read `tenacity/retry.py` from it and called it "the reference". The conda base in the images also holds boltons 23.0.0. All four repos (469 tasks) are excluded from pool P.

**Why not a whole-trial block:** Harbor sets the Daytona network policy once per sandbox. Both the mini-swe-agent install and the SWE-smith verifier (`tests/test.sh`) download uv from github.com releases (`astral.sh/uv/0.7.13/install.sh`), so a whole-trial allow-list without github.com breaks them.

**Mechanism** ([`harbor_agents/trial_agents.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1555295d4d5a233e1bb854c814b927c21889574c/experiments/post_training/sft_shootout/harbor_agents/trial_agents.py), `AgentPhaseNetwork`, branch `task/207` @ `1555295d`): just before the agent's run, the live sandbox is switched to `domain_allow_list=iris.oa.dev` (the proxy host). The run starts once that host resolves, and the task's own policy is restored before the verifier. Each trial writes the applied policy to `agent/agent_network.json`, and the run's `driver_config.json` records it under `agent_network`.

**Measured** (null agent on swesmith-00008, -00698, -00763; HTTPS HEAD from inside the sandbox):

| Target | Before | Agent phase | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| `https://github.com/swesmith` | 200 | DNS failure | 200 |
| `api.github.com`, `raw.githubusercontent.com`, `codeload.github.com` | 200 | DNS failure | 200 |
| `https://140.82.112.3/`, `https://140.82.114.4/` (GitHub by IP) | 200 | TLS handshake cut | 200 |
| `https://1.1.1.1/` | 403 | TLS handshake cut | 403 |
| `pypi.org`, `deb.debian.org`, `archive.ubuntu.com`, `www.google.com` | 200 | DNS failure | 200 |

On these unchanged trees the verifier completed afterwards and scored 0, as expected. With GLM (`swe-net2`), 3/3 trials passed under the limit, and all 76 proxy calls returned 200. In one trial GLM ran `pip install pytest ...` and saw `No internet`.

**Tool-env leak:** in `swe-net2/swesmith-00763` (jd/tenacity), GLM ran `sed -n '136,175p' /root/.local/share/uv/tools/mini-swe-agent/lib/python3.12/site-packages/tenacity/retry.py`. A probe ran mini-swe-agent's real setup on one task from each of the 36 repos (`toolenv2`). It found the same 80 distributions on every image. Only three of them are pool repos: pygments (222 tasks), pandas (196) and tenacity (30). Every conda-based image also ships conda's own `boltons-23.0.0` under `/opt/miniconda3/pkgs`, including the mahmoud/boltons image (21 tasks). The install is now pinned (`mini-swe-agent-2.1.0-constraints.txt`, sha256 `c67d1ee2…`, Python 3.12), so this set cannot drift between the pilot and the full run. SWE-smith ingestion also drops any trace whose commands or outputs touch `/root/.local/share/uv/tools/`.

**Run folders** (`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/sft-shootout/generation/dryrun/`):
- `netprobe2`, `netprobe3`, `netprobe4`: network probes; `agent/network_probe.json` per trial.

comments.body:
Data point for Open-SWE, which is in the 10-05 SFT mix but not in the list above. I checked the successful traces (`resolved == 1`) of the two pinned Qwen3.8-27B mini-swe-agent partitions of `nvidia/Open-SWE-Traces` (revision `f967cba3`, 49,925 traces) for lines of the fix that show up in command output before the agent writes them.

**Rule.** A trace is flagged when at least 3 lines added by the reference patch (30+ characters, not imports or comments, not in the removed lines or the prompt) first appear in the output of a command that reads git history (`git log/show/diff`), `site-packages`, `node_modules`, `build/`, `dist/` or `.egg-info`, or the network (`curl`, `wget`, `pip download`, URLs), before the agent writes them. I then read 5 flagged traces per channel.

| Channel | Flagged | Read | Confirmed leak |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| git history | 153 | 5 | 0 |
| `site-packages` | 104 | 5 | 3 |
| `node_modules` | 83 | 5 | 0 |
| other (`build/lib`, network, …) | 29 | 5 | 1 |

- **Git history:** no case like the SWE-smith one. The git hits I read were the agent's own checkout or edits, or an older commit unrelated to the fix.
- **A newer release of the task's own package is installed in the image.** This is a different path from the mini-swe-agent tool env above: the system `site-packages` (`/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages`) holds a newer release of the package being fixed, and that release already contains the fix. For example, the task repo is `mkdocs-include-markdown-plugin` `2.8.0` while `3.4.1` is installed; the other two are `pytest-snapshot` `0.6.3` and `trie` `1.4.0` (which already has the `get_proof` the task asks for). The fourth case is a stale `build/lib/` copy inside the repo (oauthenticator). In all four, the agent found the copy (for example, diffed it against `/testbed`) and said it would not copy it; I did not check whether it used it anyway.
- **Size:** scaling each channel's hit rate up to its flagged count gives roughly 45–135 real cases among the 369 flagged traces, about 0.1–0.3% of the 49,925. Traces the rule did not flag were not checked.
- Newer revisions of the same dataset, not in the pin, also had network access during generation: in revision `9b4efcda`, 3 traces fetch the task's own upstream repository.

Examples and context: https://claude.ai/artifact/9vD2VkqXVPq5xNBA7Z1afp (section A3). Happy to share the IDs of the 369 flagged traces with their channel labels.

issues.author: ClassicLarry
issues.body:
Issue is to describe the Hero Run scaling ladder, config, and track its performance.

Tracking: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/reports/535B-A23B-18T-Token-Hero-Run-Scaling-Ladder--VmlldzoxNzc2MDM5Ng

Details on the full model spec is in the comment below.

### Why run a scaling ladder?

1. This lets us project the model performance and compare it to the scaling projections of our prior recipes. If our projection looks meaningfully worse, then we know we need to go back to the drawing board on some aspect of the model or data. This step can catch a lot of bugs!
2. We can look at how training dynamics change as we scale, in particular the gradient norms and token dropping. In our last run, the scaling ladder caught gradient norm growth to over 4 as we scaled out token horizon, which caused us to find a fix with logit z loss. Later ablations showed that without this fix, runs under certain conditions like high batch size would completely blow up mid-run.
3. We can project our evals across the entire trajectory of the run. This means that across the entire ~100 day run, we know exactly how we are doing compared to the projection. If at any point we fail to match the projection, it can prompt early investigation into training dynamics.
4. If something strange start to happen in the Hero run, we can reference the smaller scales runs to see if its actually normal. For instance, in prior scaling ladders we saw the grad norm grow heavily up to 40% of the run, then decrease as the LR decays. When we saw this on the hero run, having the small scale reference gave us confidence we didn't need to intervene, as long as the gradient followed the same pattern (steady growth for 40% of run).
5. It only costs 1% of total compute.
### What is our EP hardware implementation?
Described in detail here: https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/rav/moe-fixed-wave-a2a-384/2026.08.17/index.html.
We are hand-rolling our own EP implementation, props to @ravwojdyla, since we have not found a more performant variant on JAX XLA on GPU. 

### What is our long context extension plan?
Our last run was 8k seqlen pretrain, followed by 65k extension for 1T tokens, followed by 262k extension (to occur end of Aug). Prior to that run we have used 4k seqlen pretrain. For this run we are going back to 4k seqlen pretrain to start, to enable better expert balancing (twice as many sequences per batch). We wanted to minimize risk here because our EP token dropping implementation is more experimental. (our last run was dropless FSDP). Prior tests showed token dropping grow from ~7% to ~40% when extending from 4k to 65k seqlen. Our new pooled/wave EP drops about half as many tokens (3%) at 4k seqlen; however the token dropping is likely still excessively high at 65k seqlen.

We will spend 1-2 days to do an early cooldown at roughly 10-20 days into the run, to enable RL experiments, which will be our first full scale data point at how longer context influences dropping. A nice property of this test is that the cooldown will not contaminate or impact the main run, so we have some flexibility to collect data on how an extension approach impacts dropping. Our options will be:
1. If we have landed a Jax Mixture of Kittens or dropless ragged all-to-all, then we can swap to that for the cooldown. Prior small scale tests showed the model was robust from swapping from small amounts of dropping (5%) to dropless mid-run.
2. Otherwise, we can increase our capacity factor, and accept some amount of dropping.
3. If we find that neither of these options are suitable, the next option would be to introduce sequence level balancing mid-run (though forcing the experts to re-specialize mid-run will likely be worse than accepting some amount of dropping). 

Extending context will involve updating qk_mult according to mscale=X⋅ln(new_seqlen/old_seqlen)+1, testing coefficients near 0.1 (can quickly eval a range during extension on 1 rack). If the data from the first cooldown looks smooth, will plan on 4k->8k at 50 pct into run, then 8k->65k at about 95 pct, then a targeted 262k phase near end, based on data we collect from taking the 67B-A2B from 65k to 262k.

Have further derisked token dropping by staying at 2 shared experts, each at half width. 8 active experts are also at half width. However due to latent MoE 2x compression on active experts, we are effectively running at hidden_dim width neurons shared, and 2x hidden_dim neurons routed. Having 1/3 of our neurons come from shared expert will provide a stronger backbone in the event of high dropping. We see learning still progress with zero loss spikes even at 40 pct dropping.

### What if we see delays, beyond our buffer (hardware failure, MFU degradation)?
Up to roughly 25% of the token budget, the default approach will be to compensate by decreasing the token horizon of the run. Since we are using linear LR decay, we would update the decay rate to still reach 0.05 peak at whatever the new horizon point is, and update the datamix.
