spillover_issues.author: chrismc91
spillover_issues.body:
🤖 Curated Python code evaluations fail every attempt during grading with `Grading environment setup failed: exit=1`. The model's responses are fine, but no sample is scored. This affects HumanEval+, MBPP+ and CRUXEval on current main.

The code graders declare `python3 /tests/prepare.py` as an environment setup command ([`convert_python`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/code.py)). `prepare.py` reads the candidate's answer from `/app/answer.txt` to build the test program. [`_grade_on`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/runtime/grading.py) runs setup commands before it installs the submission archive that contains `/app/answer.txt`, so `prepare.py` fails:

```
File "/tests/prepare.py", line 15, in main
    response = Path("/app/answer.txt").read_text()
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/app/answer.txt'
```

Reproduce:
1. Run a curated `cruxeval`, `humanevalplus` or `mbppplus` evaluation from main.
2. Read `data/evaluation_attempts` in the run's results. Every finished attempt has `outcome = infra_error`, and its result blob carries the traceback above in `grade.diagnostics.stderr`.

Expected: the code graders can read the candidate's answer, either because the answer is installed before `prepare.py` runs or because preparation runs after the submission is installed.

Observed in CRUXEval run `20261113-192007-Qwen-Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-2c59e4d3702e48eab27ff3b1ddbe5c60-cruxeval-dda752051d0a55b3a9b6706ffcd6a9fe`, where every attempt on all 20 smoke items failed this way. HumanEval+ and MBPP+ use the same setup command; I have not run them yet.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

`convert_python` puts `prepare.py` in environment setup, but `_grade_on` installs the answer archive after setup. The runtime order is intentional: a candidate file must be able to replace a setup fixture. PR #10115 changes grading failure classification in the same runtime file but does not address this recipe.

**Relevant code**
- [`code.py#L103-L130`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/code.py#L103-L130) — Python grader recipe.
- [`grading.py#L621-L650`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/runtime/grading.py#L621-L650) — setup precedes answer installation.
- [`test_runtime.py#L911-L930`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/taskcompendium/tests/test_runtime.py#L911-L930) — setup fixture replacement contract.

# Proposed Fix

Run `prepare.py` immediately before `program.py` in the Python grader command, after the answer archive is installed. Advance the code recipe revision and check the published grader recipe in a regression test.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body: 🤖 Fix proposed in #11408. It runs Python code preparation after answer staging and advances CODE_REVISION. Eight focused TaskCompendium tests pass; the affected runner's Harbor `os.pidfd_open` failure reproduces on unmodified main. The live evaluation suites have not been rerun.

comments.author: penfever
comments.body: 🤖 Fresh production evidence from the Atlas difficulty v17 rounds (2026-11-17): the four Evalchemy code graders (cruxeval, humaneval, humanevalplus, mbppplus) burned 600+ infrastructure attempts each — every attempt, valid submission or not, because `python3 /tests/prepare.py` runs as a setup command (`importers/evalchemy/code.py` line 113) and the submission archive (which carries `/app/answer.txt`) installs only after setup (`runtime/grading.py::_grade_on`). Repro: grade any of these sources with the small-solver campaign; the grading environment setup fails with `FileNotFoundError: /app/answer.txt` inside the rebuilt task-curation env image. Fix landed on `atlas-env-audit` as 1ecadd3fdb ('Stage script-grader submissions before setup commands run'): for script graders with an answer path the submission archive installs before setup too; the post-setup install still runs, preserving replace-afterward semantics for setups that write fixtures at the answer path. Behavioral tests in `lib/taskcompendium/tests/test_script_grader.py`.

## 2. Trace-Backed Failure Analysis

### 2.1 `mrcr-65k` (26.49%, n=901; all 901 classified, 15 read directly)

Mochi prepends the exact requested 10-character random string on **806/901 (89.46%)** of prompts, and **186/901 (20.6%)** score `> 0.9` on MRCR's graded string-similarity metric. Mean `mrcr_accuracy` declines with needle count and across the four length buckets below 40k (`n_chars // 4`); the single 40k+ item scored 80.78%:

| Slice | n | Mean `mrcr_accuracy` |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2 needles | 299 | 36.29% |
| 4 needles | 302 | 28.71% |
| 8 needles | 300 | **14.47%** (graded string similarity) |
| 0–10k (`n_chars // 4`) | 325 | 31.68% |
| 10–20k (`n_chars // 4`) | 283 | 27.15% |
| 20–30k (`n_chars // 4`) | 159 | 20.05% |
| 30–40k (`n_chars // 4`) | 133 | 19.66% |
| 40k+ (`n_chars // 4`) | 1 | 80.78% |

Across the **620** items that hit the exact random prefix with `score <= 0.9`:
- **423 / 620 (68.2%)** matched another same-topic occurrence by a 60-character substring heuristic, with **331** matched occurrences later than the requested one and **92** earlier (measured direction; not opportunity-normalized). Under literal stripped-output equality with the same topic heuristic, **323 / 620 (52.1%)** matched another same-topic occurrence (**275** later, **48** earlier).
- **26 / 620 (4.2%)** matched a different-topic assistant turn under the 60-character substring heuristic.
- **171 / 620 (27.6%)** had no classified alternative-turn match under this heuristic (this residual count does not separate paraphrases from partial or truncated outputs).
- The remaining **95 / 901 (10.5%)** failed the exact-prefix check (`score = 0`).

### 2.2 `ifbench` (26.00% strict / 32.33% loose prompt; 27.91% strict / 34.88% loose instruction; all 300 classified, 15+ read)

Per-category means across all 300 prompts (344 total verifiable instructions; per-prompt category scores can be fractional when a prompt carries multiple constraints of the same type):

| Category | Prompts with category | Strict mean (sum / prompts) | Loose mean (sum / prompts) | Examples from inspected replies |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `repeat` | 9 | **0.00%** (0.0 / 9) | **0.00%** (0.0 / 9) | Misses exact sentence/phrase repetition or adds surrounding prose |
| `sentence` | 28 | **3.57%** (1.0 / 28) | **7.14%** (2.0 / 28) | Violates exact sentence-level structure (boundary words, keyword-per-sentence, bounds) |
| `words` | 85 | **11.76%** (10.0 / 85) | **17.65%** (15.0 / 85) | Violates forbidden words, required word frequency, or letter constraints |
| `ratio` | 44 | **15.91%** (7.0 / 44) | **15.91%** (7.0 / 44) | Misses punctuation/sentence/word ratio targets |
| `custom` | 11 | 27.27% (3.0 / 11) | 45.45% (5.0 / 11) | Extra prose or formatting wrappers break strict checks |
| `format` | 96 | 36.98% (35.5 / 96) | 52.60% (50.5 / 96) | Large strict-to-loose gap (+15.6 pp); inspected replies include markdown wrappers/preambles, wrong nesting depth, or non-emoji glyphs (`❖`) |
| `count` | 62 | 58.06% (36.0 / 62) | 59.68% (37.0 / 62) | Overshoots word/paragraph counts with preambles or closings |

No literal `<think>` tag was found in any of the 300 stored outputs. In inspected failing replies, recurring patterns include conversational preambles/wrappers that break strict format or count checks, inline self-correction text written into the graded reply (e.g. `"Wait — that doesn't indent properly..."`), and explicit refusal/surrender on strict character constraints.

### 2.3 Tool-Contract Sub-Weaknesses: BFCL x5 (165 failed trials audited, 22 raw traces read) and SWE-smith r6 (469 retained audited, 45+ traces read)

**BFCL x5 ([issue 11538](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11538): 450/615 = 73.17% final-selected record score under the retry rule; per-run 92, 92, 91, 86, 89 / 123; 449 known first-attempt wins with 1 unavailable first-attempt reward; 59 tasks 5/5, 12 tasks 0/5):**
- Weakest task categories: `simple-java` **53.3%** (8/15), `parallel` **62.9%** (22/35), `live-irrelevance` **65.5%** (95/145), `live-multiple` **74.3%** (130/175), `live-simple` **75.6%** (34/45), `multiple` **77.1%** (27/35), `parallel-multiple` **77.1%** (27/35).
- Verifier-log classification across all **165** failed trials (from the 615 saved `test-stdout.txt` logs):
  - **44 (26.7%) — residual `irrelevance` category failures** (`39 live-irrelevance + 5 irrelevance` not caught by missing-file or invalid-JSON checks). In inspected traces, Mochi emitted a tool call with guessed arguments instead of `[]`; the residual count itself does not verify the cause of every trial.
  - **44 (26.7%) — `live-multiple` verifier mismatches** (inspected examples include minor argument formatting differences such as `"Santa Cruz, US"` vs `"Santa Cruz, USA"` or selecting a sibling function).
  - **23 (13.9%) — missing `/app/result.json`** (`11 live-irrelevance`, `1 irrelevance`, `2 parallel-multiple`, `2 simple-python`, `2 simple-javascript`, `2 live-simple`, `1 live-multiple`, `1 parallel`, `1 simple-java`). The verifier logs establish file absence; in inspected irrelevance traces Mochi replied in plain text instead of writing `[]`, and in some inspected non-irrelevance traces it called BFCL target function names directly as Pi tools instead of writing `/app/result.json`.
  - **18 (10.9%) — `parallel` (12) and `parallel-multiple` (6) verifier mismatches** (inspected examples include omitted calls, parameter mismatches, or double-nested list syntax `[[...]]`).
  - **11 (6.7%) — `simple-python`**, **8 (4.8%) — `multiple`**, **7 (4.2%) — `live-simple`**, **6 (3.6%) — `simple-java`** (inspected examples emit JSON objects instead of Java constructor strings like `new QName(...)`), **2 (1.2%) — invalid JSON** in `/app/result.json`, **1 — `live-relevance`**, **1 — `live-parallel-multiple`**.

**SWE-smith 128x8 r6 screen (snapshot counts: 469 retained, 463 scored, 184 passed = 39.74%; 115/173 = 66.47% in the audit's exception-free scored bucket; 111/147 = 75.51% in readout-`CLEAN` evidence-complete rows; 69/289 = 23.88% on `AgentTimeoutError` attempts; 184/462 = 39.83% vs Snowball 43604 88/462 = 19.05% on the 462 both-scored join):**
- **Extra `"command"` key and malformed-tool counts (kept in separate denominators):**
  - **69/469** retained attempts included at least one parsed `read` call with an extra `"command"` key (**391/1,707** parsed `read` calls), and **13/469** included an extra `"command"` key on `edit`.
  - The first named malformed-tool category in the readout-`BAD` rows was **`read` for 12/19**, **`edit` for 6/19**, and **`bash` for 1/19** (contrasting with Snowball 43604's malformed nested-`edit` pattern).
  - Raw `<tool_call>` text appeared in assistant messages in **21/58** exception-free `reward=0` attempts (**15 `read`, 6 `edit`**). Inspected examples contain malformed JSON combining `"command":` with `"path":` or `"view_range":` (e.g., `{"name": "read", "arguments": {"command": "view_range": [1, 100]}}`), which suggests a hypothesis of schema bleed from `str_replace_editor`-style training traces into Pi's `read`/`edit` schemas.
- **Exception-free `reward=0` residual (37/58 without raw `<tool_call>` text):** Across all 58 exception-free `reward=0` attempts, 38 had at least one parsed `edit` call and 20 did not (vs 115/115 with a parsed `edit` call in the audit's exception-free passing bucket). In 12 inspected edited failures, Mochi modified code and ran local checks/pytest before finishing, yet failed hidden verifier tests; the audit script does not classify patch defects across all 37.
- **Timeouts (`289/469 = 61.6%` `AgentTimeoutError` at 900 s):** Among the 220 timed-out failures (`reward=0`), median progress is 18 agent steps, only **40/220 (18.2%)** contained a parsed `edit` call (vs **68/69 = 98.6%** of timed-out passes), and **160/220 (72.7%)** ran `git log`/`git show`/`git diff` commands before the 900 s cap.

### 2.4 `ds-1000-local` (27.00% = 54/200; all 200 classified, 25 ATIF trajectories read)

`ds-1000-local` sits inside Snowball 10/05's (`27.85% [23.12–31.00]`, k=6) and Qwen3.6-35B's (`26.75% [23.50–28.50]`, k=9) observed ranges, slightly below Nemotron-3.5-30B's range (`28.46% [27.50–30.50]`, k=9), and below Gemma-4-26B (`41.50%`, k=1). Its error breakdown differs from comparators:
- **Outcome partition (200 tasks):** 43 exception-free pass, 95 exception-free fail, **60 `AgentTimeoutError` at 1,800 s** (49 fail, 11 pass), and **2 `ModelInitiatedTmuxFailure`** (both fail). In the single checked comparator runs from EvalDash, timeouts were 1–6/200 (Qwen3.6: 1, Nem3.5-30B: 3, Gemma-4: 4, Snowball 10/05: 6).
- **Inspected Terminus-2 trajectories (25 total: 10 timeout-0, 10 clean-0, 2 tmux-0, 3 timeout-1):**
  - In the 10 inspected timeout failures (10–20 agent steps, ~7.4k–8.5k completion tokens), Mochi repeatedly rewrote `/workspace/solution/solution.py` (4–9 times) and ran custom import/`runpy` checks until hitting 1,800 s (one passing timeout, `ds-1000/541`, timed out right on Terminus-2's `"task_complete": true` confirmation turn).
  - In the 10 inspected exception-free failures (4–15 steps), Mochi wrote runnable code and marked the task complete while missing part of the prompt or execution contract (e.g., `ds-1000/104` replaced `&` with `&` without evaluating the resulting expression; `ds-1000/127` hardcoded `df.sample(n=1, random_state=0)` instead of sampling 20% of rows).
  - Both `ModelInitiatedTmuxFailure` cases occurred when sending shell control sequences during recovery from a hung command/quote.

### 2.5 `gsm8k-0shot` (83.55% = 1,102/1,319; all 217 failures classified, 20 read) — Extractor-Sensitivity Caveat

- **145 / 217 misses (66.8%) contain the normalized gold number in the final 250 characters under the regex used here.** Of those, **29** also match a verification keyword (`check`/`verify`/`double-check`/`confirm`) and **116** do not. The other **72** did not match the gold-number heuristic.
- This flags candidates for extractor sensitivity (in inspected replies, Mochi stated the gold number and then either restated a prompt quantity or appended a verification equation whose final number the last-number regex picked up). A verified corrected accuracy was not measured, so this audit neither estimates a corrected GSM8K score nor rules out genuine arithmetic errors.

### 2.6 Other Teams' Mochi Evaluations

- **Identity under `/think` ([issue 11418](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11418)):** Reports **222/320 (69.4%)** foreign-maker self-claims (Google/Gemini 129, Anthropic/Claude 41, OpenAI/ChatGPT 23, Zhipu 11) and **43/320** Marin-alone answers with reasoning enabled, versus near-100% Marin with `/nothink`, and proposes adding thinking-mode identity examples (noting `identity-data` is `/nothink`-only). Causality and the effect of adding those examples are untested here.
- **Variant effect prediction ([issue 11181](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11181)):** Closed exploratory evaluation on two 300-variant autosomal Mendelian train panels (10% positive rate). Raw-DNA log-likelihood scored AUPRC 0.178 (no prefix) / 0.189 (healthy prefix) with 61.1% / 60.7% within-group wins on missense, and AUPRC 0.150 / 0.141 with 50.0% / 49.3% within-group wins (near chance) on TSS-proximal variants.

---

## 3. Proposed Candidate Target Skills (with Fast-Eval Proposals and Non-Eval Data Ideas)

*Data hygiene rule:* **Eval-side traces and benchmark prompts/outputs are never used as training data.** Every training data proposal below relies exclusively on freshly synthesized or non-eval open templates verified programmatically. Probe runtimes below are rough estimates and not yet measured on Mochi's serve.

### Proposal 1: Long-Context Ordinal Multi-Needle Retrieval and Verbatim Copy
- **Target gap:** Largest observed deficit vs peers (`mrcr-65k` 26.49% vs Qwen3.6 92.08% and Nemotron-3.5-30B 45.75%), with 423/620 prefix-matching low-score items matching a different same-topic occurrence by 60-character substring (323 under literal stripped-output equality), predominantly later than requested.
- **Proposed fast eval (rough estimate: minutes-scale):** A 100–200 item synthetic multi-needle probe at 8K–64K context (2/4/8 repeated-topic needles, querying the *k*-th 1-indexed occurrence with a random prefix), scored deterministically in Python by exact prefix and string similarity without an LLM judge.
- **Proposed clean training data:** Programmatically synthesize multi-turn dialogues (8K–64K tokens) mixing filler turns with 2–12 repeated requests on fresh non-MRCR topics, paired with final-turn ordinal retrieval queries distributed uniformly over *k* from 1 to *N* (covering both `/think` counting chains and `/nothink` direct-copy targets).

### Proposal 2: Strict Verifiable Constraint Following and Output Discipline
- **Target gap:** Strict instruction-following gap vs peers (`ifbench` 26.00% strict vs Gemma-4 43.44%, DeepSeek-V4-Flash 40.00%, Nemotron-3.5-120B 38.00%, Qwen3.6 34.57%), with `repeat` (0.00%), `sentence` (3.57%), `words` (11.76%), and `ratio` (15.91%) lowest.
- **Proposed fast eval (rough estimate: minutes-scale):** A 200-item held-out synthetic constraint suite covering word/sentence/ratio/repeat/format/no-preamble constraints, scored purely by deterministic Python verifiers without an LLM judge.
- **Proposed clean training data:** Programmatically compose fresh prompts combining 1–3 verifiable lexical/structural constraints (forbidden/required words, exact sentence/word counts, keyword-per-sentence, ratio bounds, strict JSON/markdown structure, no preamble/postscript), generate candidates, and **rejection-sample strictly using deterministic Python verifiers** (keeping only 100%-passing responses across both `/think` and `/nothink` formats).

### Proposal 3: Tool-Schema Adherence and Abstention Across Diverse Tool Contracts
- **Target gap:** Addresses the concrete tool-contract weaknesses observed in BFCL x5 (`simple-java` 53.3%, `parallel` 62.9%, `live-irrelevance` 65.5%) and the extra-`"command"` `read`/malformed-call defects observed in SWE-smith r6 (69/469 attempts with extra `"command"` on parsed `read`; 12/19 readout-`BAD` first-tool `read`; 21/58 exception-free `reward=0` raw `<tool_call>` text).
- **Proposed fast eval (rough estimate: minutes-scale):** A 150–200 item single-turn synthetic tool-calling probe testing: (a) unfamiliar file/code tool schemas deliberately distinct from `str_replace_editor` (checking valid Hermes JSON and zero undeclared keys), (b) irrelevance/abstention prompts requiring an explicit empty tool list or required artifact, and (c) parallel and typed-argument multi-call prompts. Graded deterministically by JSON-schema and AST checks without container spinup.
- **Proposed clean training data:** Synthesize diverse tool definitions (varying parameter names across file readers/editors, SQL/API clients, and typed Java/JS/Python signatures) with programmatically verified trajectories teaching strict adherence to declared JSON schemas, calibrated abstention when no tool applies or required arguments are missing, and parallel call arrays.

---

## 4. What Is Missing to Decide (Absence of Completed Full-Size Scores in This Snapshot)

In the retained EvalDash cache for `mochi-sft-step400407` (46 recorded runs: 23 `succeeded`, 20 `step_failed`, 2 `infra_failed`, 1 `running`), the following benchmarks have no completed full-size score. Recorded failure statuses alone do not establish backend-death causes or rule out model-side behavior, and absence of a row means no run was found in this snapshot (not a proof it was never run elsewhere).

| Benchmark | Snapshot status on Mochi step 400,407 | Snowball 10/05 EP-Oct (k) | Qwen3.6-35B EP-Oct (k) | Why it matters for targeting |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| **Micro210** (per-source suite) | No completed run found in the reviewed Micro210 ledger or EvalDash snapshot | 41.44% / 40.91% suite pooled (runs 44627 / 44628) | — | Per-source breakdown across internal post-training domains; aligns Mochi with Snowball ablation ledgers |

| `tb2-recovery` / `ot-tblite-recovery` | `1 step_failed` each (`2026-11-17T14:35:25`) | 11.28% (6) / 22.17% (5) | 35.77% (9) / 60.13% (9) | Long-horizon terminal/shell agency |
| `bixbench-pi` / `tau3-pi` | No run found in snapshot | 14.72% (6) / 6.30% (5) | 34.81% (9) / 36.50% (4) | Multi-turn scientific analysis and policy/tool dialogue |
| `aime24` / `olympiadbench` / `math500` (full) | `aime24`: `2 step_failed` (`16:27:39`, `18:18:58`); `olympiadbench`: `1 step_failed` (`14:51:31`); `math500`: `1 step_failed` (`18:18:58`), `1 infra_failed` (`19:12:42`), plus 18- and 20-item `succeeded` smokes at 100% | 79.67% (6) / 22.47% (5) / 96.33% (6) | 94.59% (9) / 35.00% (9) / 98.86% (7) | Hard-math headroom vs peers (cannot be inferred from `gsm8k-0shot`) |
| `gpqa-diamond` | No run found in snapshot | 66.43% (5) | 84.82% (7) | Graduate-level STEM reasoning |
| `mmlu-pro` | `2 step_failed` (`2026-11-16T16:27:39`, `18:18:58`) | 72.38% (5) | 85.26% (7) | Broad 10-way academic/domain knowledge |
| `cruxeval` / `nupa` | `2 step_failed` each (`2026-11-16T16:27:39`, `18:18:58`) | 58.63% (3) / 11.24% (4) | 91.94% (3) / 82.99% (8) | Code-execution reasoning (`cruxeval`) and numeric/algorithmic precision (`nupa`) |
| `mrcr` (128K full) | `1 step_failed` (`2026-11-16T16:27:39`) | 19.25% (5) | 91.40% (7) | Long-context behavior past 65K |

| **Controlled thinking-mode check** on `mrcr-65k` & `ifbench` | Not yet run on the same serve | — | — | Tests Mochi's sensitivity to thinking mode on the same serve before attributing the full gap to model capacity |

**Suggested next decision sequence (read-only recommendations; no jobs launched):**
1. Run a controlled thinking-on vs thinking-off sensitivity check on `mrcr-65k` and `ifbench` on the same serve, alongside completing the missing fast EvalDash benchmarks (`aime24`, `math500` full, `mmlu-pro`, `gpqa-diamond`, `cruxeval`, `nupa`) and a Mochi Micro210 baseline.

🤖

# Research

The step 400,407 audit identifies model and serving hypotheses, but no isolated repository defect: `mrcr-65k` and `ifbench` each have one full-size Mochi run and no matched thinking-mode check. The 145 GSM8K misses with a gold number near the end are extractor-sensitivity candidates, not a verified corrected score. The failed EvalDash records also need their own failure classification before reruns. Tool-call data work is already tracked in [#11536](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11536), and the Micro210 policy is being frozen in [#11686](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11686).

**Relevant code**
- [Evaluation launcher](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evaluation/cli.py) — resolves model and evaluation runs.
- [Evaluation records](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/records.py) — preserves run status and provenance.

# Plan

1. Freeze the Mochi export, tokenizer, serve and harness revisions, generation settings, task IDs, seeds, source `record.json` files, and a GPU/time budget. Classify each `step_failed` and `infra_failed` record from its saved artifacts; do not infer backend failure from status alone.
2. On the same serve, run matched thinking-on and thinking-off panels for `mrcr-65k` and `ifbench`, holding prompts, seeds, context limits, and output budgets fixed. Report paired score changes with uncertainty, MRCR needle-count and length slices, IFBench strict categories, truncation, and failures. If mode changes the scores, resolve that confound before attributing the gap to SFT data.
3. Complete the missing full-size fast EvalDash panel (`aime24`, `math500`, `mmlu-pro`, `gpqa-diamond`, `cruxeval`, `nupa`) after the failure classification, using the existing launcher and recording each terminal result. Run a Mochi Micro210 baseline against the frozen policy from #11686 when available. Separately regrade the 145 flagged GSM8K misses against the retained outputs and canonical scorer; open a scoped scorer fix only if a grading defect is reproduced.
4. Start with the ordinal multi-needle proposal if the matched mode check leaves a substantial MRCR gap. Make separate train and held-out synthetic templates, verify no eval prompt or trace enters training, and measure a 100–200 item probe before any SFT run. Compare a matched Snowball control and candidate, then promote to Mochi only if the held-out probe and full MRCR evaluation improve without losing Micro210 or BFCL. If that gate fails, report the negative result and evaluate the strict-constraint proposal next; coordinate tool-schema work with #11536.

| Sub-suite (n=50 each) | `/nothink` pass [marginal Wilson 95%] | `/think` pass [marginal Wilson 95%] | Notes |

| `irrelevance_abstention` | **38.00%** (19/50) [25.86–51.85] | **100.00%** (50/50) [92.87–100.00] | `/nothink` scored **0/25 (0.0%)** on missing-required-argument prompts (`missing_ticket` 0/9, `missing_station_id` 0/8, `missing_repo_slug` 0/8) and **19/25 (76.0%)** on domain-mismatch (31 total over-calls); the `/think` configuration passed all 50 abstention items (25/25 on both) |
| `parallel_and_typed` | **100.00%** (50/50) [92.87–100.00] | **100.00%** (50/50) [92.87–100.00] | 25/25 parallel 2–3 calls + 25/25 strict typed JSON/Java-expression args in both configurations |
| `schema_adherence_non_sre` | **100.00%** (50/50) [92.87–100.00] | **84.00%** (42/50) [71.49–91.66] | All 8 `/think` mismatches (`patch_snippet` 0/7, `pi_edit` 1/7) emitted schema-valid `inspect_file` (7) or `read` (1) calls with 0 undeclared keys and 0 malformed JSON, rather than patching directly |
| **Total (150)** | **79.33%** (119/150) [72.16–85.04] | **94.67%** (142/150) [89.83–97.27] | The verifier found zero replies with the undeclared `command` key, malformed parsed tool-call blocks, or unbalanced tool-call tags in the 300 Probe 3 final answers (including 18/18 clean `pi_read` in both modes) |

- **Abstention contrast:** Under `/nothink`, Mochi fired 31 over-calls across the 50 abstention items (all 25 missing-required-argument prompts plus 6/25 domain-mismatch questions); the `/think` configuration passed all 50 abstention items (0 over-calls, 0 both-fail).
- **Single-turn schema adherence vs SWE-smith r6:** The verifier found zero replies with the undeclared `command` key, malformed parsed tool-call blocks, or unbalanced tool-call tags in the 300 Probe 3 final answers. The single-turn probe did not reproduce the SWE-smith pattern. Multi-turn context is one candidate to test in a matched follow-up.

---

### 3. Updated Targeting Implications (Read-Only Summary)

1. **Multi-needle ordinal retrieval at high needle count (`8 needles`: 52.5% `/nothink`, 50.0% `/think`)** persists under both configurations, alongside lower `<|start_think|>` emission in longer nominal bands (63.3% at 8k down to 20.0% at 56k) and 10 early-EOT unclosed think spans plus 1 cap hit on Probe 1 `/think`.
2. **Tool abstention under `/nothink` (38.0% overall; 0/25 on missing-required-argument prompts)** is a sharp deficit whereas the `/think` configuration passed all 50 abstention items (100.0%). Single-turn `parallel_and_typed` passed 50/50 in both configurations and `schema_adherence_non_sre` passed 50/50 (`/nothink`) and 42/50 (`/think`, with all 8 mismatches being schema-valid `inspect_file`/`read` calls), without reproducing the SWE-smith `command`-key pattern.
3. **Deterministic constraint following scored higher under the `/think` configuration (82.5% -> 96.7%; 19 think-only passes vs 2 nothink-only)**, with three of the four Probe 2 `/think` failures hitting the 4,096-token cap (compared with one 4,096-token cap hit and ten early EOTs on Probe 1 `/think`). This motivates running a controlled configuration check on full `ifbench` and `mrcr-65k` before committing large synthetic-data budget to constraint SFT.

## Part Three (Design): Synthetic Training Data Design for Two Target Skills

**Scope:** Design-only proposal for two programmatically verified training datasets targeting the two sharpest weaknesses surfaced by the Mochi 3-probe diagnostics above. **No training packet or job is proposed yet** — this design will be gated on the matched Snowball 10/05 proxy probe results before any data generation or training launch.

**One-hour continuation geometry reference:** Under our standard one-hour long-loop SFT continuation schedule (**60 updates × 32 packs/update = 1,920 packs, or 503,316,480 packed positions at 262,144 positions/pack**), all pack budgets below are sized directly against `1,920` total packs using the pinned tokenizer and chat template (`marin-community/marin-tokenizer-tools`, revision `3f6879acdaf3dae7874b2d48c7d11b9d8c6faf09`). Proposed example counts below assume near-full packing at the proposed mean lengths; actual packing utilization, realized per-update row doses, and realized supervised target counts will be verified by a CPU packing audit before any training launch. Every training dataset is strictly segregated from evaluation probes and benchmarks.

---

### Skill A: Nth-of-Many-Similar-Passages Retrieval (8K–64K Context, 4–16 Needles)

**Target defect:** On Probe 1, Mochi dropped from 90.0% at 2 needles to **52.5% (`/nothink`) / 50.0% (`/think`)** at 8 needles, while `<|start_think|>` opening-marker emission under `/think` declined from 63.3% (8k) to 20.0% (56k), and 10 replies stopped at EOT with unclosed think spans plus 1 hit the 4,096-token cap.

1. **Generator:**
   - Synthesizes multi-turn conversations stratified across **4 context-length bands** (`8K`, `16K`, `32K`, `56K` tokens; equal-weight band average `~28,000` tokens/example, staying strictly within `[8,000, 64,000]` rendered tokens) and **5 needle counts** `N ∈ {4, 6, 8, 12, 16}` (weighted toward higher needle counts: `15%` at 4, `15%` at 6, `25%` at 8, `25%` at 12, `20%` at 16).
   - Within each conversation, `N` similar passages for a shared `(domain, entity_id)` are distributed across early, middle, and late turns interspersed with multi-paragraph filler turns from other domains. Passages vary across **multiple structural styles** (prose briefs, bulleted checklists, key-value memos, tabular rows, short Q&A logs, and meeting notes) to avoid single-template overfitting.
   - The final user turn asks for the `k`-th (1-indexed) occurrence verbatim, with `k` sampled **uniformly over `{1..N}`**. Prompt phrasing varies between a random 8–12 character prepend token (50% of examples) and clean direct-copy without a prefix (50%).
   - **Mode split (`50% /nothink`, `50% /think`):**
     - `/nothink` (`Reasoning: /nothink`): target output is the exact verbatim `k`-th passage (with prefix if requested) and no extra prose.
     - `/think` (`Reasoning: /think`): target output opens with `<|start_think|>`, lists a concise 1-line numbered anchor for occurrences `1..N` in order (target length `~120–350` tokens, capped at `<= 512` tokens), closes cleanly with `<|end_think|>`, and outputs the exact verbatim `k`-th passage.

2. **Deterministic verifier (zero LLM judge; 100% gate before packing):**
   - Renders each example with `marin-tokenizer-tools@3f6879a` and verifies:
     - Prompt token count is inside `[8,000, 64,000]` and total sequence length `<= 65,536`.
     - All `N` target occurrences are pairwise distinct (unique record IDs and pairwise `SequenceMatcher` ratio `< 0.85`).
     - Extracted final answer (after stripping `<|start_think|>...<|end_think|>` on `/think` items) matches the exact `k`-th occurrence verbatim (100% string equality, including exact prefix when requested).
     - On `/think` items: exactly one `<|start_think|>` and one `<|end_think|>`, think span `<= 512` tokens, and enumerated count equals `N`. On `/nothink` items: zero `<|start_think|>` or `<|end_think|>` markers.
     - **Render-and-packed-mask round-trip check:** After packing into `262,144`-token rows with `segment_ids`, decodes the masked target positions (`weight[i] == 1 -> token[i+1]`) for every packed segment and verifies exact equality with the intended terminal assistant span plus EOT.

3. **Topic and seed disjointness from pinned eval corpora:**
   - Dedicated training seed namespace: `mochi-train-skillA-ordinal-v1` (disjoint from eval seed `mochi-probes-20261119-eval-only-v1`).
   - **Build-time blocklist:** Excludes all 12 Probe 1 operational domains (`substation fault brief`, `greenhouse irrigation log`, `harbor berth dispatch`, `zoning variance memo`, `observatory exposure entry`, `coldchain batch audit`, `waterworks valve ticket`, `geothermal well bulletin`, `rail switch advisory`, `aquifer piezometer note`, `cleanroom filter record`, `bridge bearing inspection`), Probe 1 crew/region/status vocabularies, and MRCR literary genres (`poem`, `riddle`, `short story`, `essay`, `haiku`, `blog post`).
   - Uses a disjoint catalog of 20+ fresh operational domains (e.g., aviation maintenance workcards, library acquisition slips, freight customs declarations, museum conservation notes, pharmacy compounding sheets, hydrology gauge bulletins, textile dye-lot cards, acoustics chamber logs, foundry melt tickets, vineyard harvest records, satellite pass bulletins, municipal fleet work orders).
   - **Pinned-corpus overlap audit:** Automated build-time check against the pinned Probe 1 input file and the cached 901-item MRCR-65K prompt corpus verifies zero overlap in domain labels, entity codes, and lowercased alphanumeric-normalized 8-grams computed strictly over non-boilerplate payload/content text (excluding shared chat-template markers and generic instruction framing). This certifies disjointness from those scanned pinned corpora rather than broader evaluation independence against unseen benchmarks.

4. **Loss mask (assistant-only — terminal retrieval turn strictly):**
   - **Shifted target convention:** Set `weight[i] = 1.0` iff `token[i+1]` is in the selected assistant span after the header (`[128006, 78191, 128007, 198]`), through and including its EOT (`128009`).
   - For Skill A, **select only the terminal retrieval turn**; all earlier turns (system header, all user turns, all prior assistant filler/needle turns) and all segment-boundary/padding positions receive `weight[i] = 0.0`, so gradients come exclusively from the retrieval target rather than synthetic filler turns.

5. **Size for a one-hour run (packs & idealized example count):**
   - At `~28,000` proposed mean tokens/example and near-full packing, `~9.36` examples fit per `262,144`-position pack (isolated via `segment_ids`).
   - **Proposed one-hour budget:** **`120` packs (`6.25%` of `1,920` packs; `31.46M` packed positions; `~1,123` examples under ideal packing)** — sweep range `80–160` packs (`4.17%–8.33%`, `~749–1,498` examples under ideal packing). Actual packed utilization and realized supervised target-token counts will be measured in the CPU packing audit before launch, and general-skill retention will be measured on Micro210 and BFCL rather than assumed from pack share.

---

### Skill B: Abstain or Ask When a Required Tool Argument Is Missing (Thinking Off)

**Target defect:** On Probe 3 `/nothink`, Mochi scored **38.00% (19/50)** on `irrelevance_abstention` — firing **31 over-calls across all 50 abstention prompts** (**25/25** on missing-required-argument prompts, `0.0%` pass, plus **6/25** on domain-mismatch prompts, `76.0%` pass) — whereas the `/think` configuration passed all 50 abstention items.

1. **Generator:**
   - All examples are rendered with `enable_thinking=False` (`Reasoning: /nothink`) and OpenAI-format tool definitions inside `<tools>...</tools>` using the exact Hermes `<tool_call>` contract.
   - **Example-level stratum allocation (`45% / 20% / 35%` over examples):**
     - **`45%` Missing-required-argument abstention examples:** User asks to perform an action matching one of 3–6 declared tools, where 1–2 `required` parameters are withheld in the structured fixture (absent from both user prompt and conversation context). Half include an explicit "do not guess" cue and half are **natural prompts with no cue**. Target turn-1 assistant reply: **zero `<tool_call>` blocks**, concise 1–2 sentence clarification that explicitly asks the user to supply the withheld parameter(s). A subset are 2-turn follow-ups (turn 1: assistant asks for missing parameter -> turn 2: user provides the fixture value -> turn 2 assistant emits the valid `<tool_call>`), which adds positive tool-call reply turns beyond the 35% positive-only example share.
     - **`20%` Domain-mismatch / unsupported-tool abstention examples:** User asks a general question or requests an action not covered by any declared tool. Target assistant reply: **zero `<tool_call>` blocks**, concise plain-text answer or note that no declared tool supports the request.
     - **`35%` Positive tool-calling control examples (same tool catalog, all required arguments supplied):** Drawn from the same schemas and actions as the abstention strata (covering single-call, parallel `2–3` calls, and strict typed arguments: booleans, integer arrays, nested objects). For matched subsets, generator builds explicit **minimal pairs** sharing the exact same schema, action, and background context with only the required parameter value withheld (abstention) versus supplied (positive call); overall strata proportions (`45% / 20% / 35%`) are not 1:1 paired across every item.

2. **Deterministic verifier (zero LLM judge; 100% gate before packing):**
   - Validates every generated example against its **structured fixture** before packing:
     - Validates every tool schema in `<tools>` (`type: "object"`, valid `properties` and `required` list).
     - Asserts exact `Reasoning: /nothink` system header and zero `<|start_think|>`/`<|end_think|>` tokens in assistant turns.
     - On **abstention turns**: asserts zero `<tool_call>` or `</tool_call>` substrings and non-empty reply (`10–80` words). For missing-required-argument turns, verifies against the structured fixture and full conversation text that (a) each withheld required parameter's ground-truth value is absent from all prior user/system text and (b) the templated/structured clarification reply contains an explicit request phrase (interrogative or request verb) directed at the specific withheld parameter(s) (not merely an incidental name mention).
     - On **positive tool-call turns** (35% positive controls + turn 2 of 2-turn follow-ups): parses every `<tool_call>...</tool_call>` block with the strict Hermes parser, asserts zero malformed JSON, zero unbalanced tags, declared tool name, **zero undeclared keys**, all `required` keys present, exact JSON types, and exact equality against the **fixture-backed ground-truth arguments**.
     - **Render-and-packed-mask round-trip check:** After packing into `262,144`-position rows with `segment_ids`, decodes masked target positions (`weight[i] == 1 -> token[i+1]`) per segment and verifies exact equality with the selected assistant span(s) plus EOT.

3. **Topic, schema, and seed disjointness from pinned eval corpora:**
   - Dedicated training seed namespace: `mochi-train-skillB-abstention-v1` (disjoint from `mochi-probes-20261119-eval-only-v1`).
   - **Build-time blocklist:** Excludes all 11 Probe 3 tool names (`read`, `edit`, `bash`, `inspect_file`, `patch_snippet`, `fetch_log_slice`, `get_station_telemetry`, `get_release_tag`, `schedule_maintenance`, `configure_alert_rule`, `invoke_java_binding`), all Probe 3 prompts, and all BFCL function names/prompts in the pinned 123-task set.
   - Synthesizes 40+ fresh tool schemas from disjoint operational domains (e.g., warehouse inventory transfers, invoice reconciliation, CI artifact promotion, shift roster lookup, transit route dispatch, lab specimen intake, DNS record updates, cloud quota requests, fleet fuel logging, library hold management) with varied `snake_case` and `camelCase` parameter names.
   - **Pinned-corpus overlap audit:** Automated build-time check against the pinned Probe 3 input file and cached 123-task BFCL prompt set verifies zero tool-name overlap and zero lowercased alphanumeric-normalized 8-gram overlap over non-boilerplate prompt text (excluding shared `<tools>` wrapper boilerplate). This certifies disjointness from those scanned pinned corpora rather than broader evaluation independence against unseen suites.

4. **Loss mask (assistant-only):**
   - **Shifted target convention:** Set `weight[i] = 1.0` iff `token[i+1]` is in the selected assistant span after the header (`[128006, 78191, 128007, 198]`), through and including its EOT (`128009`).
   - On single-turn examples, the single assistant reply is selected; on 2-turn follow-ups, **both** the turn-1 clarification reply and the turn-2 valid tool-call reply are selected. System header, `<tools>...</tools>` JSON schemas, user turns, `<tool_response>` spans, and boundary/padding positions all receive `weight[i] = 0.0`.

5. **Size for a one-hour run (packs & idealized example count):**
   - At `~550` proposed mean tokens/example and near-full packing, `~477` examples fit per `262,144`-position pack (isolated via `segment_ids`).
   - **Proposed one-hour budget:** **`32` packs (`1.67%` of `1,920` packs; `~15,252` examples under ideal packing)** — sweep range `24–48` packs (`1.25%–2.50%`, `~11,439–22,878` examples under ideal packing). Realized packing utilization and supervised target-token share will be measured in the CPU packing audit before launch, and any effect on general/tool-calling balance will be checked on Micro210 and BFCL.

---

### Mixing with General Replay in a One-Hour Continuation (`1,920` Packs Total)

All comparisons below hold the starting checkpoint, optimizer/LR schedule, precision bundle, and non-replaced general replay rows fixed against the matched general-only control:

| Proposed arm (60 updates × 32 packs = 1,920 packs) | Skill A packs (%) | Skill B packs (%) | General replay packs (%) | Total replacement packs (%) | Replacement package tested |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **Matched general-only control** | `0` | `0` | `1,920` (100.00%) | `0` (0.00%) | Baseline continuation (no added skill data) |
| **Single-skill Arm A (recommended first)** | `120` (6.25%) | `0` | `1,800` (93.75%) | `120` (6.25%) | Replaces 120 general packs with Skill A (`8K–64K`, 4–16 needles) |
| **Single-skill Arm B (recommended first)** | `0` | `32` (1.67%) | `1,888` (98.33%) | `32` (1.67%) | Replaces 32 general packs with Skill B (`/nothink` abstention + positive controls) |
| **Combined Arm A+B** | `120` (6.25%) | `32` (1.67%) | `1,768` (92.08%) | `152` (7.92%) | Replaces 152 general packs (comparable by row share only to prior 1h `164`-pack / 8.54% runs) |

**Mixture, packing, and gating plan:**
- **Separate named `MixtureDataset` sources:** Pack Skill A (`skill_a_ordinal_retrieval`) and Skill B (`skill_b_nothink_tool_abstention`) into independent `262,144`-position Levanter caches with exact per-document `segment_ids` (zero cross-document attention) and interleave deterministically with `general_replay` across all 60 updates. Before any training launch, verify realized per-update row doses and realized supervised target counts in a CPU packing audit.
- **Optional per-source temperature matching:** Conditional on enabling the trainer's temperature-matching option and binding exact `MixtureDataset` source IDs (`disabled_sources=("skill_a_ordinal_retrieval", "skill_b_nothink_tool_abstention")`), the regularizer applies only on selected `general_replay` targets.
- **Planned evaluation gates (thresholds frozen before any launch; strictly disjoint from training data):** Evaluate Snowball proxy arms within the matched equal-budget (`max_tokens=4,096` for both `/nothink` and `/think`) 3-probe setup (the earlier Mochi run1 probes used 1,024 vs 4,096 and supply context only), tracking: (1) Probe 1 8-needle retrieval and long-context `<|start_think|>` opening/closure; (2) Probe 3 `/nothink` abstention gain gated on zero positive-call regression on `schema_adherence_non_sre` and `parallel_and_typed`; (3) BFCL x5 (`live-irrelevance` and positive-call categories); and (4) Micro210 general and agent retention against the matched general-only control.

---

### Realized CPU Packing Audit Addendum (Built Caches & Skill B v2 Cue Balance)

The pack budgets above (**Skill A: `120` train packs; Skill B: `32` train packs; Combined: `152` train packs**) remain unchanged. Both caches were built and audited on CPU at 262,144 positions per pack using the E12-B Levanter TreeCache zarr3 layout. The audits verified the shifted assistant-only mask, exact packed-array readback and per-segment round-trips. The `cw-us-east-02a` upload receipts record SHA-256 readback verification for all 28 objects per cache. Draft PR 11730 is at `dac1546a5c`.

- **Skill A (`skill_a_ordinal_retrieval`):**
  - **Train:** **`120` packs** (`963` rows, `27,365,607` real positions, `86.99%` packing utilization, **`208,167`** supervised target tokens; `482` `/nothink` and `481` `/think`; bands `241` at 8k, `241` at 16k, `241` at 32k, `240` at 56k; needles `144` at 4, `144` at 6, `243` at 8, `240` at 12, `192` at 16).
  - **Loss-weight dose knob (`w = 30.0` rescaled cache):** At `w = 1.0`, `208,167` supervised target tokens represent `0.047%` of a 60-update 1,920-pack Snowball arm (`~442.6M` supervised tokens). A rescaled immutable cache keeps byte-identical `input_ids` and scales supervised `loss_weights` to `{0.0, 30.0}`, giving `effective_loss_weight_sum = 6,245,010.0` on train (`1.39%` loss share over `442,395,665 + 6,245,010`), `228,570.0` on validation, and `228,750.0` on test (all 28 objects SHA-256 readback verified). This weight is a knob chosen for a `1.39%` loss share, not a measured optimum.
  - **Validation / Test:** `4` packs (`35` rows, `91.52%` utilization, `7,619` targets) and `4` packs (`35` rows, `91.42%` utilization, `7,625` targets), covering all five needle counts.
  - **Disjointness audit:** `0` normalized non-boilerplate 8-grams and `0` exact domain-label and tool-name matches in the scanned corpora — Probe 1 (`1,738,264` eval 8-grams), Probe 2 (`6,459`), Probe 3 v1 (`1,976`), Probe 3 v2 (`1,810`, scanned in the `w = 30.0` receipt), and Micro210 validation (`112,434`) — with all positive/negative controls passing. Because Skill A shares Probe 1's multi-turn ordinal retrieval format, any Skill A readout treats Probe 1 as an in-format check and pairs it with the published `mrcr-65k` benchmark on the same export.
- **Skill B v2 (`skill_b_nothink_tool_abstention`, cue-balanced rebuild; stays at `w = 1.0` on disk until it has a Mochi-side route):**
  - **Cue-balance revision:** The rebuild uses six anti-guessing paraphrases and includes a cue in about half the rows in each stratum. The first-turn cue rates below come from the realized rows. Second-turn cue balance is measured separately.
  - **Train:** **`32` packs** (`10,475` rows, `8,374,493` real positions, `99.83%` packing utilization, **`590,681`** supervised target tokens; `100% /nothink`; strata: `3,144` missing-single, `1,572` missing-twoturn, `2,096` domain-mismatch, `2,094` positive-single, `1,569` positive-parallel). Realized first-turn train cue balance: `P(abstain | cue) = 0.6504` vs `P(abstain | no_cue) = 0.6502` (first-turn absolute gap about `0.00012` before rounding); restricting to missing-argument and positive-control rows, `0.5629` vs `0.5628` (`|diff| = 0.0001`); per-family first-turn cue rates `0.5000` missing-arg, `0.5000` domain-mismatch, `0.4999` positive controls; `786/1,572` follow-up turns carry a cue, and all follow-up turns have a call target. The near balance of the measured cue does not establish absence of other predictive wording.
  - **Validation / Test:** `2` packs (`665` rows, `99.71%` utilization, `37,304` targets) and `2` packs (`667` rows, `99.87%` utilization, `37,520` targets), both passing the same cue-balance audit (`|diff| <= 0.02`).
  - **Disjointness audit:** `0` normalized non-boilerplate 8-grams and `0` exact domain-label and tool-name matches in the scanned corpora — Probe 1, Probe 2, Probe 3 v1, Probe 3 v2 (`1,810` eval 8-grams), and Micro210 validation — with all six positive/negative controls passing.

comments.author: Min-Li
comments.body:
@karansag I looked at the SFT data for your Skill B (ask when a tool argument is missing).

What I found:
* With thinking off, the model almost never saw this situation in training. Only 4,634 training conversations are "tools + a user request" with thinking off. That is 0.01% of the SFT mix.
* The other tool data with thinking off is coding agents (Open-SWE, OpenCode, SWE). There the assistant calls a tool on almost every turn.
* With thinking on, there are about 600,000 "tools + a user request" conversations. In about 149,000 of them the assistant asks for a missing value.
* So I think the model calls the tool because it has almost no examples of asking with thinking off. Your plan to add such examples makes sense.

One more thing:
* In `agentic_v1/tool_calling`, about 10% of the first tool calls use a fake value, like `verification_code: "1234"` or `api_key: "your_api_key_here"`. That is about 25,000 conversations. Maybe we should drop them.

Charts and examples: [report](https://claude.ai/artifact/TFnBivs8n5XFoMQ6rohd3u)

spillover_issues.title: [post-training] Mochi hero SFT (step 400,407) weakness analysis: benchmark gaps, trace failures, and candidate target skills

spillover_issues.author: cweill
spillover_issues.body:
## TL;DR

Synthetic documents that show AI systems choosing aligned actions (Tice et al. 2026, arXiv:2601.10160) shift small Marin-stack models toward aligned answers. The shift generalizes to questions whose documents were held out, and a word-shuffled copy of the documents produces a much smaller shift. We now test whether the effect follows the number of documents, as backdoor poisoning does (Souly et al. 2025), or their fraction of the training tokens. Tice et al. list this question as open. Runs use continued pretraining on Marin's released isoFLOP checkpoints. Status: in progress; one seed per arm so far.

## Description

Related: #11582 (the Data Belay judge scored every safety source "no" with no safety metric in its eval groups). The margin below is a candidate safety metric for small models.

**Metric.** Tice et al. released 4,174 two-choice AI-scenario questions, each with an aligned and a misaligned answer. For each question we compute the mean per-token log-probability of the aligned answer minus that of the misaligned answer, teacher-forced after `{question}\n\nAnswer:`. The "raw margin" is the mean over questions; higher means more aligned. Training documents cover a hash-selected half of the questions. We report the other half as held out.

Small models cannot use Tice et al.'s A/B letter format, so we validated the margin on their released 6.9B base models:

- Their letter-format protocol, rerun by us, reproduces their Table 3 within about 2 SE. Article-split misalignment rates: unfiltered 0.439 (paper 0.447), alignment-upsampled 0.104 (0.092), misalignment-upsampled 0.482 (0.508).
- The raw margin ranks the three models in the same order on both question splits. Article split: +0.053, +0.450, -0.060.
- A calibrated variant subtracts the margin after a question-free `Answer:` prompt. It misses the held-out textbook-split effect, so it is not the primary metric.

**Result 1: from scratch.** d768 Llama (8 layers), 1B DCLM tokens, Marin tokenizer, `train_lm` on one H100, seed 0. 16k aligned documents (about 25M tokens, 2.5%) replace DCLM text, each seen once.

| arm | raw margin, held-out | misaligned rate, held-out | val bpb |
|---|---|---|---|
| control | +0.028 ± 0.016 | 48.2% | 1.2398 |
| aligned documents | +0.216 ± 0.015 | 36.9% | 1.2441 |
| word-shuffled documents | +0.068 ± 0.015 | 46.3% | 1.2404 |

**Result 2: Marin isoFLOP checkpoints, untouched.** Seven DCLM-family checkpoints from 1e18 to 1e20 FLOPs (273M to 1.9B parameters including embeddings). All score 50% on the letter format because each answers one letter regardless of the question. The raw margin stays between +0.06 and +0.09 across sizes, near Tice et al.'s unfiltered 6.9B model (+0.053).

## Hypothesis or Goal

Measure whether the effect of k aligned documents depends on k or on k/N, where N is the number of training tokens, and how this changes with model size.

Design: continued pretraining of the 1e18 d768 checkpoint on N tokens of DCLM with k aligned documents, each seen once. N ∈ {12.5M, 50M, 200M, 800M}; k ∈ {0, 1k, 4k, 16k}; a k=0 control at every N; a word-shuffled control at k=16k, N=200M. The same grid at N ∈ {50M, 200M} then runs on the 3e18 d1024 and 3e19 d1536 checkpoints.

**Predictions, recorded before any results from this grid.** Effect = arm margin minus the k=0 control at the same N, fit as a + b·log(k / N^α). α near 0 means a count law; α near 1 means a fraction law. Our hypothesis: a count law holds when nothing else in the corpus addresses the trait, and a fraction law holds when other documents compete with it. About 7% of DCLM tokens are in documents that mention AI, so we predict α near 1 for this grid. A later grid on AI-filtered DCLM should move α toward 0.

## Status

- Done: metric validation on Tice et al.'s 6.9B models; ladder baselines; from-scratch seed-0 result above.
- Running: the 15-run grid on the 1e18 d768 checkpoint.
- Next: 3e18 and 3e19 grids, then more seeds.

Limitations: one seed per arm; the ± values are standard errors over questions, not seeds. The margin is validated against behavior on three 6.9B models only. Tice et al.'s documents and questions declare no license, so we use them for research and do not redistribute them.

## Links

* Logbook: research branch to follow
* Preregistration: the predictions below were first posted in marin-community/marin-logbooks#65 at 2026-11-18 22:38 UTC, before any continued-pretraining results; that issue's edit history is public.
* W&B runs (public): https://wandb.ai/cweill-self/alignment-dose
* Important updates:

## Decision Log

- Primary metric changed from the calibrated margin to the raw margin after the 6.9B validation, before any continued-pretraining results.
- Widened N from 4x to 64x on the smallest model. The exponent α is estimated with precision proportional to log of the N range.

## Conclusion


---

🤖 **Preregistration for batch 2** (19 continued-pretraining runs), posted before any of them start. These follow a methodology review of batch 1; batch 1 results will be posted separately.

Written 2026-11-19T00:55Z, before any of these runs started. Model: Marin 1e18 d768 isoFLOP checkpoint unless noted.
Effect = held-out raw margin (nats/token) minus the k=0 control with the same N, seed and schedule.
Fit from batch 1 (seed 0, cosine schedule, documents spread uniformly): effect = a + b·ln(k / N^α).

## Held-out point (cosine, uniform placement): N = 800M, k = 1k

- All-cells fit (α = 0.46): predicted effect **+0.048**.
- Fit on N ≤ 200M only (α = 0.39): predicted effect **+0.059**.
- Batch 1 suggests α rises with N, so we expect the observed value at or below +0.048. An observation below +0.035 or
  above +0.070 would mean the log-linear form is misspecified at this dose (0.19% document share).

## Placement under a fixed cooldown (WSD: constant LR, linear decay over the final ~50M tokens at every N)

Arms: k = 4k with all documents inside the final-50M decay window at N = 200M and N = 800M; k = 0 controls under the
same schedule at both N; k = 4k with all documents in the first 50M tokens at N = 200M.

- If recency explains the N-dependence: late-window effects at 200M and 800M are equal within noise (|difference| below
  ~0.02), and the early-window effect at 200M is well below the late-window one.
- If competition with the rest of the corpus explains it: the late-window effect at 800M is smaller than at 200M by
  roughly the amount the uniform runs show (+0.162 at 200M vs +0.117 at 800M, a 0.045 drop).
- We expect recency to explain at least half of the drop.

## Seeds

Two more data-order seeds for k = 0 and k = 4k at N = 50M and N = 200M (cosine, uniform). No directional prediction;
these measure seed-to-seed spread. We expect the spread of effects across seeds to exceed the question-bootstrap SE.

## Model size (3e18 d1024 checkpoint, cosine, uniform)

k = 0 and k = 4k at N = 50M and N = 200M, and k = 16k at N = 200M. Exploratory: these runs can detect only a large
change in α (SE about 0.1–0.15). No directional prediction.

| Held-out cell N = 800M, k = 1k: +0.048 (all-cells fit) or +0.059 (N ≤ 200M fit); outside 0.035–0.070 means the form is misspecified | **+0.052**, within range |
| Recency: under a fixed WSD decay, end-of-run effects at 200M and 800M equal within ~0.02; start-of-run effect well below | 200M **+0.198**, 800M **+0.178** (difference 0.020); start of run **+0.076** |
| Competition: the end-of-run drop matches the uniform drop (0.045) | drop 0.020, so recency accounts for about 55% of the uniform drop; prediction "at least half" holds |
| Seed spread exceeds the question-bootstrap SE | **wrong**: effect SD across 3 seeds is 0.001 at N = 50M and 200M, against a paired question SE of ~0.007 |
| d1024: exploratory | +0.221 / +0.190 / +0.262 at 50M-4k / 200M-4k / 200M-16k, against +0.193 / +0.162 / +0.230 for d768 |

Placing the documents in the final decay also raises the effect: at 800M, +0.178 at the end against +0.117 spread through the run.

**Controls** (N = 200M, about 4k documents' worth, cosine, d768)

| arm | effect |
|---|---|
| DCLM documents mentioning AI, character-matched to the aligned documents | +0.003 |
| word-shuffled aligned documents (16k) | +0.025 |
| misaligned documents (Tice et al., same seen questions) | +0.090 |
| aligned documents | +0.162 |

The misaligned documents describe AIs choosing the misaligned action, but they raise the aligned-answer margin, on held-out questions too. General AI discourse does not. The likeliest reading is familiarity with Tice-style scenario documents of either polarity; Tice et al. note that their documents explain why the AI avoided the alternative. With likelihood scoring, a raw-margin increase alone is not evidence of a directional shift; only the aligned-minus-misaligned difference is.

**What this does and does not show.** The fits and the placement result describe the total effect. Whether the directional part follows the same k, N and placement dependence is untested. The margin is a likelihood readout on Tice et al.'s own scenarios in base models, with no post-training. OpenAI's alignment team midtrained an o4-mini-sized model on the same documents and found the effect held on these questions but closed on out-of-distribution chat and agentic evaluations after RL ([How far does alignment midtraining generalize?](https://alignment.openai.com/how-far-does-alignment-midtraining-generalize/), March 2026). This study measures how document count, run length and placement move a near-distribution prior; it does not show that the prior survives post-training. The checkpoints span ~75M–185M non-embedding parameters, so we do not extrapolate to Marin-scale runs. If the recency result holds at larger scale, the relevant length for a Marin run is the anneal or midtraining window, not total pretraining tokens.

**Next.** Misaligned-document arms at N = 50M and 800M (k = 4k), to measure how the directional part scales with N.

Per-run results will be linked with the research branch. W&B (public): https://wandb.ai/cweill-self/alignment-dose

comments.author: cweill
comments.body: Correction to the update above. The comparison behind "most of the N-dependence is recency" (a drop of 0.045 from N = 200M to 800M with documents spread through the run, against 0.020 with documents in the final 50M tokens) mixes two learning-rate schedules: the spread-out runs used cosine and the end-window runs used WSD. Placement and schedule changed together, so we withdraw the "about 55% of the drop" estimate and the implied α ≈ 0.27. The same-schedule comparison stands: under WSD at N = 200M, documents in the first 50M tokens give +0.076 and documents in the last 50M give +0.198. The missing arms, documents spread through the run under WSD at N = 200M and 800M, would separate placement from schedule.

comments.author: cweill
comments.body:
🤖 **Update: placement at a fixed schedule, and how the directional part scales.** Four more runs: documents spread through the run under WSD at N = 200M and 800M, which closes the gap named in the correction above, and misaligned documents at N = 50M and 800M.

_Figure (placement at a fixed schedule; directional part across N) to be attached._

**Placement, same schedule.** All runs use WSD (constant LR, then linear decay over the final ~50M tokens); k = 4k aligned documents; effect is measured against the WSD k=0 control at the same N.

| N | spread through the run | inside the final 50M | final ÷ spread |
|---|---|---|---|
| 200M | +0.177 | +0.198 | 1.12 |
| 800M | +0.124 | +0.178 | 1.44 |
| drop, 200M → 800M | 0.053 | 0.020 | |

The schedule does not cause the N-dependence: spread-out documents lose 0.053 under WSD, against 0.045 under cosine. At a fixed schedule, putting the documents in the final decay cuts the loss from 0.053 to 0.020, so recency accounts for about 60% of the N-dependence of the total effect. The advantage of late placement grows with N, as recency predicts. Documents in the first 50M tokens of a 200M run give +0.076.

**Directional part across N.** Cosine schedule, documents spread through the run, k = 4k; effect is measured against the cosine k=0 control at the same N.

| N | aligned | misaligned | directional (aligned − misaligned) | directional share |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50M | +0.193 | +0.102 | +0.092 | 47% |
| 200M | +0.162 | +0.090 | +0.072 | 45% |
| 800M | +0.117 | +0.070 | +0.047 | 40% |

From N = 50M to 800M the directional part falls to 0.51 of its value, the shared part to 0.68, and the total to 0.60. With documents spread through training, the directional part dilutes faster than the total effect suggests.

**Confidence.** Seed 0 for every cell; seed-to-seed SD at two cells is 0.001, and the paired question SE per effect is about 0.007. Placement and the directional part are each measured at one dose (k = 4k), so we report ratios across N, not fitted exponents. Untested: the directional part under late placement, and both at other model sizes.

**Implication, at this scale.** For a fixed amount of alignment data, placing it in the final learning-rate decay keeps most of the effect as training gets longer. Spreading it through training loses more, and the directional part loses the most. If this holds at larger scale, the length that matters for a Marin run is the anneal window, not total pretraining tokens, and a document budget should be judged by the aligned-minus-misaligned difference, not the raw margin alone.

spillover_issues.author: penfever
spillover_issues.body:
`marina apps table load` stages rows as 250-row INSERT batches through the applet SQL gateway (`infra/marina/src/marina/table_load.py`, `INSERT_BATCH_ROWS = 250`). There is no server-side bulk path (COPY, staged parquet ingestion, or a released-job runner) for large app datasets.

Impact: any app load beyond a small dataset drives thousands of gateway statements. During the RL Data Atlas preview reload (a 320-source serving catalog, ~51,000 item rows and the retained-assessment carry-forward), the sustained statement stream crashed the shared Cloud Run gateway with 503s ("The service you requested is not available at this time", service error -27) while production shared the same deployment. The gateway's 10-second per-statement guard (`QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS = 10000` in `infra/marina/src/marina/applets.py`) also rejects legitimate statements: per-pipeline retained-copy INSERT..SELECTs over ~150,000 indexed rows, and batched item inserts spiking past 10 seconds under contention on a table carrying ~2.4 million retained rows plus four indexes including a GIN index.

Observed events (2026-11-18): repeated 504 statement timeouts during the staged load; one 503 gateway crash mid-load; the load aborted without selecting. The Atlas loader already bounds everything it can locally (per-table byte budgets, row-count caps, per-pipeline and per-bucket carry-forward copies, a deduplicated probe through materialized summaries) — the remaining constraint is the transport, not the statements.

Options:
1. The apps tooling gains a server-side bulk path: stage rows to object storage, one server-side COPY per table through the app's database role (the released-job runner or an ops-authorized maintenance connection).
2. The released-job runner (`marina.jobs.job_engine()`) runs load jobs inside the Marina runtime with direct database access — currently blocked on runner capacity in the infrastructure-owned runtime configuration.

Until one lands, large app loads can only use paced, resumable gateway drivers with retry-on-flap, which is fragile at this volume.

# Research

`apps table load` reads the full Arrow table, then sends one SQL request per 250-row batch. Atlas uses a separate loader but sends its batches through the same gateway. Each request gets a 10-second statement timeout; changing only `table_load.py` would leave the Atlas reload exposed. Released jobs already have an app-role database engine, but `runtime.toml` grants runner capacity only to Echo and EvalDash.

**Relevant code**
- [`table_load.py#L60-L88`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ea1257ca8d7a968397f2493b968035c8eb1caa46/infra/marina/src/marina/table_load.py#L60-L88) — 250-row INSERT generation.

- [`applets.py#L1089-L1122`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ea1257ca8d7a968397f2493b968035c8eb1caa46/infra/marina/src/marina/applets.py#L1089-L1122) — app role and 10-second guard.
- [`rl_data_catalog/load.py#L57-L95`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ea1257ca8d7a968397f2493b968035c8eb1caa46/infra/marina/apps/rl_data_catalog/load.py#L57-L95) — Atlas gateway batches.
- [`jobs.py#L23-L51`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ea1257ca8d7a968397f2493b968035c8eb1caa46/infra/marina/src/marina/jobs.py#L23-L51) — direct app-role engine and runner limits.

# Proposed Fix

This needs a runtime and app-loader change, followed by a general table-loader change:

1. Add an on-demand bulk runner in `runtime.toml` and Pulumi, with explicit per-app permission, resource and time limits, and no scheduler trigger. Run released app modules through `job_engine()` so writes use the selected app's role. Keep the 10-second SQL gateway guard for interactive requests.
2. Move the Atlas import into a released job. Pin the source snapshot, stream row data to Postgres through the worker (probe the current driver for `COPY FROM STDIN`), run retained-copy SQL through the same direct connection, check counts, and switch `atlas_current` only after validation. A failed run must leave the previous snapshot selected and be safe to retry.
3. Add a bulk mode to `apps table load`: upload the input to an app-scoped regional object prefix, submit a bounded worker run using server-resolved app role and validated table name, stream into a staging table, then commit an append or atomic replacement. Track the staged object's digest and run status so a retry cannot duplicate rows; delete abandoned staging objects.

Done when an Atlas preview reload of the reported ~51,000 items against the indexed retained table completes without bulk SQL gateway traffic, the previous snapshot survives an injected load failure, and real-Postgres tests cover app-role isolation plus append, replace, and retry behavior. Record gateway request count, load duration, and row counts before enabling the path for production.

spillover_issues.author: penfever
spillover_issues.body:
`grade_math_candidate` converts math_verify's `TimeoutException` into `GradingInfraError("math verifier deadline exhausted")`. For some tasks the timeout is deterministic: every attempt of the same task parses a candidate/reference combination that exceeds the deadline, so the task records only infrastructure attempts and the source stays permanently pending — retries cannot change the outcome.

Observed in small-v16 (`2026.11.14.43/small-v16`, exited successfully), source `pafitis:hardmath` (13 of its 100 selected tasks are pending):
- 78 infrastructure attempts across 13 tasks; the sampled receipts show 11 distinct tasks whose every attempt ended with `GradeResult(status=Outcome.INFRA_ERROR, error='math verifier deadline exhausted')`, e.g. `hardmath-1e2483b884b23134518281560e7093cdb0689ff00aaf5ef6de464e5ff9aef213`, `hardmath-0a3338878b6532ef6fae4cbde3092f9653bf84206b34288958ef7c77044040bf`, `hardmath-986bc6ec98013391ee11cc99227c50a728625b18521826dbbd5cc41a845d73c8`.
- Every attempt consumed a full solver trial (model inference + judge) before the deadline failure.

Reproduce:
1. Grade a `pafitis:hardmath` candidate listed above against its TaskSpec reference with the protocol's math-verify profile and deadline.
2. `math_verify` raises `TimeoutException` inside its parse/verify; the grader maps it to `GradingInfraError`; the trial records `INFRA_ERROR` with no reward.
3. Repeating the attempt reproduces the same timeout.

Expected: a deterministic per-task deadline failure should be distinguishable from transient infrastructure load — e.g. a larger or shape-specific parse deadline, a cheaper pre-check for pathological candidate/reference pairs, or a typed condition that stops retrying and reports the task as ungradeable instead of consuming the full attempt budget.

Grader code: `lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_math.py:316-318` (`except TimeoutException ... raise GradingInfraError("math verifier deadline exhausted")`), deadline via `math_verify.utils.timeout` at `lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_math.py:325`.

Evidence receipts (S3, no PII): `s3://marin-rno2a/marin/rl-data/atlas/difficulty/2026.11.14.43/small-v16/trials/<sha256("pafitis:hardmath")>/attempts/<task_key>/*/attempt.json`.

comments.body:
🤖

# Research

Verifyit maps every math-verify deadline during reference parsing, candidate parsing, or comparison to the same infrastructure error. In draft PR #11277, Atlas runs another full trial after an unscored attempt and resumes every task without a scored result, so repeated verifier deadlines consume solver work and leave the source pending. The receipts establish repeated failures, but do not yet show which grading phase timed out or whether the candidate text was the same across attempts.

**Relevant code**

- [`grade_math.py#L309-L318`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/0169e8a4feccf4db58a3b3fac50c5f24c78be473/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_math.py#L309-L318) — collapses deadline phases
- [`grade_math.py#L48-L54`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/0169e8a4feccf4db58a3b3fac50c5f24c78be473/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_math.py#L48-L54) — five-second main-thread deadline
- [`difficulty_trials.py#L370-L387`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7c86252b6c790c1d9feb1fc02ceb025359fe8303/experiments/post_training/task_curation/difficulty_trials.py#L370-L387) — retries unscored trials
- [`difficulty_trials.py#L494-L508`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7c86252b6c790c1d9feb1fc02ceb025359fe8303/experiments/post_training/task_curation/difficulty_trials.py#L494-L508) — resumes unscored tasks
- [`difficulty.py#L275-L315`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7c86252b6c790c1d9feb1fc02ceb025359fe8303/lib/finestore/src/finestore/rl/difficulty.py#L275-L315) — excludes failures from scored coverage

# Proposed Fix

1. Replay several affected TaskSpecs and archived candidate outputs in the pinned grader environment. Record the reference, candidate, profile, and input hashes, and identify whether each timeout occurs in reference parsing, candidate parsing, or comparison. Test the same input again under the same deadline before treating it as deterministic.
2. Carry a typed timeout phase through Verifyit's infrastructure verdict. Run a bounded reference preflight before solver inference in the grader's main process or an isolated child process; the current signal deadline is disabled in worker threads. A confirmed fixed-reference timeout becomes a terminal, unscored task condition. Candidate-dependent timeouts remain infrastructure failures while retryable; after a cumulative retry cap, record a terminal `grader_blocked` reason without assigning a zero reward.
3. Extend Atlas's attempt receipts and recovery filter with a terminal blocked status and reason. Add `blocked_tasks` to measurement accounting, so `scored + retryable pending + blocked` equals the selected population; use a distinct blocked source status when no retryable tasks remain. Historical infrastructure receipts remain unclassified. Blocked tasks never enter `n` or `solved`. Coordinate the Atlas portion with draft PR #11277, which owns these paths.

Test the fixed-reference path before any solver call, candidate/compare timeout classification, recovery across campaign versions, and unchanged scoring for gradeable tasks. Replaying the sampled HARDMath tasks should show no repeated full trials after a terminal diagnosis and no invented solver scores. A longer verifier deadline should be evaluated from the replay timings before changing the global five-second limit.

comments.author: XiaoyuanWang111
comments.body:
🤖 I replayed the `math` mode on the pinned HARDMath mirror to see which step runs out and whether it depends on the reply. The comparison runs out, and only for some replies: the conversion check and a reply equal to the reference finish on every row, while a reply that is another equation often reaches the deadline.

The data is `pafitis/HARDMath_processed_training` at 937e9f10, all 702 rows. Each contract is built from `ground_truths` as `math_answer_task` builds it and graded through `verifyit.grade.run` on main, one process per call. 684 rows convert; the other 18 have the unparseable reference of #11510. The replies are constructed. I have no access to the stored attempts, so I cannot say which replies the 13 pending tasks received.

| reply | scored 1 | scored 0 | deadline |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| no answer file (the conversion check) | 0 | 684 | 0 |
| `\boxed{reference}` | 684 | 0 | 0 |
| `\boxed{42}` | 0 | 684 | 0 |
| `\boxed{reference of the next row of the same question type}` | 0 | 491 | 193 |
| `\boxed{reference with its first number raised by 1}` | 0 | 532 | 152 |

- **Which rows.** The 193 are 102 of the 125 ODE rows and 91 of the 101 symbolic nondimensionalization rows. Their references are equations, `[y = …, y = …]` and `\epsilon=…`. The other three question types (458 rows) never reach the deadline.
- **Which step.** In all 193 calls, parsing the reference and parsing the reply return within 0.5 s. The time goes into math-verify's comparison of the two equations (`sympy_compare_relational`): its symbolic equality check, then solving both equations with SymPy (`sympy_solve_and_compare`). With the deadline set to 20 s, 41 of the 193 comparisons finish, in 5.1 to 19.6 s, and 152 do not.
- **Which replies.** For symbolic nondimensionalization, the reference with one exponent changed reaches the deadline on 81 of 89 rows. The reference regrouped as `\epsilon=\frac{a_{1} a_{3}^{p/q}}{a_{2}^{p/q} a_{3}}` (`p/q` is its exponent), which is equal for positive coefficients, reaches it on 74 of 89 and scores 0 on the other 15. The right-hand side alone, without `\epsilon=`, scores 1.0 on all 101.

For the retry limit of #11518 this means the verdict follows the reply. A task is blocked once three consecutive attempts reach the deadline, which here means three replies that are another equation, wrong or regrouped; a reply in the reference's own form scores 1.0 in under a second. The blocked tasks leave `n`, and the tasks the solver got right stay.

One case, row 9 of the train split, with row 20's answer (the same expression with exponent 17/6) as the wrong reply:

```python
from verifyit.grade import GradingInfraError
from verifyit.modes.grade_math import grade_math_candidate
from verifyit.spec import MathSpec, MathType

reference = r"\epsilon=\frac{a_{1} \left(\frac{a_{3}}{a_{2}}\right)^{\frac{19}{9}}}{a_{3}}"
spec = MathSpec(expected=reference, math_type=MathType.EQUATION)
for reply in (reference, "42", reference.replace("19}{9", "17}{6")):
    try:
        print(grade_math_candidate(spec, reply).reward, reply)
    except GradingInfraError as error:
        print(error, reply)
```

It prints `1.0`, `0.0` and `math verifier deadline exhausted`.

On the conversion side, `convert_hardmath` passes `ground_truths` whole, so the reference keeps its left-hand side. The two older HARDMath loaders (`_prepare_hardmath`, `_hardmath_records`) keep only the right-hand side and reject answers that contain `[`. With those two rules 383 rows remain, and with the next row's answer as the reply none of them reaches the deadline; the slowest call takes 0.49 s.
