- **Phase tags.** With the `convert_hardmath` contracts 562 calls reach the deadline over all the replies I graded, and all of them report `phase: comparison`. None is a reference parse, so none of them counts toward the block.
- **`convert_hardmath_rhs`.** None of its 7,319 calls reaches the deadline, and the slowest takes 2.75 s. The wrong replies score 0: the two in the table, the last number raised by 1, a changed exponent, the first member alone, and exchanged members. The exceptions have the reference's value: 34 integral rows whose two members are the same text, and 3 integral rows whose reference has the coefficient `0.00`.
- **`polynomial_roots`, 65 rows.** The dataset writes these answers as `\left[…\right], \left[…\right]`. `convert_hardmath` grades that text as one SCALAR. `convert_hardmath_rhs` puts it inside `[` and `]` and grades a LIST of two members. A reply in the dataset's form then scores 0 on all 65 rows: `_split_members` removes the reply's first `[` and last `]` as if they enclosed the whole text, and the reply splits into three members. The golden control carries the outer brackets and scores 1, so admission does not show this. On main the same split scores `(1,2),(3,4)` 0 against the LIST reference `[(1,2),(3,4)]`.
- **Regrouped answers.** For symbolic nondimensionalization, the regrouping `\frac{a_{1} a_{3}^{p/q}}{a_{2}^{p/q} a_{3}}` of my earlier comment scores 0 on 89 of 89 rows with `convert_hardmath_rhs`. With `convert_hardmath` it reaches the deadline on 74 and scores 0 on 15.

Row 122 of the train split, with its own answer text as the reply:

```python
from verifyit.modes.grade_math import grade_math_candidate
from verifyit.spec import MathSpec, MathType

answer = r"\left[ - \sqrt{\frac{1.00}{\epsilon}}, \  \sqrt{\frac{1.00}{\epsilon}}\right], \left[ \frac{1.00}{\epsilon}, \  -1.00\right]"
print(grade_math_candidate(MathSpec(expected=answer, math_type=MathType.SCALAR), answer).reward)
print(grade_math_candidate(MathSpec(expected=f"[{answer}]", math_type=MathType.LIST), answer).reward)
print(grade_math_candidate(MathSpec(expected=f"[{answer}]", math_type=MathType.LIST), f"[{answer}]").reward)
```

It prints `1.0`, `0.0` and `1.0`. The first contract is the one `convert_hardmath` builds for this row and the other two use the one `convert_hardmath_rhs` builds.

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
🤖 The `_split_members` false negative is fixed on main and on `atlas-env-audit`, and the HARDMath RHS release re-grades clean.

**The fix.** `_split_members` dropped a sequence's first and last characters whenever they read as an opener/closer pair by type, so a reply whose members carry their own brackets lost one bracket per side and split into broken members. It now strips the outer layer only when the first opener's balanced close is the last character, and otherwise splits the top level as is. PR on main: #11739 (row-122 and `(1,2),(3,4)`-vs-`[(1,2),(3,4)]` regression tests included, both verified failing before the fix; full verifyit suite green). Landed on `atlas-env-audit` via atlas-push at 91ebdc65fe (1,536 verifyit tests green on the rebased head).

**Re-grade of the HARDMath RHS release** (684 converted rows of `pafitis/HARDMath_processed_training@937e9f10` under the `convert_hardmath_rhs` contracts at the landed head; every call through `verifyit.grade.run` in its own process; cells are rows scored 1 / scored 0 / at the deadline):

| reply | scored 1 | scored 0 | deadline |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| the contract's own reference | 684 | 0 | 0 |
| the dataset's answer text | 684 | 0 | 0 |
| the answer of the next converted row | 0 | 684 | 0 |
| the contract reference with its first number raised by 1 | 0 | 684 | 0 |

The dataset's answer text was 619/65/0 under the bug; the 65 `polynomial_roots` false negatives are gone and the wrong replies still score 0. None of the 2,736 calls reaches the deadline and the slowest takes 1.27 s; all 65 `polynomial_roots` rows score 1 on the dataset's own form.

**Receipt impact.** No receipt of the RHS release computed a reward under the bug: conversion receipts validate references only (the reference `[\left[…\right], \left[…\right]]` split correctly even under the bug — that is why admission missed this), the retained census is a static conversion census, the lexical scan is text-only, and the retained-release receipt, fingerprint index and license receipt bind identity, not grades. No difficulty-campaign trial tree exists anywhere under `s3://marin-rno2a/marin/rl-data/atlas/difficulty` for the rhs source hash `83371b10…`, and no SAMPLE QC ran for the variant, so no difficulty measurement or admission receipt needs re-measuring. The only record the bug corrupted is the replay table in the comment above (619/65/0), which this table supersedes. Nothing deleted, nothing re-registered.

**The 89 symbolic-nondimensionalization regroupings** score 0 because math-verify's equivalence check is conservative, not because of a contract bug. The regrouping `\frac{a_{1} \left(\frac{a_{3}}{a_{2}}\right)^{p/q}}{a_{3}}` → `\frac{a_{1} a_{3}^{p/q}}{a_{2}^{p/q} a_{3}}` parses on both sides; SymPy cannot prove the identity without positivity assumptions (`simplify` leaves a nonzero difference), and proves it exactly with `positive=True` symbols. The dataset's coefficients are positive, so the regrouped reply is semantically right and loses the point — a false negative of the verifier's exactness, never a false positive. Examples (row → reference → regrouped reply, all scoring 0):

- row 9: `\frac{a_{1} \left(\frac{a_{3}}{a_{2}}\right)^{\frac{19}{9}}}{a_{3}}` → `\frac{a_{1} a_{3}^{\frac{19}{9}}}{a_{2}^{\frac{19}{9}} a_{3}}`
- row 20: `\frac{a_{1} \left(\frac{a_{3}}{a_{2}}\right)^{\frac{17}{6}}}{a_{3}}` → `\frac{a_{1} a_{3}^{\frac{17}{6}}}{a_{2}^{\frac{17}{6}} a_{3}}`
- row 29: `\frac{a_{1} \left(\frac{a_{3}}{a_{2}}\right)^{\frac{5}{4}}}{a_{3}}` → `\frac{a_{1} a_{3}^{\frac{5}{4}}}{a_{2}^{\frac{5}{4}} a_{3}}`

Scripts and per-call ledgers: `experiments/active/difficulty-11511-followup/{regrade-rhs-release.py,nondim-regrouping-analysis.py}` with their JSON outputs.

spillover_issues.title: [verifyit] math_verify deadline exhausts deterministically on some tasks

spillover_issues.author: penfever
spillover_issues.body:
A symbolic math reply that is equal to the reference only under positivity assumptions scores 0, because math-verify's comparison cannot prove the identity for unassumed symbols. The grader never awards a false positive here — the failure mode is a conservative false negative on an equivalent answer. On the HARDMath mirror (`pafitis/HARDMath_processed_training@937e9f10`), 89 of 89 symbolic-nondimensionalization rows whose reference carries a power of a ratio score 0 when the reply regroups the same expression into a ratio of powers (89 of the 101 `nondimensionalization_symbolic` rows have that form; measured through `verifyit.grade.run` under the `convert_hardmath_rhs` contracts, replay in [#11511 (comment)](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11511#issuecomment-7006269885)). This is independent of the member-splitting bug fixed in #11739.

Reproduce:
1. Grade a regrouped reply against its reference with the symbolic math grader:

    ```python
    from verifyit.modes.grade_math import grade_math_candidate
    from verifyit.spec import MathSpec, MathType

    # HARDMath_processed_training@937e9f10, question_type nondimensionalization_symbolic
    cases = [
        (r"\frac{a_{1} \left(\frac{a_{3}}{a_{2}}\right)^{\frac{19}{9}}}{a_{3}}",
         r"\frac{a_{1} a_{3}^{\frac{19}{9}}}{a_{2}^{\frac{19}{9}} a_{3}}"),  # row 9
        (r"\frac{a_{1} \left(\frac{a_{3}}{a_{2}}\right)^{\frac{17}{6}}}{a_{3}}",
         r"\frac{a_{1} a_{3}^{\frac{17}{6}}}{a_{2}^{\frac{17}{6}} a_{3}}"),  # row 20
        (r"\frac{a_{1} \left(\frac{a_{3}}{a_{2}}\right)^{\frac{5}{4}}}{a_{3}}",
         r"\frac{a_{1} a_{3}^{\frac{5}{4}}}{a_{2}^{\frac{5}{4}} a_{3}}"),    # row 29
    ]
    for reference, reply in cases:
        spec = MathSpec(expected=reference, math_type=MathType.SCALAR)
        print(grade_math_candidate(spec, reply).reward)  # 0.0, 0.0, 0.0
    ```

2. Each row prints 0.0; the reference itself, the reply form with the outer ratio kept, and wrong replies grade normally, so the 0 comes from the comparison of two parsed expressions, not from a parse failure.

Expected: the regrouped reply grades 1.0. It equals the reference wherever the coefficients are positive, and these datasets' coefficients are positive constants (for example `1.00`); a silent 0 for a semantically correct answer shape undercounts measured solve rates for any source whose answers contain powers of ratios.

Confirmed root cause of the 0: both sides parse to expressions, and the equality needs positivity. Row 9 parses to `a_1*(a_3/a_2)**(19/9)/a_3` (reference) and `a_1*a_3**(19/9)/(a_2**(19/9)*a_3)` (reply); `sympy.simplify(gold - target)` without assumptions leaves a nonzero difference, and the same simplify with the symbols declared `positive=True` returns exactly 0.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

The reported regrouping parses on both sides, but `math_verify.verify` compares symbols without the positivity needed to prove the identity. VerifyIt has no domain assumptions in `MathSpec`; the shared task converter constructs that spec without source-specific symbol metadata. A global positive-symbol rule would change scores for tasks with unrestricted variables (for example, `\sqrt{x^2}` versus `x` at negative `x`).

**Relevant code**
- [`grade_math.py#L106-L155`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1a8a628d2613b3b730f84ea317c99e8c5f2c94a8/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_math.py#L106-L155) — symbolic comparison
- [`grade_math.py#L367-L405`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1a8a628d2613b3b730f84ea317c99e8c5f2c94a8/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_math.py#L367-L405) — candidate scoring
- [`spec.py#L143-L149`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1a8a628d2613b3b730f84ea317c99e8c5f2c94a8/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/spec.py#L143-L149) — math contract fields
- [`answers.py#L108-L123`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1a8a628d2613b3b730f84ea317c99e8c5f2c94a8/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/convert/answers.py#L108-L123) — shared spec construction
- [`math.py#L209-L215`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1a8a628d2613b3b730f84ea317c99e8c5f2c94a8/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/skyrl/math.py#L209-L215) — HARDMath conversion on main

# Proposed Fix

1. Audit the 89 affected `nondimensionalization_symbolic` questions in `pafitis/HARDMath_processed_training@937e9f10` for an explicit positive domain for each symbolic coefficient. The presence of positive numeric constants alone does not establish the domain of every symbol. Record any exceptions and leave those contracts unchanged.
2. Add an opt-in tuple of positive symbol names to `MathSpec`, defaulting to empty. After ordinary scalar comparison fails, substitute positive SymPy symbols on both parsed expressions and retry an exact, deadline-bounded comparison. Keep equations, sets, and the default grading policy unchanged; validate names and reject malformed contracts.
3. Pass the assumption only from a HARDMath conversion whose audited question establishes it. Coordinate this with the RHS-only HARDMath contract on the `atlas-env-audit` integration branch; main currently converts the whole `ground_truths` field.
4. Add public-API regressions for the three reported regroupings, a wrong exponent, and `\sqrt{x^2}` versus `x` with and without an explicit positive `x`. Replay all 89 affected rows and wrong-answer controls through `verifyit.grade.run`; accept the change only if the supported regroupings score 1, wrong replies remain 0, and no calls reach the deadline. The implementation PR should use `Fixes #11740`.

This spans the grader contract, shared conversion, and an audited dataset release, so it needs a scoped implementation rather than a global comparator change.
